entries.definition: Power mean (p = 4) of every 20-80 tool grade a prospect carries plus the FanGraphs physical grades, on the 20-80 scale. The exponent weights extreme tools: one elite grade lifts the composite more than balanced average grades do.
entries.methodology: Hitters: equal-weight power mean (p = 4) of hit, pwr, run, field, arm, pitch_sel and bat_ctrl plus the FanGraphs -2..+2 physical grades (Frame, Athleticism) mapped to the FV scale (-2→30, -1→40, 0→50, +1→60, +2→70). Pitchers: the physicals (Frame, Athleticism, Delivery) join fb/sl/cb/ch in a p = 3 stuff power mean, then overall = 0.65·stuff + 0.35·cmd. Output is the raw power mean on the 20-80 scale (50 average, 60 plus, 70 elite), with no z-scoring. A 70 PWR / 45 HIT prospect (arithmetic mean 57.5) reads ~58 at p = 4 against ~57.6 at p = 3.
entries.formula:
Tool = (Σ tool_grade^4 / n)^(1/4)
hitter inputs: hit, pwr, run, field, arm, pitch_sel, bat_ctrl, frame_fv, athl_fv
pitcher: Tool = 0.65 · power-mean(fb, sl, cb, ch, frame_fv, athl_fv, delivery_fv; p=3) + 0.35 · cmd
entries.example: A 70 PWR / 45 HIT prospect with 50s elsewhere posts a Tool near 58, above the 57.5 arithmetic mean, because the p = 4 mean weights the 70.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Weighted offensive composite on the 20-80 scale: HIT 40 / PWR 40 / BCTRL 10 / PSEL 6 / RUN 4.
entries.methodology: Weighted mean of the hitter's offensive 20-80 grades, output on the 20-80 scale (50 average, 60 plus, 70 elite). HIT and PWR carry 40% each; bat control and pitch selection fill out the profile; speed is a small term. Field and arm live in D-Tool.
entries.formula:
O-Tool = Σ w_i · grade_i / Σ w_i
weights: HIT 0.40, PWR 0.40, BCTRL 0.10, PSEL 0.06, RUN 0.04
entries.example: A 60 HIT / 60 PWR hitter with 50s elsewhere posts an O-Tool of 58.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Weighted defensive composite (p = 3 power mean) on the 20-80 scale: DEF 60 / ARM 30 / RUN 10; catchers DEF 70 / ARM 30.
entries.methodology: Weighted power mean (p = 3) of the position player's defensive 20-80 grades, output on the 20-80 scale (50 average, 60 plus, 70 elite). Field carries 60%, arm 30% and run 10% (speed already feeds range through the field grade, so it is a small term). Catchers drop run and move field to 70%, because the catcher field grade absorbs framing, blocking and receiving. The p = 3 mean rewards an elite glove more than a plain weighted mean would.
entries.formula:
D-Tool = (Σ w_i · grade_i^3 / Σ w_i)^(1/3)
non-catcher weights: DEF 0.60, ARM 0.30, RUN 0.10
catcher weights:    DEF 0.70, ARM 0.30 (RUN dropped)
entries.example: A 70 DEF / 50 ARM / 50 RUN center fielder posts a D-Tool near 62; a 50/50/50 baseline lands at 50.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Active-prospect flag: grade or tool velocity AND a performance gate, under an age cap. Tuned to flag about 10-40 prospects league-wide.
entries.formula:
breakout = (fv_upgrade ≥ +5 OR tool_velocity ≥ +3)
         AND perf_gate_pass
         AND (age ≤ 24 starters/hitters, age ≤ 25 relievers)
entries.visual: 50★→ aquamarine ★ + pulsing bottom edge
entries.example: A 20-year-old A+ hitter whose consensus rose +5 FV in four months while running RPS+ 118 flags ★. A 26-year-old AAA arm with the same jump does not (age cap), and neither does a riser at RPS+ 96 (no performance gate).
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Soft-pink ^ in the top-right corner of an FV badge: at least one source published a '+' upside grade on the latest snapshot.
entries.methodology: When an outlet publishes a grade such as 45+ or 40+, the player carries the Upside mark. Capped at FV ≤ 50: at 50+ and above the grade already prices the upside. The badge gets the ^ glyph and a pink top edge; the tooltip lists the sources. On Spotlights it shows as a pink driver chip when a source added a '+' in the trailing 6 months. The glyph is ^ so it does not collide with the health '+' pill.
entries.visual: 45^→ soft-pink ^ + pink top edge
entries.example: A source publishing 45+ on a 19-year-old shortstop puts the ^ on his FV badge. A 55+ from the same outlet shows no mark (above the FV 50 cap).
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: CollegeSavant's tracked-skill index: 100 = the season's college pool average, +10 = one standard deviation better. College-relative, not a Single-A projection.
entries.methodology:
Pool-anchored z-average of TrackMan tracked skills on the 100 + 10z scale (same as SC+), against the per-year college cohort the percentile sliders use.

Hitters: two equal families, contact quality (90th-percentile exit velocity, barrel%, hard-hit%) and plate discipline (zone-contact%, -whiff%, -chase%). Pitchers: stuff and whiffs (Stuff+, swinging-strike%, induced chase%) and contact suppression (-barrel%, -hard-hit%, -xwOBA against). Missing components drop out.

Each component is z-scored against its cohort, signed so higher is better, averaged within its family, and the two families are averaged. Rescaled 100 + 10z, unclamped.

Observation only (no scouting prior). CollegeSavant Stuff+ does not predict pro outcomes in the matched data.
entries.formula: CS+ = 100 + 10 × avg(family means of z-scored tracked components vs the per-year college cohort)
entries.example: A hitter at +1.2σ 90th-percentile EV, +1σ barrel% and +0.8σ hard-hit% with average discipline lands near CS+ 115.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: What a college line projects to against Single-A pitching: an expected value plus a P10-P90 band. A matched-pair projection.
entries.methodology: Each CollegeSavant player is joined by name to draft_players and to his later Single-A (A / A+) statline in prospects.db. Per stat, a regression to the mean is fit over the matched pairs (predicted = Single-A mean + shrunk slope x (college value - college mean)), so a weak relationship pulls hard toward the level mean. K% and BB% exist on both sides and are the matched-pair translation; hitter OPS (from college xwOBA) ships EXPERIMENTAL because college tracked data barely forecasts Single-A production. The band is the P10-P90 residual range and widens with thin support; leave-one-out coverage runs near the 80% target. No strength-of-schedule or park adjustment. Which leg to trust is read off the backtest, not fixed: a leg whose r2 is below 0.10 is flagged low signal on every surface, and the leg that clears it differs by side. 2026-09-24 reading: hitter K% r2 0.17 (leave-one-out MAE 5.34 against 5.91 for predicting the Single-A mean) clears it, while hitter BB% (r2 0.02) and OPS (r2 0.01) do not; pitcher BB% r2 0.11 (3.14 against 3.38) clears it, while pitcher K% r2 0.03 (4.01 against 4.00) shows no measurable edge over the mean and is flagged. Stuff+ does not predict Single-A outcomes in the matched data, so the pitcher translation is K% / BB% only.
entries.formula: proj_single_a = single_a_mean + shrunk_slope x (college_value - college_mean); band = P10-P90 of the fit residuals
entries.example: A college hitter at a 12% strikeout rate projects to about 23.7% at Single-A, with an 80% band near 15-32%.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Pool-anchored composite of tracked Statcast and zone signals. 100 = pool mean; 10 points = one standard deviation. Board filter chips: 105+ above pool, 95 and under below pool, 120+ elite.
entries.methodology:
Hitters: contact quality (average exit velocity, hard-hit%, barrel%) + zone discipline (z-contact%, -whiff%, -chase%). Pitchers: top-pitch average velocity + induced whiffs + induced chase + inverted hard-hit and barrel allowed.

Each component is z-scored against the side-matched active pool, averaged, and rescaled 100 + 10z (the scale shared with CS+, DvM+, KRP+ and pStuff+). It is a z-score index, not the ratio family (wRC+, OPS+) where a point is about one percent. The Python (statcast_plus.py) and the JS fallback (getStatcastPlus) both use 10.

Two cut sets on one scale: the Python tiers are 110 / 90 (±1σ, used by downstream gates); the board chips are 105 / 95 / 120.

Used by: the SC+ filter chip, the SC+ driver chip on Spotlights, the tiebreak inside fvCmpDesc for same-FV prospects, faller and rebounder confirmation in Spotlights scoring, and the per-side farm aggregates. Blank with no tracked data.
entries.formula: SC+ = 100 + 10 x avg(z-scored components vs side-matched pool)
entries.example: A hitter at EV 92 (+1σ), HH% 45 (+1σ) and Z-Con% 88 (+0.5σ) averages +0.83σ: SC+ 108.
entries.visual: SC+ 122SC+ 101SC+ 84
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Separates prospects with the same FV by projected MLB success. Cohort-aware (MiLB / Draft / Overseas) and injury-aware. A 0-100 talent base, then health and upside multipliers; published range 0-130.
entries.methodology:
Blends scouting grades, cohort-normalized performance and development signal into a renormalized 0-100 base, then multiplies by health and upside. Tuned per cohort for the chance of becoming a useful MLB regular, not current-season output.

Base weights. MiLB (active): Tool composite 0.24, RPS+ 0.22, SC+ 0.20, per-tool max 0.10, pStuff+ 0.08 (pitchers), age-vs-level 0.10, stock movement 0.06. Draft: DS+ 0.27, RPS+ (college) 0.21, Tool+ 0.18, Tool composite 0.10, per-tool max 0.10, age 0.10, movement 0.04. Overseas: Tool+ 0.22, cohort RPS+ 0.20, translation-adjusted wRC+ 0.20, FIP 0.18 (one of the two performance legs per player), Tool composite 0.08, per-tool max 0.08, age 0.04, movement 0.04.

Known gap: the active MiLB RPS+ term reads a statline field the active payload does not carry (the board's RPS+ pill is computed in the browser), so that 0.22 weight is inert on the active cohort and the rest renormalize. The draft and overseas RPS+ terms fire.

Where eFV exists (active MiLB), the eFV-implied 6-year WAR enters at 0.90 and dominates; it falls back to the eFV grade decimal and drops out on draft and overseas, where eFV abstains. Each signal is normalized to 0-1 and clipped; missing signals drop and the rest renormalize.

Multipliers: on the IL x0.70, post-Tommy-John window x0.85, severe or long IL history x0.86, moderate IL history x0.94, upside '+' flag x1.06, breakout flag x1.12. Rounded and clamped to 0-130. Used for same-FV order on the Draft and Overseas lists, the surplus nudge in trade evaluations and the 'TBS NN' line on Trade Audit cards. The Active list's overall rank breaks ties server-side on FV, then tools, then currently-on-IL.
entries.formula: TBS = round( clamp( 100 x sum(signal_i x weight_i) / sum(weight_i present) x health_multiplier x upside_multiplier, 0, 130 ) ), per-cohort weights as listed above.
entries.example: Two 50-FV shortstops with similar tools, one healthy (RPS+ 118), one on the 60-day IL: the healthy bat scores ~8-10 TBS higher and ranks ahead.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Level-relative rate index family (100 = average). Three displays share the RPS name and not a scale: the active board's RPS+ is a browser-computed RATIO (a point is about one percent of the cohort mean); RPS-Draft+ (rps_draft_plus) and RPS-Intl+ (rps_intl_plus) are Z-SCORE indexes where 15 points is one standard deviation.
entries.methodology:
Three surfaces, three keys since the 2026-08-19 rename.

1. ACTIVE MiLB board, RPS+. Computed in the browser (prospx _buildRpsPlusCache); active payloads carry no rps field. Raw score = level-relative performance plus an age term: hitters use wRC+ vs level minus 100, pitchers use 100 minus ERA- vs level, and both add -10 x the age-vs-level gap in years. Cohorts are integer age x position group, falling back to age only under 30 prospects. Index = 100 x (raw + 100) / (cohort_mean + 100), times a position multiplier applied after normalization (C 1.08, MI 1.05, CF 1.04, INF 1.02, CI 1.00, P 1.00, OF 0.99, COF 0.97, DH 0.92; pitchers stay 1.00 because ERA- is already position-neutral), rounded, clamped 0-250. Gate: 15 games (hitters) or 15 innings (pitchers) and a known age. MLB players show wRC+ or xFIP with FIP- instead. The active TBS composite once carried a statline rps term (weight 0.22) that was never populated; the 2026-08-19 fix removed it, a no-op on served TBS.

2. DRAFT, RPS-Draft+ (rps_draft_plus, draft_export.py) = 100 + 15 x z of the college-performance score against the draft class, clamped 60-140. No age or position cohort, no position multiplier. Draftees with college stats only.

3. OVERSEAS, RPS-Intl+ (rps_intl_plus, overseas_export.py) = 100 + 15 x z of the cohort performance signal against the international cohort, sign flipped for pitchers, clamped 60-140, null under five players per side.

The three are never pooled into one ranking.
entries.formula:
ACTIVE (browser, RPS+): 100 x (raw + 100) / (cohort_mean + 100) x position_multiplier, rounded, clamped 0-250; raw = level-relative performance (hitters wRC+ vs level - 100, pitchers 100 - ERA- vs level) - 10 x age-vs-level years; cohort = integer age x position group (age-only under 30 in cell)
DRAFT (rps_draft_plus): 100 + 15 x z(college performance vs class), clamped 60-140
OVERSEAS (rps_intl_plus): 100 + 15 x z(cohort performance signal, pitcher sign flipped), clamped 60-140
entries.example: A 21yo catcher and a 21yo first baseman with the same wRC+ vs level read different active RPS+: x1.08 against x1.00. A college bat at rps_draft_plus 115 is one full standard deviation above his class, a larger gap than 115 on the active board.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Farm development index: 100 = league-mean FV growth, 10 points = one standard deviation across the 30 orgs. Drives the Development branch of the farm grade.
entries.methodology: Each farm's cumulative FV growth over a trailing window (1y through 8y; 7y is the principal window) scored against the league-mean farm. Acquisitions are nullified (a trade-in adds nothing to the receiving farm's development) and graduations do not subtract, so it measures development of prospects already in the system. The blended trajectory_score weights the principal 7y window 60%, 3y 30% and 1y 10%.
entries.formula:
DvM+ = 100 + 10 · (org_growth − league_mean_growth) / league_stdev
trajectory_score = 0.60·7y + 0.30·3y + 0.10·1y
entries.example: An org at 7yDvM+ 130 grew its prospects' aggregate FV three standard deviations faster than the average farm over seven years, acquisitions excluded.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Lifetime change in a prospect's consensus tool grade - first observation to latest.
entries.methodology: For each tool with ≥2 consensus snapshots: delta = last grade − first grade. Feeds the +N / -N chip beside each tool on the prospect page, the Tool development table, and the org rollups (HitDvM+, PowerDvM+, …, ToolDvM+). A tool observed once has no delta (not enough signal), which is different from no change.
entries.formula: tool_delta(tool) = consensus_grade_latest(tool) − consensus_grade_first(tool)
entries.example: Jesús Made's game power went from 30 (FG 2024 pre-season) to 60 (2026 pre-season): +30 over 12 observations.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Org tool-development composite, weighted by what each position needs. 100 = league-mean pace; +10 = 1σ.
entries.methodology:
Position-weighted blend of the org's per-tool DvM+ (HitDvM+, PowerDvM+, SpeedDvM+, FieldDvM+, ArmDvM+, PitchSelDvM+, BatCtrlDvM+ for hitters; FBDvM+, SLDvM+, CBDvM+, CHDvM+, CmdDvM+, CtDvM+ for pitchers). Each per-tool DvM+ is the league-anchored 100 + 10z of the org's mean lifetime tool delta across its multi-cycle actives. Each tool is weighted by its importance to the position bucket: catchers' Field and Arm, outfielders' Speed, starters' Fastball and Command.

Computed per bucket (C / INF / OF / SP / RP) from the bucket's own per-tool DvM+ (org-wide value when a cell is sparse), then blended across buckets by how many prospects the org develops in each.

FanGraphs physical grades are excluded (static values with no multi-snapshot history). Attribution is current org: a traded prospect brings his lifetime delta. Display only; not in farm_score.
entries.formula:
ToolDvM+ = Σ_bucket (n_bucket · ToolDvM+_bucket) / Σ_bucket n_bucket
ToolDvM+_bucket = Σ_tool (w_tool · DvM+_tool) / Σ_tool w_tool
where w_tool is the tool's position-importance weight for that bucket
entries.example: An org that develops Field and Arm in its catchers and Fastball and Command in its starters outscores an equal-on-average org whose gains came in low-importance tools. NYM 106 (1st of 30) ≈ +0.6σ.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Per-tool org development index. 100 = league mean; +10 = 1σ.
entries.methodology: Same shape as DvM+ and ToolDvM+, one tool at a time. For each tool group (Hit, Power = mean of game_pwr and raw_pwr, Speed, Field, Arm, PitchSel, BatCtrl, FB, SL, CB, CH, Cmd, Ct), every org's mean lifetime delta across actives with ≥2 consensus observations of that tool, anchored 100 + 10z across the league. Cells with fewer than 3 contributing prospects render ' - '.
entries.formula: ToolDvM+ = 100 + 10 · (org_mean_lifetime_delta − league_mean) / league_stdev
entries.example: MIL HitDvM+ 119 and PowerDvM+ 124: a power-bat development specialist, about +2σ of game-power growth over the league mean.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Hit-tool index: reliability-weighted blend of performance (AVG + contact), Statcast (zone contact + whiff) and the Hit / Bat Control grade. 100 = average.
entries.methodology: Base weights 45% performance / 25% Statcast / 30% Hit tool. Performance = 0.6 · AVG-vs-level + 0.4 · K%-avoidance-vs-level; performance and Statcast are down-weighted by sample reliability (performance anchored at 170 AB, zone signals at about 200 tracked pitches), so a thin sample leans on the scouting prior. AVG and K% avoidance are distinct contact measures, so both stay. Hit grade = mean of Hit and Bat Control (50 → 100, ±10 ≈ ±20). The Statcast pool anchors (z-contact ≈ 80%, whiff ≈ 26%) are placeholders pending per-level MiLB calibration.
entries.formula:
HIT+ = Σ wᵢ·xᵢ / Σ wᵢ
perf:     x = 100·(0.6·AVG_ratio + 0.4·contact_ratio),  w = 0.45 · AB/(AB+170)
statcast: x = 0.5·Zcon/80 + 0.5·26/Whiff (×100),  w = 0.25 · pitches/(pitches+200)
tool:     x = 100 + (mean(Hit,BatCtrl) − 50)·2,  w = 0.30  (prior)
entries.example: A AA hitter at .300 (level .246) with a 16% K% (level 22.5%), 82% zone contact, 55 Hit and 60 Bat Control: perf ~133, Statcast ~103, tool ~115 → HIT+ ~122.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Isolated power indexed to the level-average ISO. 100 = level average; a point is about 1% (the wRC+ ratio convention).
entries.methodology: ISO (SLG − AVG) against the current level's average ISO from DATA.level_norms, the same baseline every '+' metric uses: 120 is 20% above, 80 is 20% below. Empirical-Bayes shrunk toward the level average by AB (ISO stabilizes around 150 PA). No scouting blend (that is POW+). Hitters only, 40-game minimum.
entries.formula: ISO+ = 100 + (100·ISO/level_avg_ISO − 100) · AB/(AB+150)   (empirical-Bayes shrunk toward the level average by AB)
entries.example: A High-A hitter at .180 ISO where the level averages .130 posts ISO+ ~138.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Hitter power index: reliability-weighted blend of ISO+ (performance), Statcast (hard-hit + barrel) and the Power grade. The grade anchors thin samples; observed stats take over as PA accrue. 100 = average.
entries.methodology:
Base weights 45% performance / 25% Statcast / 30% Power grade. Performance and Statcast are down-weighted by their own reliability (ISO stabilizes around 150 PA; batted-ball quality in tens of batted balls).

The performance signal is ISO+ alone. An HR-rate+ term was dropped because ISO+ and HR-rate+ correlate 0.91 across active hitters and double-counted one trait. Against graduate outcomes the reliability-weighted POW+ predicts MLB ISO at 0.50, up from 0.35.

Power grade 50 → 100, ±10 ≈ ±20. Statcast pool anchors (hard-hit ≈ 33%, barrel ≈ 6%) are placeholders pending per-level MiLB calibration. PWR+ is the retired label, kept as a search alias.
entries.formula:
POW+ = sum(w_i x x_i) / sum(w_i)
perf:     x = the UN-shrunk level-relative ISO ratio (the ISO+ pill's pre-shrink value; the AB discount enters through w, so the sample penalty is applied once),  w = 0.45 x AB/(AB+150)
statcast: x = 0.55 x HH%/33 + 0.45 x Brl%/6 (x100),  w = 0.25 x BBE/(BBE+40)
tool:     x = 100 + (Power_grade - 50) x 2,  w = 0.30  (prior, full weight)
entries.example: A AA hitter at ISO+ 145, 40% hard-hit and 9% barrel (Statcast ~134) with a 60 Power grade (tool 120) → POW+ ~135.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Plate-discipline index: BB% minus K% against the level mean, sigma-scaled (100 = level average, 10 points = one standard deviation of that differential at the level), blended 70/30 with the Pitch Selection (PSel) grade.
entries.methodology: Raw = 100 + 10 · (player_diff − level_diff) / sigma_level, with diff = BB% − K% and sigma_level the standard deviation among qualifying hitters at the level (pooled sigma when the level pool is thin). The additive scale (1 point = 1 percentage point) was retired 2026-07-29 because the level sigma runs ~7.5pp (AAA) to ~9.9pp (CPX). The raw index is blended 70/30 with the PSel grade, mapped by the outcome-calibrated piecewise curve (50 → 100; roughly 40 → 85, 60 → 122). Hitters only; the raw half needs 20+ games (20-39 reads provisional). Below the gate a graded prospect gets the tool alone; without a PSel grade the raw stat stands alone. Formerly Disci+.
entries.formula:
PD+ = 0.7 · raw + 0.3 · tool+
raw = 100 + 10 · (diff_player − diff_level) / sigma_level, diff = BB% − K%
tool+ = outcome-calibrated piecewise map of the PSel grade (50 → 100)
entries.example: A hitter one standard deviation above his level's BB%−K% posts raw 110. Juan Soto's prospect-era differential ran ~25pp above the typical bat, about +3σ, a raw near 130.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Peripheral pitcher index: K%, BB% and HR/9 against the level mean. 100 = level-average peripherals; 10 points ≈ one standard deviation.
entries.methodology:
Z-score composite of strikeout rate (+), walk rate (−) and HR/9 (−), each against the pitcher's current level mean. K% and BB% are per batter, so relievers and starters read on one basis (K/9 over-rewards short outings). Pitchers only; the gate passes at 20 innings or 30 batters faced.

Weights 0.55 / 0.30 / 0.15, renormalized over the components on file. Sigma is the level's empirical standard deviation where the level-norms block has one, else 15% of the level mean. Clamped 0-250.

One implementation: storage._compute_peripheral_stf_plus feeds the statline field the prospect card and the breakout gate read. The PROSPX leaderboard's JS version was reconciled onto this formula on 2026-07-29, so card and leaderboard agree.

The 'p' marks the peripheral version, next to FVStuff+ (scouting grades) and aStuff+ (measured AAA pitch physics).
entries.formula:
pStuff+ = 100 + 10 x [0.55 z(K%) - 0.30 z(BB%) - 0.15 z(HR/9)] / (sum of the weights present), clamped to 0-250.
z uses the level's empirical sigma when the level-norms block carries one, else 0.15 x the level mean. K% and BB% are per-batter rates.
entries.example: A AA pitcher at 30% K%, 7% BB% and 0.8 HR/9 where the level means are 22% / 9% / 1.0 posts pStuff+ ~125.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: In-house pitch-quality model for AAA pitchers, scoring per-pitch kinematics against run value. 100 = qualified-AAA pool mean, 10 points = one standard deviation of that pool; higher is better. Named after the industry Stuff+ convention; it is our AAA-trained model, not FanGraphs Stuff+.
entries.methodology:
Built to score stuff for pitchers who have not debuted. Public Stuff+ (FanGraphs; Eno Sarris and Max Bay) covers MLB tracking only. A LightGBM regressor is trained on Savant minors per-pitch data (AAA, 2023 on) to predict each pitch's run value from physics alone: velocity, spin, extension, arm-side-signed horizontal and vertical movement, release point, arm angle, and the velocity gap off the primary fastball. No pitch-type labels and no results enter the features.

A pitcher's score is his season mean predicted run value, shrunk toward the pool mean below 300 pitches, scaled so 100 is the qualified-AAA mean and 10 points is one standard deviation of the SHRUNK pool. Until 2026-08-04 the divisor was the raw pool's spread, so the index moved 7.16 points per sigma (an aStuff+ of 110 was +1.40σ). Served rows read slightly under 10 points per sigma because they reach down to 50 tracked pitches against the pool's 340 floor; that is reliability shrink, not scale.

Validated season-out (train 2023-24, score 2025) and gated forward against graduates' first-MLB outcomes; the eval ships in data/stuff_plus_aaa_eval.json whatever it says. 2026-09-11 reading (n = 21 debuts): final-AAA aStuff+ tracks first-MLB K% (r 0.47) and not run prevention (r 0.02 on inverted ERA); the ERA leg is unpowered at this sample. A strikeout-stuff signal, not an ERA forecast.

Differs from FanGraphs Stuff+ (MLB-only, different data and target), pStuff+ (peripheral results vs level) and FVStuff+ (scouting grades).
entries.formula:
aStuff+ = 100 + 10 · (μ_pool − RV̂_shrunk) / σ_pool
where RV̂_shrunk = (n · RV̂ + 300 · μ_pool) / (n + 300)
entries.example: A AAA starter whose pitches grade one standard deviation better than the qualified pool over 1,500 tracked pitches posts ~110; the same stuff over 150 pitches reads nearer 103.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Scouting-grade pitch composite: power mean of fastball and secondary grades, z-scored across the prospect cohort.
entries.methodology: Power mean (p = 3) of the 20-80 Fastball, Slider, Curveball and Changeup grades, z-scored across the active-prospect cohort: 100 = cohort mean, 10 points = 1σ. pStuff+ measures results (K%, BB%, HR/9) against level peers; FVStuff+ measures projected stuff from scouting reports. They diverge when results outrun or lag the scouting view. Formerly 'Stuff grade+'.
entries.formula:
FVStuff+ = 100 + 10 · (composite_stuff − μ) / σ
where composite_stuff = (Σ pitch_grade^3 / n)^(1/3)
entries.example: A 70 fastball / 60 slider / 55 curve / 50 change composite is ~62; with a cohort mean of 55 and σ of 6, FVStuff+ ≈ 112.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Per-prospect expected MLB surplus value in $M from the value framework, continuous in FV (a 47.3 prices between 45 and 50). Prospects only; debuted players are valued on realized WAR (see Surplus value). Not OrgSur+, the farm-level index.
entries.methodology:
Sur+ is the value framework's prospect surplus: a mixture over five career outcomes (bust / bench / regular / good / star), each outcome's control-year WAR path priced season by season at the tiered $/WAR, netted of pre-arb and arb costs, probability-weighted, discounted at net 7 percent, passed through the v6 EV calibration, and scaled by the position multiplier. Priced through the clemens_2026 valuation set (Ben Clemens' 2026 FanGraphs framework). Hitters price above pitchers at equal FV (injury and role-conversion attrition).

The single-path formula (peak WAR × 6 × ramp × success probability × tier rate) and its dollar anchors are retired.
entries.formula:
Sur+ = iso_cal( Σ_bucket P(bucket | FV, side) × PV( Σ_season WAR_s × $/WAR_tier(WAR_s) − cost_s ) ) × position_mult
priced through the active valuation set (clemens_2026); see Value Framework
entries.example: A FV 47.3 hitter prices on the interpolated curve between his FV 45 and FV 50 neighbors, not at either one; a shortstop at the same grade carries the shortstop multiplier on top.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Graduate metric: MLB WAR per season minus the WAR per season his grade implied over the same MLB seasons, shrunk toward 0 on a thin sample. One definition, baked once per graduate.
entries.methodology:
One computation (value_framework.wag), baked into each graduate's block and read by every PROSPX and farm surface: the graduate card tile, chart and summary, the graduates list, pill and sorts, the board's surplus cell, the Time Machine, WARWAG, and the farm grade's Talent Translation and Boom and Bust rates. The overseas signings table is the one exception: it still serves the plain residual against the survivor WAR per season at the grade.

Baseline: the grade's expected WAR over the same number of MLB seasons, busts included, at the eFV grade he carried at debut (consensus FV where eFV abstains). Matched to seasons, not plate appearances: an injury-shortened season counts as a season, so WAG reflects accumulation over time. The chart draws each season's WAR against the same per-season baseline.

The number shown is the per-season residual times a reliability weight w on his measured MLB exposure, so a thin sample regresses hard toward 0.

Exposure is his MLB PA (hitters) or innings (pitchers) from the MLB Stats API rows (PA read as AB x 1.1). Where those rows carry nothing for his role, as for graduates with no MLB row on file (Mike Trout among them), the gate reads the war_daily PA or innings of the stints his WAR sums, stored with his WAR. For the season in progress that load can run ahead of a WAR last refreshed earlier. Where neither exists the gate reads each season as 600 PA or 200 IP and the block says exposure_measured false.

Boom and bust are the 80th and 20th percentiles of the expectation at his exposure, called only once measured exposure reaches 200 PA or 80 IP. Below that he reads unsettled and no WAG is shown.

WAR basis: eWAR from the 2026-09 epoch (bWAR before it). A position player's WAG is unchanged by the epoch; a pitcher's moves with his FIP re-pricing within role.
entries.formula:
WAG = w x (WAR/season - E[WAR/season | eFV at debut, same seasons]), 0 <= w < 1
w = reliability weight on measured MLB PA or IP (MLB Stats API rows, else the war_daily stints of his WAR)
boom: percentile >= 0.80 · bust: percentile <= 0.20 · gate: 200 PA or 80 IP measured
entries.example: 1.4 WAR per season against a 1.2 baseline is a residual of +0.2. A veteran with thousands of PA serves close to +0.2; a rookie at 250 PA serves well under half of it.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Graduate metric: WAR per season plus WAG per season.
entries.methodology: WAR per MLB season plus WAG (see WAG), read from the same baked block, so it rewards graduates who are both productive and ahead of their grade. Shown only where WAG is shown (measured exposure past the gate), else None and the row sinks in the WARWAG sort. Sort on the Graduates list. WAR basis: eWAR from the 2026-09 epoch.
entries.formula: WARWAG = WAR/season + WAG
entries.example: 2.5 WAR per season exactly on grade: WAG 0, WARWAG 2.5. 2.5 against a 2.0 baseline with w 0.9: WAG 0.45, WARWAG 2.95.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The module behind every FV↔WAR↔$ conversion. Prospects flow FV → projected WAR → projected $; debuted players use realized WAR → $. The two are never mixed in one ratio.
entries.methodology:
Engine v2.0, a career-path mixture (the v32.1 single-path formula is retired). A prospect is priced as a mixture of five outcomes (bust / bench / regular / good / star) with P(bucket | FV, side) fit on the Clemens 2025 published percentage tables (proportional-odds ordinal model; training_n 678 hitter / 437 pitcher, data/value_framework_fitted.json). Each bucket carries a per-season WAR path over the seven control years in the valuation set (three pre-arb plus four arb; clemens_2026 params.control.years 7). Each season is priced at the tiered $/WAR (convex: a star season costs more per win), costs (league-minimum pre-arb, escalating arb) are netted, and the result is probability-weighted and discounted at net 7 percent (clemens_2026 params.discount.net_rate 0.07: a 10 percent discount rate minus 3 percent annual win-cost growth). The FV → WAR level comes from the fitted EV anchors (see FV → WAR). The v6 EV calibration (isotonic-real-v6-evframe-2026-07-31), a count-weighted isotonic map fit on resolved-cohort bin means, makes the published number an expected value (no $0 floor on low tiers). Production prices through the clemens_2026 valuation set (checksummed anchors; the fa_implied $/WAR re-anchor is disabled under it). Every input is configurable and every FV interpolates, not just the 5-point anchors. Backend and frontend read one generated snapshot (data/value_framework.json and .js).

Two regimes, never mixed:
• **Prospects** (pre-debut, FV grade): the mixture above. A projection.
• **Debuted / MLB players** (career_war on file): actual WAR × $/WAR_overall. A realized figure.
The Transactions Trade Audit uses neither regime directly: it prices every party, prospect or veteran, at today's Trade Machine trade value, one forward currency on both sides. Career WAR is context there and never enters a total.
entries.formula:
Prospect: Surplus($M) = iso_cal( Σ_bucket P(bucket|FV,side) × PV( Σ_season WAR_s × $/WAR_tier(WAR_s) − cost_s ) ) × position_mult
Vet: Value($M) = career_war × $/WAR_overall (≈ $11.74M, rolling 3yr 2024-2026)
entries.example: A FV 60 hitter is priced as his whole outcome mix, bust mass included: each bucket's control-year WAR path is priced season by season, netted of costs, weighted, discounted and calibrated. Bobby Witt Jr. (veteran): 22.5 career WAR × $11.74M ≈ $264M realized value. Different quantities, both shown.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Three-tier $M per WAR the free-agent market pays (fringe / mid / star), rolling three-year average. Tier-aware for per-player prices; the overall rate for career aggregates.
entries.methodology:
From FanGraphs' 2026 'What Are Teams Paying for a Win in Free Agency': teams pay non-linearly for projected first-year WAR, and the star premium has roughly doubled since 2020-2023, so a flat $/WAR misprices both ends. The framework uses the rolling 2024-2026 average of the article's three tiers, dispatched off projected per-season WAR.
• **Prospect surplus**: each projected season prices at the tier its WAR falls in.
• **Veteran career WAR**: the overall rate ($11.74M), because a career aggregates seasons from every tier.
Used for prospect surplus and contract surplus.

The fa_implied re-anchor (rescaling the tier level to the FA signings-implied series, trailing three winters) exists in the engine and is disabled under the production clemens_2026 set: served prospect dollars sit on the published FanGraphs rates, checksummed at load. The signings-implied series is published in the FA module ($/WAR by winter).
entries.formula:
$/WAR ≈ $6.97M (0-1 WAR) · $8.76M (1-2) · $13.63M (2+) · $11.74M overall (rolling 2024-2026)
Per-prospect: dispatches off WAR_peak. Per-vet: uses overall.
entries.example: A 4-WAR season prices at $13.63M per WAR; a 0.5-WAR season at $6.97M. A 30-WAR career prices at 30 × $11.74M = $352M on the overall rate, which avoids over-pricing late-career seasons that sit in lower tiers.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The FV → WAR conversion. Three quantities are served and they are not interchangeable: a prime/talent anchor (peak season if he makes it; display), an EV anchor (expected WAR per season over the first six MLB seasons, busts included; prices every dollar), and the survivor expectation (expected WAR per season given no bust; the overseas signing WAG baseline).
entries.methodology:
Quoting one number for different quantities is the common FV → WAR error. Prime WAR (fv_to_prime_war) is survivor talent at peak, the industry table (a 60 FV as a 3-WAR regular); it drives the displayed prime path and headline peak WAR. EV WAR (fv_to_6yr_avg_war) averages every outcome, bust mass included, across the first six seasons; it is the only quantity multiplied by $/WAR, and it runs 2-3x below prime at most grades. Survivor WAR (survivor_expected_war) is the EV curve conditioned on not busting, from the same bucket probabilities; the overseas signings' WAG and the client FV_WAR_ANCHORS read it. The graduate WAG does not: it is measured against the busts-included expectation at the eFV grade at debut (see WAG).

EV anchors, 2026-09-04 fit (data/value_framework_fitted.json empirical_anchors): FV 80 3.50, FV 70 2.49, FV 65 2.01, FV 60 1.44, FV 55 0.98, FV 50 0.68, FV 45 0.32, FV 40 0.071; FV 35 0.0069, FV 30 0.0058, FV 25 0.0051, FV 20 0.0044. Each anchor at FV 45-60 is a 50/50 blend of our resolved-cohort mean (2014-2020 cohorts, eWAR labels) and a public reference scaled from Edwards' fWAR tables; FV 65 and 70 weight the reference 0.71 and 0.82 for thin cells (n 19 and 8), and FV 80 is the reference alone. The FV 20-40 knots are declared values (amended 2026-09-04), a floor and not a measurement. Half-grades interpolate linearly. The EV table drives surplus value, Sur+, $/FV-pt and the projected career WAR behind the trade-regret view.
entries.formula:
Prime/talent anchor (survivor, display): 80→6.5, 70→4.7, 65→3.8, 60→3.0, 55→2.3, 50→1.7, 45→1.1, 40→0.6
EV anchor (all outcomes, prices dollars): see the dated 2026-09-04 row in the methodology; half-grades interpolate
Survivor expectation (overseas signing WAG baseline): EV anchor conditioned on P(not bust), per side
entries.example: A FV 60 reads as a ~3-WAR player at peak if he makes it (prime), is worth ~1.44 expected WAR per season over his first six seasons once busts and the ramp are priced (EV), and is expected ~1.55 per season as a hitter who does not bust (survivor). Dollars always multiply the EV figure.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Per-FV, per-side probability of each career outcome bucket (bust / bench / regular / good / star). The curve is fit on the Clemens 2025 PUBLISHED percentage tables, not on the site's resolved cohorts; our resolved rows enter only through the out-of-fold dispersion correction on top. The bust share is the served bust risk.
entries.methodology:
Borrowed, per side, continuous in FV: p_bucket_given_fv is a proportional-odds ordinal model (per-side cutpoints and slope in data/value_framework_fitted.json). Training rows are the Clemens 2025 published percentage tables at FV 45, 45+, 50, 55 and 60, reconstructed to integer counts (count = round(pct * n)) and expanded to one row per player: training_n is 678 hitter and 437 pitcher. Corrected 2026-09-04: this entry previously said the buckets were estimated from our resolved cohorts; they are not. Extrapolated at both ends: no published five-bucket table exists under FV 45, so everything served below 45 is the fit extended downward, and the FV 65+ cells were dropped for thin n (hitter ≤ 3, pitcher ≤ 2).

Dispersion correction: a per-side Platt map in log-odds, logit(p') = A + B * logit(p), fit out of fold on our resolved rows (n 516: 244 hitters, 272 pitchers), A/B 0.7268/0.3749 hitter and 0.7269/0.3553 pitcher. Strictly monotone, so it moves no rank, grade or dollar. It applies only where p_bust is read at the eFV odds grade; on a consensus FV key the curve shows a level error rather than a slope error, so the trade machine and the projections page read it uncorrected.

The odds are keyed on _odds_grade = realized_implied_fv while the board shows outcome_implied_fv. Measured 2026-08-07, the two maps agreed on 76.8 percent of rows below FV 40, 1.6 percent at 40-45 and 0.0 percent above 45, so at the top of the board the odds and the grade beside them are not two readings of one number.

The bucket names come from the Clemens per-season talent bands (bust <0.5, bench 0.5-1.5, regular 1.5-2.5, good 2.5-4.0, star 4.0+ WAR), but the engine prices each bucket at a level scaled to the grade, below the band edges at almost every grade (a FV 60 hitter's star bucket prices at about 2.7 WAR per season), so the bands name the buckets and are not their levels. The fit replaced a hand table from public research (Sickels 2002-2012, McDaniel / Longenhagen 2014-2020). The distribution feeds the surplus mixture, the star-odds diagnostic and the outcome chart on every card, and it is re-scored nightly against resolved outcomes by the live calibration monitor with a bust-bucket drift tripwire.
entries.formula: P(bucket | FV, side) = proportional-odds ordinal fit on the Clemens 2025 published tables (per-side cutpoints + slope), over buckets bust < bench < regular < good < star; bucket levels scaled to FV, not the band edges; served p' = sigmoid(A + B * logit(p)) per side, read at _odds_grade = realized_implied_fv
entries.example: The same FV yields a different five-bucket mix for a hitter than for a pitcher, and the surplus engine weights the whole mix, not one success percentage.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A prospect's surplus per FV point: Sur+ / FV. Prospects only; an MLB player has no meaningful per-FV rate.
entries.methodology: Per prospect: $/FV = Sur+ / FV, after the position multiplier and on the continuous FV. For a trade side: sum prospect dollars and prospect FV, then divide. On a Trade Audit card every party is priced at the Trade Machine trade value; the MLB players' dollars on a side are named separately and never enter the ratio. Used to compare trade sides on cost-controlled prospect capital and to benchmark orgs.
entries.formula:
Per-prospect: $/FV-pt = Sur+ / FV
Per trade-side: $/FV-pt = Σ(prospect_$) / Σ(prospect_FV)  (vet $ reported separately)
entries.example: A trade where Org A receives 15 FV of prospects worth $25M plus one veteran worth $48M reads '$73.0M (15 FV · $1.7M/FV) incl. $48.0M (1 vet)', never $73M / 15 = $4.9M per FV.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Active prospects' current FV per $M of trailing-3yr draft-pool spend. Fast-cycle companion to war_per_m_pool.
entries.methodology: Companion to the WAR-per-$M draft-pool signal. war_per_m_pool sums graduate career WAR from the (T-5)..(T-2) drafts and lags about five years; fv_per_m_pool sums the current consensus FV of the still-active prospects from the same drafts and moves with the next ranking cycle. Same denominator (the org's pool dollars for the window), so high FV per $M with low WAR per $M is a leading signal (the talent is there, the WAR has not arrived) and the reverse says graduate success is not being replenished. Gated only on pool > $0.
entries.formula: fv_per_m_pool = Σ(active_fv | drafted T-5..T-2) / (org_pool_$ T-5..T-2 / 1M)
entries.example: Org X spent $35M of pool over T-5..T-2 and holds 280 FV points of active prospects from those drafts: 8.0 FV per $M, while WAR per $M can still read 0.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Org-level $ surplus per FV-point of active prospect capital. Captures the quality-of-FV-mix dimension.
entries.methodology: Inside the fin_active_surplus leaf. The org's total active-prospect Sur+ ($M) divided by its total active-prospect FV points. High means the FV sits in premium positions (SS, CF, top SP) or high grades where the surplus curve is steep; low means depth-heavy (many FV 45-50 corner and bench profiles). Separates two orgs with the same raw FV points. Gated at ≥5 contributing actives.
entries.formula: surplus_per_fv_pt_mm = Σ(Sur+ across actives) / Σ(FV across same actives)
entries.example: Org A: 250 FV points, $400M surplus → $1.6M per FV point. Org B: 400 FV points, $300M → $0.75M.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Starting pitcher - projects to start games (typically 5+ innings per outing).
entries.methodology: Carries the workload: 5+ innings per outing in a five-man rotation. The projection needs 3+ quality pitches and command good enough to face a lineup several times. SP-projected prospects usually grade above relief-projected arms with similar stuff, because innings count for more than leverage in WAR. The `SP` filter chip matches SP-tagged prospects only (not SIRP / MIRP / bare RP).

entries.definition: Relief pitcher - generic relief role. Rolls up SIRP + MIRP + bare RP for filtering.
entries.methodology: The 'RP' filter chip is a rollup: single-inning relievers (SIRP: closer, setup), multi-inning relievers (MIRP: bulk, long relief) and bare-RP prospects with no role yet. Use the SIRP / MIRP chips when the leverage-versus-bulk split matters.

entries.definition: Single-Inning Relief Pitcher - closer or high-leverage setup role (~1 inning per outing).
entries.methodology: FanGraphs tags a pitcher SIRP when his projected role is one-inning, high-leverage relief: closer, setup, fireman. Typically above-average fastball velocity plus at least one plus secondary, without the depth or command to turn a lineup over. The most leverage per inning of any role and the fewest innings, so even an elite SIRP rarely projects above FV 50-55.

entries.definition: Multi-Inning Relief Pitcher - long relief, bulk follower, or swingman (~2+ innings per outing).
entries.methodology: FanGraphs tags a pitcher MIRP when his projected role is 2+ innings per outing: long relief, bulk behind an opener, or swingman. Typically starter-quality stuff with a command or depth gap that keeps him out of the rotation. More innings than a SIRP and less leverage per inning; the FV ceiling sits between a starter and a SIRP.

entries.definition: Future Value: the 20-80 grade for the MLB role a prospect is most likely to settle into. 50 is an average regular.
entries.methodology: Tracked sources (FanGraphs, MLB Pipeline, ESPN, Just Baseball, TJStats, Baseball America, The Athletic) publish a 20-80 grade per prospect. The consensus FV quantile-maps each source's grade onto the FanGraphs scale, averages them at equal weight (every source votes 1.0; the 2026-06 accuracy weights were reverted 2026-07-25 as unearned) and rounds up; a player only one source has ever graded is pulled one third toward FV 35. FV 50 is a projected MLB regular, 60 a first-division regular or future star, 70+ a perennial All-Star ceiling.
entries.formula:
consensus FV = ceil( mean( scale-normalized latest FV per source ) ), clamped 20-80
single-source case: (2/3) · FV + (1/3) · 35 until a second grade lands
entries.example: Jackson Holliday's FV 65 as a prospect meant a future star: a tier above an everyday regular, below a perennial All-Star.

entries.definition: The standard scouting ladder. 20 = far below MLB, 50 = MLB average, 80 = elite.
entries.methodology: Scouting grades have used this scale since the 1950s. 50 is an MLB-average regular or role player, 60 a first-division regular or All-Star, 70 a perennial All-Star, 80 a Hall of Fame ceiling. Used for individual tools (Hit, Power, Speed, Field, Throw, Fastball) and for Future Value.
entries.example: A 70-grade fastball means top ~5% of MLB starters. A 70-grade hit tool means batting-title contender.

entries.definition: 20-80 grade for bat-to-ball ability and projected batting average.
entries.methodology: Contact rate, plate coverage, pitch recognition and projected batting average against MLB pitching. 50 ≈ .260, 60 ≈ .290, 70 ≈ .320.

entries.definition: 20-80 grade for in-game power output (HRs and extra-base hits).
entries.methodology: How much raw power plays in games, given swing path, pitch recognition and approach. Almost always ≤ raw power for the same player.

entries.definition: 20-80 grade for BP / theoretical max power, regardless of in-game application.
entries.methodology: Peak capability: exit velocity, batting-practice home-run distance, peak EV. Game power adds whether the swing gets to it in competition.

entries.definition: 20-80 grade for foot speed. 60-yard dash, home-to-first time, baserunning instincts. Displayed as RUN across the site (the legacy abbreviation SPD also resolves).
entries.methodology: Plays on both sides of the ball: offense (baserunning, BABIP, extra bases) and defense (range, jumps, recovery). Run contributes to both the offensive (O-Tool, 4% weight) and defensive (D-Tool, 10% weight for non-catchers) composites for hitters.

entries.definition: 20-80 grade for defense; range, hands, instincts, throwing accuracy.
entries.methodology: Grades are position-relative: a 60 Field at SS is not the same skill as a 60 at 1B. 50 = an average MLB defender at the position.

entries.definition: 20-80 grade for arm strength and accuracy.
entries.methodology: Most important at OF, SS, 3B and C; less at 1B and 2B. 60+ is a plus arm, 70+ elite (Andruw Jones, Yadier Molina).

entries.definition: A prospect becomes 'Debuted' the moment MLB records their first MLB game.
entries.methodology: The MLB API's mlbDebutDate is the source of truth: once set, the prospect leaves the active pool for the Debuted tab. A prospect outrighted off the 40-man is also promoted out (a 40-man history already makes him a non-prospect). With neither signal, the debut date falls back to the earliest MLB-season Opening Day in career stats. Rookie-eligibility thresholds (130 AB / 50 IP / 45 active-roster days) are not used; they produced wrong dates whenever an input was stale.
entries.formula: debuted iff mlbDebutDate is set OR an outright transaction is on file

entries.definition: League- and park-adjusted offensive value, published by MLB. 100 = MLB average; 120 is 20% above, 80 is 20% below. Displayed, never derived: the MLB Stats hitter board reads MLB's published figure verbatim beside HEM+, the offense-rate index the site computes. Coloured on the value ruler at 145 / 130 / 120 / 100 / 85.
entries.methodology: Read verbatim from MLB's bulk season-total feed, matched by player id, so a traded hitter reads one season line and two name keys on one player cannot produce two numbers. MLB only; MiLB uses the level-relative RPS+ proxy. It runs wider than HEM+ because it is unshrunk: over the pooled 2021-2026 qualified pools (2,069 hitter-seasons) published wRC+ has a standard deviation of 25.3 against 17.7 for HEM+. So the column bands at 85, 120 and 145, the cuts that reproduce the HEM+ band shares on the wider distribution. Shown at 100+ plate appearances, like the site's other rate indices.
entries.origin: Industry metric. Linear-weights framework by Tom Tango and coauthors (The Book); wRC+ implemented by FanGraphs and published by MLB. We display it as the offensive baseline next to our own metrics and compute no version of it.

entries.definition: On-base Plus Slugging; OBP + SLG. The simplest catch-all hitter rate.
entries.methodology: .700 is below average, .800 an above-average regular, .900+ star level. No park or league adjustment; wRC+ has both.
entries.formula: OPS = OBP + SLG
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: Isolated Power, SLG minus AVG. Pure power rate.
entries.methodology: Removes singles from slugging. .140 is MLB average, .200 above average, .250+ elite.
entries.formula: ISO = SLG − AVG
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: Batting Average. Hits divided by at-bats.
entries.methodology: H / AB. Ignores walks and does not separate singles from homers; still a contact signal. .260-.270 is MLB average, .300+ above average.
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: On-base Percentage. Times reached base (H + BB + HBP) divided by plate appearances.
entries.methodology: Contact and discipline together. .330 is MLB average, .380+ elite. Reached-on-error does not count.
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: Slugging Percentage. Total bases per at-bat; weights extra-base hits.
entries.methodology: (1B + 2·2B + 3·3B + 4·HR) / AB. .425 is MLB average, .500+ is above-average, .550+ is elite.
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: Walk rate. Walks divided by plate appearances.
entries.methodology: ~8% is MLB average, 12%+ elite. Sticky across levels: a strong A+ walk rate usually carries into AAA and MLB.
entries.formula: BB% = BB / PA
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: Strikeout rate. Strikeouts divided by plate appearances; lower is better for hitters.
entries.methodology: MLB average is ~22%. Under 18% is above-average contact; 28%+ is a swing-and-miss concern. Mostly sticky across levels.
entries.formula: K% = K / PA
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: Earned Run Average. Earned runs allowed per 9 innings.
entries.methodology: No park or defense adjustment. 4.00 is MLB average, under 3.50 above average, under 3.00 elite. FIP and xFIP remove defense.
entries.formula: ERA = ER · 9 / IP
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: Fielding-Independent Pitching. ERA-scaled, using only K, BB, HBP, HR.
entries.methodology: What a pitcher's ERA would be with league-average results on balls in play. ~4.00 is MLB average; FIP- is the 100-anchored version. The MLB Stats bullpen and starter boards do not show this statistic: their Skill FIP column is a sample-shrunk version with a role-pool constant (see Skill FIP).
entries.formula: FIP = ((13·HR) + 3·(BB+HBP) − 2·K) / IP + constant
entries.origin: Industry metric. Created by Tom Tango, building on Voros McCracken's DIPS insight; popularized by FanGraphs.

entries.definition: Walks + Hits per Inning Pitched. Baserunner volume.
entries.methodology: (BB + H) / IP. 1.30 is MLB average, under 1.20 above average, under 1.10 elite.
entries.formula: WHIP = (BB + H) / IP
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: Expected FIP. FIP using league-average HR/FB rate instead of actual HR allowed.
entries.methodology: Removes home-run luck. More predictive year to year than FIP. ~4.00 is MLB average, under 3.50 above average.
entries.origin: Industry metric. Created by Dave Studeman (The Hardball Times): FIP with a league-average home-run rate substituted for actual homers.

entries.definition: Park- and league-adjusted FIP scaled to 100 = MLB average. Lower is better.
entries.methodology: 100 is league-average defense-independent run prevention; 80 is 20% better, 120 is 20% worse. Lower is better.
entries.origin: Industry metric. The FIP- park- and league-adjusted index, implemented by FanGraphs (100 = average, lower is better).

entries.definition: Strikeouts per 9 innings. Legacy here: K% (per batter) is the site's strikeout rate.
entries.methodology: 9 K/9 is MLB average for a starter, 11+ elite. K% is more stable across roles because starter and reliever innings per appearance differ. K/9 is used only as a fallback when batters faced is missing on an older MiLB row.
entries.formula: K/9 = K · 9 / IP
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: Walks per 9 innings. Legacy here: BB% (per batter) is the site's walk rate.
entries.methodology: 3.0 BB/9 is MLB average, under 2.5 above average, under 2.0 elite command. BB% is preferred because it normalizes for innings per appearance. BB/9 is a fallback when batters faced is missing on a career row.
entries.formula: BB/9 = BB · 9 / IP
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: Home runs allowed per 9 innings.
entries.methodology: ~1.3 HR/9 is MLB average, under 1.0 above average. Strongly park- and league-dependent.
entries.formula: HR/9 = HR · 9 / IP
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: Pitcher strikeout rate: strikeouts per batter faced. The site's strikeout rate (replaced K/9).
entries.methodology: Does not depend on innings per appearance, unlike K/9. ~22% is MLB average, 28%+ elite. When batters faced is missing on a career row, it is approximated from K/9 at ~4.3 batters per inning.
entries.formula: K% = K / TBF (fallback: K/9 ÷ 0.387 when TBF missing)
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: Pitcher walk rate: walks per batter faced. The site's walk rate (replaced BB/9).
entries.methodology: Same reasoning as K%. ~8% is MLB average, under 7% above average, under 6% elite command. Approximated from BB/9 ÷ 0.387 when batters faced is missing.
entries.formula: BB% = BB / TBF (fallback: BB/9 ÷ 0.387 when TBF missing)
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: Wins Above Replacement: one-number value estimate covering offense, defense, baserunning and position. The site's served WAR is eWAR (eephus WAR): the Baseball-Reference run frame with pitching re-priced on FIP; fielding unchanged pending SDR; position players match bWAR.
entries.methodology:
One series for every realized WAR: eWAR v2, read from one per-season map (career totals, per-season columns, current-season pills, WAR sorts, WAG's observed leg, eFV labels, arbitration, farm WAR per season). bWAR (Baseball-Reference via pybaseball's war_daily) is the input frame and was the served series through 2026-08. The 2026-09 epoch moved the served and label series to eWAR by owner decision, not on an accuracy claim: eWAR loses the descriptive team-wins gate and wins pitcher persistence (gate record in the eWAR entry). A position player's number did not move; a pitcher's is re-priced on his own FIP within role. Rough scale: 2 WAR per season is a regular, 4 above average, 6+ All-Star, 8+ MVP level. The realized baseline for WAG.

Reference tables keep their source's scale: Star Odds, the FV badge's peak WAR/yr and the outcome-bucket names are FanGraphs fWAR tables; half the weight of the FV → WAR EV anchor that prices surplus is a public fWAR reference; the draft slot curve and the /hof/ JAWS and WAR7 figures are bWAR.
entries.origin: Industry framework popularized by Tom Tango, Sean Smith and others; fWAR is FanGraphs' implementation, rWAR/bWAR Baseball-Reference's, WARP Baseball Prospectus'. The site serves eWAR, built on the Baseball-Reference frame.

entries.definition: eephusWAR (eWAR), the site's served WAR from the 2026-09 epoch: the Baseball-Reference run frame with pitching re-priced on FIP; fielding unchanged pending SDR; position players match bWAR. Every realized WAR a reader sees (career totals, per-season lines, current-season pills, WAG's observed leg, eFV labels, arbitration, farm WAR/yr) reads it. Industry tables do not: Star Odds, the FV badge's peak WAR/yr, and the published half of the FV-to-WAR anchor that prices surplus are on the FanGraphs frame. Coloured on the value ruler at 6 / 4 / 3 / 2.5 / 1.5 per season, with red under zero.
entries.methodology:
Frame: bWAR is the input (Baseball-Reference war_daily via pybaseball). eWAR v2 keeps every B-Ref component (batting runs, baserunning, double plays, positional adjustment, reliever leverage chaining, rfield) and replaces one: pitching runs above average are re-priced on the pitcher's own FIP (K, BB, HBP, HR over his innings; FIP constant from the FA projection corpus), carried to the RA9 scale, park-adjusted by the row's PPF, and re-centred per season and role so the starter and reliever totals each match B-Ref's. Replacement level is re-derived per season so league eWAR sums to the bWAR target (2011-2026 build: max deviation 0.0 wins, replacement scales 0.9966 to 1.0018). A Statcast fielding swap was built, measured and removed (blend weight 0.0; both forward legs fell as the weight rose from 0 to 1), so fielding is B-Ref rfield until Will Cahoon's SDR defense lands.

A position player's eWAR equals his bWAR season by season (2026-09-03 artifact: 21,454 batting blocks, 0 differences). A pitcher's eWAR redistributes runs within role: the SP and RP pool totals are B-Ref's by construction, and the largest 120+ IP move in the eval window is Zack Godley 2018 at +3.96.

Gates (data/ewar_eval.json, 2016-2025, eWAR and bWAR on identical rows). Gate 1, team wins over 300 team-seasons, r 0.8595 against bWAR 0.8803, zero-parameter MAE 4.306 against 3.787: a loss by construction, since a FIP-based WAR drops the sequencing and balls in play that decided the games (fWAR loses the same test). Gate 2, pitcher year-to-year persistence of runs above average per 9 IP over 1,677 pairs (min 50 IP), 0.3617 against 0.1768, 2.0x; the FIP component forecasts next season's actual runs above average at 0.2573 against 0.1768 for this season's actual. At team level the forward leg is a null (full-schedule pairs 0.5920 vs 0.5913). The basis flip is an owner decision about which series the site stands on, not an accuracy claim: the eFV label swap (measured 2026-08-04) moved eFV's margin over consensus by -0.0011 (hitters) and -0.0115 (pitchers), inside floors of 0.017 and 0.016, so the Methodology page's tie frame stands.

Coverage: data/ewar.json covers 2011-2026 at the 2026-09-03 build. THE LIVE SEASON REBUILDS NIGHTLY (owner decision 2026-09-11): the pipeline re-prices the current season every night before any page reads it, on that night's war_daily frames, StatsAPI pitching lines and standings. A season freezes on November 1 of its own year; from then on its numbers are carried byte for byte (each frozen season is hash-checked) and only a hand rebuild with the whole re-anchor cascade can re-price it, so nothing fit on completed seasons moves under the nightly. A refused night (a stale frame, an older input, an unreadable data file) keeps the previous night's numbers, and the boards stamp the build date beside the number when the gap opens. A player-season with no artifact block serves bWAR, and the fallback is recorded. Build: python tools/build_ewar.py --first 2011 --last 2026 --write.
entries.formula:
eWAR = bWAR - (B-Ref pitching runs above average) + (FIP-priced pitching runs above average, centred per season x role), then rescaled per season so sum(eWAR) = sum(bWAR) league-wide
position players: eWAR = bWAR (fielding blend w = 0.0 pending SDR)
pitchers: SP and RP pool totals unchanged; individual runs redistributed within role
entries.example: Aaron Nola 2018: bWAR 9.69, eWAR 6.14 (runs allowed better than his FIP; the move is toward his published fWAR). Zack Godley 2018: bWAR -0.92, eWAR 3.04. Both from data/ewar_eval.json face_validity. A 6.0-bWAR shortstop reads 6.0 eWAR.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. Built on the Baseball-Reference run frame (war_daily via pybaseball); the FIP re-pricing of pitching follows the FanGraphs tradition.

entries.definition: The site-computed FV: an equal-weight mean of every source's grade after cross-source normalization, with single-instance shrinkage. The 2026-06 accuracy weights were reverted 2026-07-25 as unearned.
entries.methodology:
Per snapshot, the consensus is the mean of the explicit FVs from every tracked source, each first quantile-mapped onto the FanGraphs scale on the players both grade (see Normalized source grade); the per-source grades on the card stay as published. A player only one source has ever graded is pulled one third toward FV 35; the pull lifts when a second grade lands, even from the same source.

Weighting is EQUAL as of 2026-07-25. Accuracy weights (vintage-disciplined vote weights from each source's resolved track record, shrunk toward equal at k = 150, clamped [0.6, 1.5]) shipped in 2026-06 and were reverted on a hardened re-measurement: the equal-vs-weighted gap was smaller than the Spearman and AUC floors the test can resolve, so the A/B ships nothing (figures in data/consensus_weight_eval.json, ship = False). Only two of eight outlets have resolvable outcome history, and their precisions are indistinguishable, so every source votes 1.0 and data/source_weights.json carries an empty map. The draft board is equal-weight for the same reason. Disagreement metrics were never weighted.

Against its best single input the blend separates future contributors better (the AUC leg clears its floor) while the ordering gap (Spearman) sits inside the noise floor: discrimination, not ordering. The live legs, deltas and floors render in the Source Comparison view, read at render time from data/source_backtest.json (accuracy.consensus_vs_inputs).
entries.formula:
consensus FV = ceil( mean(scale-normalized latest explicit FV from each tracked source) ), clamped 20-80
single-source case: shrunk = (n_obs · src_FV + k · prior_FV) / (n_obs + k)
entries.example: A prospect graded 60, 62 and 65 lands at a normalized consensus of about 62; when the spread stretches, the Wide Spread mark shows it. A consensus outside the range of the printed grades is explained under Normalized source grade.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Trailing-window FV trajectory; direction and delta since the player's prior snapshot.
entries.methodology: Latest consensus_fv_raw against the prior point in the player's history. ▲ up by ≥1.5 FV, ▼ down by ≥1.5, - flat. Shows on list rows and as a stock chip in the detail header.
entries.formula:
stock = consensus_fv_raw(latest) − consensus_fv_raw(prior snapshot)
▲ if ≥ +1.5 · ▼ if ≤ −1.5 · "-" otherwise
entries.example: A consensus move from 48 to 50 shows ▲ +2; 48 to 47.5 stays flat (under the 1.5-point gate).
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Rank of the 30 MLB farm systems by the grade-tree composite: Value 65% · MLB Production 18% · Development 9% · Acquisition 8% (see Farm grade tree).
entries.methodology: The overall rank and letter come from the tree composite farm_score. The four older component scores still ship with per-component ranks and letters, each rescaled 0-100 across the 30 orgs: top-end (tiered FV points of the top 5 prospects; FV 80 = 250 points, FV 70 = 120), depth (the same for prospects 6-25), trajectory (smoothed FV change) and graduation pipeline (FV-weighted debuts in the trailing 12 months).
entries.formula:
farm_score = 0.65·Value + 0.18·MLB_Production + 0.09·Development + 0.08·Acquisition (see Farm grade tree)
component scores (report-card letters): top_end, depth, trajectory, grad_pipeline, each 0-100 across the 30 orgs
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Estimated MLB arrival year. Derived from level, age vs level mean, and FV grade adjustments.
entries.methodology: Starts from the current-level baseline (AAA ≈ 0.8 years to MLB, AA ≈ 1.5, A+ ≈ 2.5) and adds adjustments for performance (RPS+ vs level), age vs level, FV grade and IL / health flags. Confidence (high / mid / low) reflects the spread between the components.
entries.formula:
years_to_MLB = level_base + perf_adj + age_adj + fv_adj + health_adj
ETA year = current season + ceil(years_to_MLB, by season phase)
entries.example: Ryan Sloan (SEA, AA): base 1.35 years, +0.5 performance, −1.15 age-vs-level (young for AA), −0.25 FV leaves about 0.45 years: ETA 2027, high confidence. Every term shows in the ETA tooltip.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: FV-toward-35 pull applied when a prospect has only one published grade in their entire history.
entries.methodology: k = 0.5 shrinkage: consensus = (2/3 · raw FV) + (1/3 · 35). The badge for single-instance prospects gets a dashed amber outline and a small '1'. A FanGraphs-only prospect graded several times across snapshots is well observed and is not shrunk; only true single observations are.
entries.formula: if total_fv_instances ≤ 1: pulled_fv = (2/3) · raw_fv + (1/3) · 35
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Purple 'W' mark on the FV badge; sources disagree by ≥10 grade points (a two-tier gap).
entries.methodology: When 2+ sources have graded the player and their max-min spread is ≥10 points (e.g. FG 45, Pipeline 55), the FV badge carries a violet 'W'. Hover for the spread and source count. The consensus is averaging views that disagree.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: $M of MLB value above salary. Two kinds: PROJECTED (prospects, FV-derived) and REALIZED (debuted players, from actual WAR). Coloured on the value ruler at $100M / $50M / $20M / $5M / $1M, with red under zero.
entries.methodology:
Two measurements, one per side of the debut, kept separate:
• **Projected** (prospects): FV → projected WAR → projected $ through the value framework (Sur+), continuous in FV.
• **Realized** (debuted / MLB players): actual career WAR × $/WAR_overall ($11.74M, rolling 2024-2026) minus actual or estimated salary paid. Positive means the team beat the bet the grade implied.
Never mixed in one $/FV ratio (veterans have no FV anchor). The Transactions Trade Audit uses neither: it prices every party at today's Trade Machine trade value.

Pricing: production prices through the clemens_2026 valuation set (Ben Clemens' 2026 FanGraphs framework, tier values checksummed at load). The fa_implied re-anchor to the FA signings-implied series (data/fa_dpw_series.json) exists in the engine and is disabled under this set, so that series cannot move a prospect price. Each control season discounts at the net 7% rate: a 10% discount rate minus 3% annual win-cost growth, folded into one factor.

Calibration (v6 EV frame, isotonic-real-v6-evframe-2026-07-31): the published surplus is an expected value. The mixture's raw expectation is corrected by a count-weighted isotonic (PAVA) map fit on equal-count bin means of what 2017-2019 listed prospects returned over their control years (n = 2,236 resolved, today-priced targets), targeting the conditional mean because the trade engine consumes surplus as a price. The $0 floor on bottom-tier prospects is gone, and the map gives back the earlier median-objective MAE win; that loss is recorded in the fit provenance. Backtests re-fit against the raw layer.

For a debuted player the salary leg is the salary path (contract, league minimum, projected arbitration award). For a never debuted prospect it is the clemens_2026 service ladder. The two are kept separate on purpose: a prospect has no prior salary for the award model to raise off.
entries.formula:
projected (pre-debut): FV -> career-path outcome mixture -> SUM_t PV(tiered value of WAR_t - control-year salary), priced through the active valuation set (clemens_2026), each season escalated and discounted; the raw expectation then passes the count-weighted isotonic calibration map (v6 EV frame)
realized (post-debut): actual career WAR (eWAR basis) x $/WAR_overall - actual or estimated salaries paid
the two are never mixed into one $/FV ratio
entries.example: A FV 50 prospect's projected surplus is the calibrated expectation of the whole outcome mixture, bust paths included (a 52.3 prices above a 50.0). A graduated FV 50 who banked 12 WAR on $20M of salary shows a realized surplus near 12 × $11.74M − $20M = $121M.

entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.
entries.definition: The year by year salary a club controls a player at: contracted dollars where a contract exists, the league minimum for pre arbitration seasons, and the arbitration model's projected award for each arbitration year. Surplus is production value minus this path.
entries.methodology:
One path per player, read by the projections board, the player card and the Trade Machine, so the same player costs the same on every surface. Precedence per season: a guaranteed salary always wins; then the arbitration board's projected step; then the remaining arbitration years implied by the last class token on the board, chained through the same raise estimator the board serves. A season past the end of club control carries no price. Pre arbitration seasons are a CBA rule, not a prediction; arbitration seasons are a projection and are drawn with a dashed border.

The club's non tender option is priced on arbitration seasons only: if carrying a player for the rest of his arbitration years would cost more than he is worth, the club walks away at the last year that is still worth carrying, and the seasons after it read not tendered. That floor is applied on the expected projection path, which makes the published number a lower bound on the option's worth. A guaranteed contract has no such option, so a signed season can and does carry a negative surplus.

The salary band shown beside the surplus re prices the same WAR path at the two ends of the board's own award band. It is kept separate from the WAR band on purpose: the two errors move together, nothing here estimates how much, and the award band is not a calibrated interval. Measured, the salary band is about 1.9% of the WAR band at the median.

One rule overrides the board's own step: an arbitration award may not cut a player's salary by more than 20 percent (CBA Article VI). The board chains each award off the salary its arbitration panel knows about and cannot see an extension that pays more, so where the season before an arbitration year is a contracted one, the projected award is floored at 80 percent of the money the club is actually paying. That is a rule, not a prediction, and it is the only place this path departs from the number /arbitration/ publishes.
entries.caveat: Arbitration steps past 2026 assume the 2022 CBA structure survives; it expires 2026-12-01 and no interval covers that. Super Two cutoffs are unverified, and on most rows the class token is inferred rather than read from published service time. Where the board's grid ends on a pre arbitration season, or where no season of the window carries a salary to raise from, the club control window is not established and the path is short; the row says so, and the board prints the year it does know as a floor rather than naming an end. Player opt outs inside a signed deal are shown but not priced, and the options file they come from is a hand kept supplement of six players, not a league wide inventory: a club option folded into a contract's yearly salaries is priced here as guaranteed money. The arbitration steps themselves sit below the awards the system has actually handed out, by about 1.3x at the median rung and with no star tail at all, which makes surplus on the best players too high rather than too low.

entries.definition: The seasons a club holds a player's rights: his guaranteed contract seasons, then his remaining pre arbitration seasons at the CBA league minimum, then his arbitration seasons at the projected award. It ends with his first free agency season.
entries.methodology:
"Guaranteed through 2026" and "club control through 2030" are two different facts about the same player, and the board shows both: the guarantee is a signed deal and sits on the sub line, the seasons after it are projections and are drawn with a dashed border. The window is derived once, from the salary path, and copied into every payload, so the projections board, the player card and the Trade Machine cannot disagree about which season a club holds a player through.

Club control is a RIGHT and not a commitment. Where the model projects the club declines to tender him, the window still runs to the last controlled season and the SURPLUS stops at the cut; the tooltip on those rows says so.

Where the published arbitration grid ends on a pre arbitration season the first arbitration season is unknown, so the board says "through at least 2028" and prints the year with a trailing plus rather than naming an end it cannot derive. Those rows are also the ones whose later seasons carry no price at all.

Distinct from the 7-season valuation window used for prospect and eFV surplus, which starts at a projected ETA and prices a fixed ladder rather than a known one.
entries.caveat: A contract running past the five season projection horizon reads short here, because nothing past the horizon is priced: the window shown is the last season this platform prices, and for those rows it is the guarantee year that is the longer fact. A player option or an opt out inside a guaranteed deal can end the window EARLY, so on those rows the window shown is an upper bound: the option seasons are drawn on the salary path strip and named on the Trade Machine strip, and nothing here prices the choice. /arbitration/ publishes the ladder Spotrac lists and states no control end at all.

entries.definition: Average Annual Value. Total contract value divided by years.
entries.methodology: For deferral-heavy deals (Ohtani's $700M / 10 years is about $46M of present-value AAV) the displayed AAV is present-value adjusted, not raw money divided by years.

entries.definition: Per-team amateur signing budget. Separate IFA pool and draft pool ceilings per year.
entries.methodology: Draft pool = the sum of the team's slot values in rounds 1-10. IFA pool = the MLB-assigned international budget (base ~$5.95M plus competitive-balance additions). Teams can exceed the draft pool by up to 5% before pick penalties.

entries.definition: MLB-assigned bonus value for an individual draft pick. Sums into the team's draft pool ceiling.
entries.methodology: Every pick in rounds 1-10 has a published slot value. A team can pay over slot on one pick by signing under slot on others, inside the pool. Exceeding the pool total triggers a tax and, past 5%, future-pick penalties.
entries.formula:
team draft pool = SUM slot values over the team's picks in rounds 1-10
bonuses may cross slot per pick as long as the total stays inside the pool; total bonuses over the pool trigger a tax and, past that, future-pick penalties
entries.example: A club holding picks 11, 48 and 83 at slots of roughly $5.9M, $1.7M and $0.8M can pay pick 11 $7M by signing under slot later, as long as total bonuses stay inside the pool.

entries.definition: Major League Baseball: the top level and the target of every prospect projection.
Triple-A. The last level before MLB; many AAA prospects are MLB call-up candidates.
