entries.methodology: International League and Pacific Coast League. Average age ~26. Many AAA players are veterans; young AAA performers (≤24) are usually near-term MLB candidates.

entries.definition: Double-A. The hardest development jump; prospect projections start to get tested.
entries.methodology: Texas, Eastern and Southern Leagues. Average age ~23. Pitching quality and breaking-ball usage start to resemble MLB. Prospects who succeed at AA usually carry it forward.

entries.definition: High-A. The second full-season level above Single-A.
entries.methodology: Average age ~22. Many college draftees start here; high school draftees usually arrive after a year of A-ball.

entries.definition: Low-A / Single-A. The first full-season level.
entries.methodology: Average age ~21. The first 130+ game season after the complex or DSL.

entries.definition: Complex League. Short-season rookie ball at the team's spring-training complex.
entries.methodology: Average age ~19. Most high school draftees and recent IFAs get their first stateside reps here.

entries.definition: Dominican Summer League: the entry point for most international amateur signings. Players are 16-19.
entries.methodology: Affiliated rookie ball in the Dominican Republic; average age ~18, mostly Dominican, Venezuelan and Colombian signees. Every org runs at least one DSL team. The usual international ladder is DSL → complex league (CPX) → A-ball.

entries.definition: International Free Agent. Amateur players signed from outside the U.S., Canada, and Puerto Rico.
entries.methodology: Each org has a fixed annual IFA bonus pool. Latin American players sign at 16 (mostly the Dominican Republic and Venezuela); Asian professionals post from NPB and KBO; Cuban players sign under their own age and service rules. Top amateur bonuses run $3-5M.

entries.definition: Player is recovering from Tommy John (UCL replacement) elbow surgery. ~14-18 month recovery typical.
entries.methodology: Tommy John (ulnar collateral ligament reconstruction) is the most common pitching surgery. Typical timeline: throwing at 0-6 months, mound work at 6-12, rehab assignments at 12-14, MLB return at 14-18. Roughly 80% of recipients return to prior form within 2 years; ~10% never pitch at the same level again.

entries.definition: Player is on the Injured List. Types: 7-day (concussion), 10-day, 15-day (pitchers), 60-day.
entries.methodology: The 60-day IL frees the player's 40-man slot. The site shows every IL stint in the trailing 12 months; the Health profile totals the count and IL days.

entries.definition: 20-80 scouting grade for a pitcher's fastball - velocity, movement, shape, and command of the pitch.
entries.methodology: Usually the headline tool. 60+ is plus (mid-90s with ride or sink); 70+ is plus-plus (upper 90s with carry). The grade combines velocity, vertical and horizontal break and command of the pitch; velocity without shape rarely grades above 55.

entries.definition: 20-80 grade for the pitcher's slider (or sweeper variant) - sharpness, depth, tunneling with the fastball.
entries.methodology: Sliders sit ~5-10 mph below the fastball; sweepers add ~15-18 inches of horizontal break. Both use the 'sl' slot here because their roles overlap. 60+ is an out-pitch slider; 50 is average MLB shape.

entries.definition: 20-80 grade for the curveball - depth, shape, and command of the slowest breaking pitch.
entries.methodology: Slower than a slider (8-12 mph below the fastball against 5-10) with mostly vertical break. Spike, knuckle and standard grips all map to 'cb'. 60+ curveballs usually pair with an over-the-top arm slot.

entries.definition: 20-80 grade for the changeup (or splitter) - velo separation, arm-action deception, and command.
entries.methodology: Changeups sit 8-12 mph below the fastball with sink and fade; splitters sit in the same band with harder tumble. Different grip, same role; both use the 'ch' slot. A 60+ changeup is a starter's weapon against opposite-handed hitters.

entries.definition: 20-80 grade for locating pitches within the strike zone, not just throwing strikes.
entries.methodology: Control is throwing strikes; command is throwing the right strike. Plus command (60+) means consistently hitting the corner with the fastball and burying the breaking ball. Most prospects sit 45-50; a 60 command grade raises the ceiling sharply.

entries.definition: 20-80 grade for the cutter - a hybrid between FB and slider with late horizontal break, ~3-5 mph below the FB.
entries.methodology: FanGraphs and Pipeline do not always grade the cutter separately; Just Baseball does. 'ct' is a canonical key so JB-graded cutters enter the consensus when published. Fastball-like role with late glove-side cut.

entries.definition: 20-80 grade for a hitter's swing decisions and pitch recognition - chase / contact rate / zone awareness.
entries.methodology: Separate from the hit tool (bat-to-ball). 60+ pitch selection means low chase, high zone contact and walks. FanGraphs publishes it as its own grade; Just Baseball calls it 'Plate Disc.'. Feeds the offensive composite with Hit and Game Power.

entries.definition: 20-80 grade for barrel control - the ability to manipulate the bat in-zone, foul off tough pitches, square balls up.
entries.methodology: Part of the broader hit tool: swing path, bat-head awareness and two-strike adjustment. The difference between a plus hitter who barrels everything (60+) and a .280 hitter who often misses the barrel (50).

entries.definition: MLB's December draft of minor leaguers left unprotected by their org. Selecting team must keep the player on its MLB 26-man all season or offer them back.
entries.methodology: Held at the Winter Meetings in December. A player signed at 18 or younger must be added to the 40-man within 5 seasons, and at 19 or older within 4, or he is exposed; the protection deadline is in November. A selection costs $100K; returning the player costs the selecting team $50K.

entries.definition: The annual July amateur player draft - 20 rounds, picks from US/Canada/Puerto Rico HS and college. Distinct from the Rule 5 (Dec) draft.
entries.methodology: Each team's bonus pool is the sum of its slot values. Exceeding the pool by more than 5% costs future picks. International amateurs (DSL, Latin America) do not enter the Rule 4 draft; they sign as IFAs.

entries.definition: The 40 players a team can call up to MLB without exposing to other clubs. Drives Rule 5 protection deadlines.
entries.methodology: The active 26-man plus players on the 10- and 15-day IL plus minor leaguers added for Rule 5 protection. The 60-day IL frees a slot. Teams trim to 40 every November; DFAs and trades follow.

entries.definition: Each 40-man player has 3 (sometimes 4) option years allowing free MLB↔AAA shuttle. After they're used, the player must clear waivers to be sent down.
entries.methodology: An option is used in any season a player on the 40-man spends 20+ days optioned to the minors. Three such seasons exhaust them. An out-of-options player must clear waivers to go down.

entries.definition: MLB days accrued on the active roster or IL. 172 days = 1 'year' of service. 3 yrs → arbitration; 6 yrs → free agency.
entries.methodology: The main driver of a player's contract economics. Teams have held top rookies in AAA for two to three weeks to gain a year of control. Super Two: the top ~22% of players with 2-3 years of service reach arbitration a year early.

entries.definition: Salary process for players with 3-6 yrs of MLB service. Player + team file binding numbers; an arbitrator picks one if they don't settle.
entries.methodology:
Hearings are in February. The arbitrator picks one side's figure; there is no splitting. Most cases settle before a hearing. Salaries rise each arbitration year (roughly $1M in year one to ~$8M in year three for stars). Super Twos get a fourth arbitration year.

A club can decline to tender an arbitration eligible player, which ends its control. Surplus prices that option on arbitration seasons.

entries.definition: Service-time window from 0 to ~3 yrs MLB time. Player is paid at or near the league minimum with no salary leverage.
entries.methodology: Most graduates spend their first 2-3 MLB years here. The club sets salary unilaterally, subject to the league minimum. The 2022 CBA added a pre-arbitration bonus pool for top performers; it does not change the unilateral structure. At 3.000 years of service (or Super Two) the player enters arbitration.

entries.definition: Players in the top 22% of 2-3 service-year players get a 4th arbitration year. Costs the team an extra arb cycle.
entries.methodology: After each season, MLB ranks players with 2.000-3.000 years of service; the top 22% by service days become arbitration-eligible a year early. Teams manage call-up dates to keep top prospects under the cutoff, usually fewer than ~125 active days in the first MLB season.

entries.definition: Strategic delay of a top prospect's MLB debut to gain an extra year of team control. Less common post-2022 CBA but not eliminated.
entries.methodology: A prospect held in AAA for the first ~3 weeks of the season cannot reach 172 days of service that year, which delays free agency by a year. The 2022 CBA added Prospect Promotion Incentive picks: a club earns a draft pick when a top-100 prospect it carried for a full rookie season wins Rookie of the Year or finishes top three in MVP or Cy Young voting before arbitration, and a top-two Rookie of the Year finish earns the player a full year of service. Known cases: Kris Bryant (2015, grievance lost), Vladimir Guerrero Jr. (2019).

entries.definition: Players with 6+ years of MLB service may sign with any club once the World Series ends; the first five days are an exclusive-negotiation window with the incumbent club and the qualifying-offer period.
entries.methodology: Major-league free agency requires 6.000 years of service. The five days after the World Series are exclusive to the prior team; then the player is open to all 30 clubs. Minor-league free agency is separate: minor leaguers become free agents after their sixth professional season unless on a 40-man roster.

entries.definition: A one-year offer a club may make its departing free agent at the mean of MLB's top-125 salaries (~$21M in 2024). If he declines and signs elsewhere, the signing club forfeits draft picks and the former club gains a compensation pick.
entries.methodology: Allowed only for free agents who spent the whole prior season with the club and have never received one. Nearly every player declines. Mid-season trade acquisitions are not QO-eligible.

entries.definition: Extra draft picks awarded for QO-declined free agents, Prospect Promotion Incentive (PPI), and revenue-sharing balance.
entries.methodology: Two main sources. (1) QO compensation: a club losing a QO'd free agent gets a pick after round 1 (small markets) or later (depending on revenue and luxury-tax status); the signing club forfeits a pick. (2) Prospect Promotion Incentive: a pick after round 1 when a qualifying top prospect wins Rookie of the Year or finishes top three in MVP or Cy Young voting. The Competitive Balance Lottery also awards picks in Rounds A and B to lower-revenue clubs.

entries.definition: After a DFA: the player clears waivers and is removed from the 40-man roster to the minors. He can refuse with 3+ years of service.
entries.methodology: After a DFA the team has 7 days. If no club claims the player, he can be outrighted to the minors. He loses 40-man protection. A player with 3+ years of service or a prior outright can refuse and elect free agency.

entries.definition: Removal from the 40-man roster; the team has 7 days to trade, waive or release the player.
entries.methodology: Outcomes: outright to the minors (refusable at 3+ years of service), waiver claim, trade or release. Most DFA'd players clear waivers and accept the outright.

entries.definition: First MLB appearance. Under the debut rule, a set mlbDebutDate moves a prospect to the Debuted tab.
entries.methodology: Debuts carry a ★ chip in the transaction history. A debut removes the player from the active prospect lists and moves him to the Debuted tab, where his grade is measured against MLB results (see WAG).

entries.definition: Lump-sum payment at signing for amateur players. Draftees pull from the team's draft pool; IFAs from the IFA pool.
entries.methodology: MLB publishes draft slot values each year. Teams can exceed the pool by up to 5% with a tax; beyond that costs future first-round picks. IFA bonuses are hard-capped at the assigned pool (~$5.95M base plus competitive-balance additions) with no overage since 2017.

entries.definition: Three IL durations: 10-day (position players), 15-day (the minimum for pitchers and two-way players, post-2022), and 60-day, which also frees the player's 40-man roster spot.
entries.methodology: A 15-day stint can be transferred to the 60-day IL, which removes the player from the 40-man count. The concussion IL is a separate 7-day list.

entries.definition: Official MLB designation: 20+ MLB innings pitched AND 20+ MLB games started as a position player or DH with at least 3 plate appearances in each. Qualifying exempts the player from the pitcher-usage rules that bar position players from pitching in competitive games.
entries.methodology: Shohei Ohtani is the standard case. The site detects a two-way profile when a prospect carries both hitter (hit, game_pwr, ...) and pitcher (fb, sl, ...) tool grades, and renders both Tools cards.

entries.definition: Scouting grades come in pairs: present grade (what they show today) and future grade (projected peak). FG ships them as 'Hit 30/55' = present 30, future 55.
entries.methodology: The FUTURE grade is stored as the tool number (the projection is what the site uses). Present grades ride in _extras['present'] for sources that publish both. The present-future gap encodes development runway and risk.

entries.definition: Rookie-level stateside ball played at team training complexes (Arizona or Florida). Mostly recent draftees + DSL graduates.
entries.methodology: Two leagues: Arizona Complex League (ACL, ex-AZL) and Florida Complex League (FCL, ex-GCL). Games at team backfields, no fans. Players 17-20. The 2021 minor-league reorganization consolidated the older rookie leagues into these two.

entries.definition: Green ▲ = consensus FV rose since the last update; red ▼ = fell. Magnitude is the FV-delta.
entries.methodology: The consensus-FV change since the prior update; a player with one update reads flat. Drives the Up / Down filter on the Active list; moves ≥ 1.5 show in the row meta line.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Color-coded chip showing the player's consensus Future Value. Red = elite (70+), orange = high (60-65), yellow = mid (50-55), grey = lower (40-45).
entries.visual: 70605045
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Animated border on player headshots and cards, keyed to FV. FV 40 and below gets no treatment; each tier above adds foil, chrome or holo.
entries.methodology:
Five tiers above the FV 40 baseline, modeled on Topps Chrome refractors (holo ranks above chrome):
 • FV 70+ → LEGENDARY · animated rainbow with a pulsing glow (top ~1%)
 • FV 61-69 → HOLO · full rainbow shift
 • FV 55-60 → CHROME · silver shimmer
 • FV 50-54 → FOIL · faint silver foil
 • FV 45-49 → SHINE · static gold ring
 • FV 40 and below → no treatment
Applied wherever a headshot or card renders: list rows, spotlight cards, the prospect header, compare view.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Row pill for the Tool composite on the 20-80 scale: green ≥60 (plus), neutral ≥50, amber ≥40, red <40.
entries.visual: Tool 65Tool 52Tool 45Tool 38
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Row pill for RPS+: level-relative performance against same-age prospects at the same level (100 = cohort mean). See RPS+.
entries.visual: RPS+ 125RPS+ 100RPS+ 78
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Violet 'W' in the bottom-right corner of an FV badge - at least two FV-publishing sources disagree by ≥10 grade-points on the latest update.
entries.methodology: A violet circle with a white 'W' plus a violet right edge on the FV badge. Hover for the spread and source count.
entries.visual: 60W→ violet W + violet right edge
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Amber '1' in the top-left corner of an FV badge - only one source has ever published an explicit FV for this player. Consensus is Bayesian-shrunk.
entries.methodology: An amber circle with a white '1' plus an amber left edge on the FV badge. The player is pulled toward FV 35 (k = 0.5) until a second source grades him.
entries.formula:
adjusted FV = w x raw + (1 - w) x 35, w = 1 / (1 + K), K = 0.5, so w = 2/3
fires only when exactly one source has ever published an explicit FV; multi-source consensus is untouched (w = 1)
entries.example: A lone FV 50 report serves 2/3 x 50 + 1/3 x 35 = 45 until a second source confirms; a lone 65 serves 55.
entries.visual: 551→ amber 1 + amber left edge
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Amber chip when a player is currently on the IL. Tooltip shows IL type + days elapsed + transaction description.

entries.definition: Violet chip when the player is within ~18 months of Tommy John surgery. ETA pads automatically for the recovery window.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Cyan pill in the 'Source-by-source tool history' dropdown marking the row that feeds the Tool composite. One per source.
entries.methodology: Tool uses each source's most recent publication only (forward-fill picks the latest per source). Older rows are dimmed and do not count toward the consensus.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Amber pill on the per-source history header when a source's latest publication is >365 days old.
entries.methodology: A stale source still counts in the consensus (its last grade stands until refreshed); the pill marks the input as aging. Sources go stale when an outlet stops covering a prospect.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Above-cohort signal on a tool or rate stat - e.g., 60+ hit tool, top-decile K%.
entries.methodology: Shows in the player flag strip (3 visible, more on hover) and the Flags section on the detail page. Computed from tool grades, rate stats vs level norms and composite indices.

entries.definition: Below-cohort signal flagged for concern - e.g., 30 hit tool, bottom-decile contact, chronic injury history.

entries.definition: Spotlight badge for prospects with top-decile recent stock movement - rising fast across multiple sources.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Spotlight badge for out-of-nowhere rises - sources just started covering a prospect not previously ranked.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Spotlight badge for sustained multi-update FV movement in one direction - the steady riser/decliner pattern.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Four-branch farm grade (v40). Composite = Value 65% (aggregate risk-adjusted surplus) · MLB Production 18% (raw graduate WAR) · Development 9% · Acquisition 8%.
entries.methodology:
The v40 tree grades primarily on aggregate value. The prior tree was a per-prospect tool-development index (Development 50%, surplus normalized per prospect), so a farm could rank 3rd in total surplus and grade 15th.

(1) Value: driven by AGGREGATE risk-adjusted controlled surplus, the total dollar value of the active prospect pool from the value framework, which already prices elite ceilings non-linearly. (2) MLB Production: raw realized graduate WAR (WAR per season, top-3 cumulative WAR, boom, bust, top grads, conviction, graduation pace, HOF track); Talent Translation (WAG) is shown and not graded. (3) Development (per-tool DvM+, health, Statcast quality) and (4) Acquisition are secondary.

At the v40 reweight, grade rank correlated +0.85 with total-surplus rank (was +0.38); orgs grading above their surplus rank lead in realized graduate WAR (e.g. ATL #1), orgs below are near last.

Letters: A+ is #1, A the top 7%, F the bottom ~3%. Every leaf is z-scored across the 30 orgs; sparse leaves show ' - '. The Farm tiebreaker orders farms that share a letter.
entries.formula:
farm_score = 0.65·Value + 0.18·MLB_Production + 0.09·Development + 0.08·Acquisition
  Value          = wmean(Aggregate_active_surplus[0.68], Org_$DvM+, Grad_contract_surplus, WAR_per_$M, Draft_pool_eff, IFA_ROI)
  MLB_Production  = mean(Hitter_WAR/yr+Top3, Pitcher_WAR/yr+Top3, Boom%, -Bust%, Top3_WAR/yr, Conviction, Grad_pace, HOF_track)
  Development     = mean(Hitter_Tools_DvM+, Pitcher_Tools_DvM+, Health_Mgmt, Statcast_Quality)
  Acquisition     = mean(Draft, IFA-ROI, Trade, Waiver)
  tiebreaker = 100 + 10·z(0.40·z(total_surplus) + 0.25·z(7yDvM+) + 0.35·z(raw_graduate_WAR))
entries.example: A system graded A- with Value A, MLB Production B+, Development B and Acquisition B- is winning on aggregate surplus (the 65% branch) while its trade ledger lags; the Tendencies tab shows which acquisition channels drive the B-.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Continuous score that orders farms sharing a letter grade. 100 = league mean, +10 = one standard deviation.
entries.methodology: A z-blend across the 30 orgs: 0.40 total active surplus + 0.25 7yDvM+ (the principal window) + 0.35 raw graduate WAR, re-standardized by the blend's own spread and anchored 100 + 10z. Surplus and DvM+ are the dollar and indexed views of one controlled-value concept, so they share weight; raw graduate WAR adds realized MLB output. The weighted sum of z-scores has a spread of about 0.70, so without the re-standardization the score moved about 7 points per blend sigma; the division changes no org order. Shown under each letter with a component breakdown and a continuous 1-30 rank.
entries.formula:
blend = 0.40 x z(total active surplus) + 0.25 x z(7yDvM+) + 0.35 x z(raw graduate WAR), across the 30 orgs
tiebreaker = 100 + 10 x blend / sd(blend)
entries.example: Two B+ farms: one at +0.9 sd on the blend reads 109, the other at +0.1 reads 101. The letter ties; the tiebreaker orders them and the breakdown names the axis.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Outcome quality of how this org acquires prospects across all 4 channels: Draft, IFA, Trade, Waiver.
entries.methodology: Acquisition branch of the farm grade tree, 8% of farm_score (v40). Four equal leaves: (a) Draft: pick-slot-adjusted WAR (graduate WAR against the fitted first-six-season slot curve) blended 50/50 with Draft Ceiling Hits (recent draftees at FV ≥ 60 within 3 years). (b) IFA: WAG + WAR per season + cumulative WAR across IFA graduates. (c) Trade: net FV gained vs lost at trade dates + Trade WAR Delta. (d) Waiver: net FV from non-trade cross-org moves + Waiver Hit Rate. Each leaf is z-scored across orgs; sparse leaves show ' - '.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: How fast the org's prospects develop their tools against the league. 9% of the farm score (v40).
entries.methodology: Development branch of the farm grade tree, four leaves: (a) Hitter Tools DvM+ (mean of HitDvM+ / PowerDvM+ / SpeedDvM+ / FieldDvM+ / ArmDvM+ / PitchSelDvM+ / BatCtrlDvM+), (b) Pitcher Tools DvM+ (FB / SL / CB / CH / Cmd / Ct), (c) Health Management and (d) Statcast Quality (the org's aggregate SC+). DvM+ legs are 100-anchored (+10 = 1σ) and measure tool growth in the org regardless of starting grade: a 40 hit tool that grew to 55 over two cycles counts as development.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The org's aggregate risk-adjusted controlled value. The primary branch of the farm grade (v40: 65% of the composite), dominated by total active-pool surplus.
entries.methodology:
Value branch of the farm grade tree (the Financial branch reframed; 65% of farm_score in v40, up from 18%). A farm's grade should mainly reflect the total risk-adjusted value of its active prospect pool.

The dominant leaf (0.68) is AGGREGATE active surplus: the summed risk-adjusted, present-valued controlled surplus across the org's active prospects, which already prices elite ceilings non-linearly. Secondary leaves: Org $DvM+ (prospects appreciating against FV-tier peers), graduate contract surplus, WAR per $M, draft-pool efficiency, IFA ROI. The prior spec scored the surplus leaf per prospect, which kept high-total farms from grading up. 100-anchored (+10 = 1σ).
entries.formula: Value_score = wmean( aggregate_active_surplus[0.68], org_$DvM+[0.10], grad_contract_surplus[0.10], war_per_$M[0.04], draft_pool_eff[0.04], IFA_ROI[0.04] )
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Whether the org produces MLB players, especially top-end ones. 18% of the farm score (v40), eight equally weighted leaves.
entries.methodology:
(a) Hitter production: WAR per season plus top-3 hitter career WAR. (b) Pitcher production: the same for pitchers. (c) Boom Rate: share of settled graduates whose WAG label is boom, the 80th percentile or higher of the expectation at the eFV grade at debut. (d) Bust Rate: share at the 20th percentile or lower, entered negated. Settled = past the WAG gate, 200 PA or 80 IP measured; 5 settled minimum. (e) Top-3 graduate WAR per season. (f) Conviction: count of graduates at 3.0+ WAR per season or with a 3.5+ WAR season. (g) Grad Pace: FV 50+ graduations per year over 7 years. (h) HOF Track: graduates with a 5+ WAR season.

Talent Translation (mean WAG) is shown but not graded since v40.
entries.formula: Production_score = mean of the present leaves, each z-scored across orgs (100 = league mean): Hitter, Pitcher, Boom%, -Bust%, Top-3 WAR/season, Conviction, Grad Pace, HOF Track
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Share of an org's settled MLB graduates labelled boom: WAG at the 80th percentile or higher of the expectation at his eFV grade at debut.
entries.methodology: Leaf inside MLB Production. Each graduate carries the WAG label baked on his card (see WAG): unsettled until measured MLB exposure reaches 200 PA or 80 IP, then boom at percentile 0.80 or higher, bust at 0.20 or lower, settled between. Boom Rate = booms / settled graduates (boom, bust and settled); fewer than 5 shows ' - '. Pairs with Bust Rate (entered negated).
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Share of an org's settled MLB graduates labelled bust: WAG at the 20th percentile or lower of the expectation at his eFV grade at debut. Entered negated in MLB Production.
entries.methodology: Mirror of Boom Rate on the same gate (200 PA or 80 IP measured): bust = percentile 0.20 or lower. Bust Rate = busts / settled graduates; fewer than 5 settled shows ' - '. Higher bust share pulls the branch down.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Mean WAR/yr across the org's top-3 graduates by rate. Captures peak star-tier production without depth dilution.
entries.methodology: Leaf inside MLB Production. For each graduate past the boom/bust sample floor (2+ MLB WAR seasons, 800 PA or 200 IP), WAR per season (career WAR / MLB seasons); the leaf is the mean of the top 3. Fewer than 3 qualifying graduates shows ' - '. One Skenes plus two solid regulars (5.0, 2.5, 2.0 → 3.17) outscores ten average graduates (1.0).
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Star count: graduates the org developed with 3.0+ WAR per season, or any single season of 3.5+ WAR. A leaf of MLB Production.
entries.methodology: Counts graduates who clear EITHER career WAR per season ≥ 3.0 (a sustained above-average regular) OR a single-season WAR ≥ 3.5 (a peak year). The leaf scores the count; the tooltip names the top five by peak signal. The farm-score cap for orgs without a star was removed in v18; Conviction is one of the eight equal leaves.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: WAR per $M and FV per $M of draft-pool spend over the (T-5)..(T-2) draft window.
entries.methodology:
Draft Pool Efficiency leaf in the Value branch. Two signals on one denominator (pool dollars in T-5..T-2):
• **war_per_m_pool**: career WAR of graduates drafted in the window / pool $M. Lagging and realized. Gated at ≥3 graduates.
• **fv_per_m_pool**: current FV of still-active draftees from the window / pool $M. Moves within about 2 years of the draft.
Pool dollars come from MLB's published per-team draft pools (mlb_draft_pools). Together they cover slot-money discipline and late-round hits (WAR) and scouting and development speed (FV).
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Trailing-6yr-window WAR per $M of IFA bonus spend. Captures whether the org's international signings translated to MLB production.
entries.methodology: IFA ROI leaf in the Value branch. Numerator: career WAR of IFA graduates signed in (T-9)..(T-3), a 6-year window (IFA prospects take longer than draftees). Denominator: the org's total IFA bonus spend over the same signing years. Output: WAR per $M, gated at ≥2 graduates with a signing year and bonus on file. Splash signings show as high spend and low ROI; orgs that develop $200K-$500K signings show high ROI.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Capital-efficiency index for farm systems. 100 = league mean, +10 = 1σ.
entries.methodology: Org-level composite of WAR per $M and graduate contract surplus (current AAV − bonus amortized per year), each z-scored across the 30 orgs and anchored at 100. Same 100 + 10z dial as DvM+ and ToolDvM+. Feeds the Value branch. Not Sur+, the per-prospect surplus.
entries.formula: OrgSur+ = 100 + 10 · avg(z(WAR/$M), z(grad contract surplus))
entries.example: An org producing 0.8 graduate WAR per $M of bonus spend (one stddev above the mean) and league-average graduate contract surplus posts OrgSur+ around 105: capital-efficient on the draft side, ordinary on the development-to-contract side.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: % of recent (≤3yr) drafted actives at FV ≥ 60. Captures whether the org drafted high-ceiling talent, not just talent that beat the slot.
entries.methodology: One of two inputs to the Draft leaf (with pick-slot-adjusted WAR). Per org: drafted actives at current consensus FV ≥ 60 from the trailing 3 draft years, divided by all drafted actives from those years. Fewer than 3 drafted actives shows ' - '. Complements the retrospective, graduate-only slot-adjusted WAR with the upside already visible in recent classes.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Career WAR of acquired-in-trade graduates minus career WAR of traded-away graduates. Captures retrospective trade value.
entries.methodology: One of two inputs to the Trade leaf (with net FV at trade date). Per org: career WAR of every graduate acquired by trade minus career WAR of every graduate traded away. Positive means the org came out ahead on realized MLB production. Complements net FV, because the consensus at the trade date can lag or lead development.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: % of waiver-claimed prospects who reached MLB. Sparse-data signal - orgs with <3 claims grade ' - '.
entries.methodology: One of two inputs to the Waiver leaf (with net FV from non-trade cross-org moves). Per org: claimed-in prospects who reached MLB (career WAR on file) divided by all claimed-in prospects.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Cross-org player trade. The Acquisition branch of the farm grade rolls up net trade FV per org.
entries.methodology: Every trade involving a tracked prospect writes two fv_events: 'trade out' on the sending org and 'trade in' on the receiving org, each stamped with the prospect's consensus FV at the trade date. Per-org net = sum(fv_in) − sum(fv_out). A trade that was fair by later WAR can still register unevenly here, because trade-date FV can lag or lead development.

entries.definition: Non-trade cross-org acquisition. Counted in the Acquisition branch alongside trades.
entries.methodology: Waiver claims, Rule 5 selections and returns, contract purchases and free-agent signings. Each writes a non-trade fv_event with the prospect's most recent consensus FV (trades use FV at the trade date). The Waiver leaf sums these per org as net FV: claimed in minus released out.

entries.definition: Per-org mean WAG across graduates. Shown on the farm card; not in the farm grade since v40.
entries.methodology: WAG per graduate (see WAG): WAR per MLB season against the expectation at his eFV grade at debut (consensus FV where eFV abstains), reliability-weighted and shown once measured exposure reaches 200 PA or 80 IP. Per-org value = mean over graduates with a WAG; fewer than 3 show ' - '.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: WAR-per-million-dollars-spent across the org's graduates. Pure capital efficiency.
entries.methodology: Total career WAR from the org's graduates against total signing bonuses paid (draft + IFA). Higher = more value per dollar. Lagging: a recent class has not converted yet. Fewer than 3 graduates with both bonus and career WAR on file shows ' - '.
entries.formula: ROI = total_career_WAR / (total_bonus_USD / 1,000,000)
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Top-10 mean of composite_overall (the Tool composite) across an org's active prospects. Raw scouting quality, separate from FV consensus.
entries.methodology: Rank an org's actives by composite_overall (the 20-80 power mean behind Tool / O-Tool / D-Tool) and average the top 10, so a top-heavy farm is not diluted by ungraded depth. A system with 60 raw power grades above a 50-across-the-board system with the same FV consensus.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: IFA % × multi-year diversity. Rewards orgs with broad, steady international scouting.
entries.methodology: Magnitude (IFA share of actives) and diversity (distinct IFA signing years): score = 0.7 × ifa_pct + 0.3 × (year_span / 10, capped at 1.0). Rewards a steady international pipeline over draft-only systems.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Share of prospects flagged 'very young for level' minus 'very old for level'. Long runway vs peaking now.
entries.methodology: Per org: (very_young_count − very_old_count) / total_actives. Positive = many young-for-level prospects (long runway); negative = an old-for-level system peaking now. Uses the same age_vs_level tiers as the row chip.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Combined post-TJ share and trailing 12-month IL-days mean. Inverted: lower burden = better letter.
entries.methodology: The displayed health_burden keeps the legacy 100 × post_tj_pct + il_days_mean composite. The Health Management leaf that grades (v31.6) drops post-TJ (post-surgery outcomes often run above average, and TJ is not a hitter signal): it scores current IL% and average 12-month IL days, both inverted. Post-TJ pitcher counts ship as context and do not affect the grade.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Share of an org's tracked actives currently on the injured list (any type). Snapshot, not trailing window.
entries.methodology: il_current_count / active_count at export time, from the il_status table the per-player IL chip uses. Health Burden weights 12-month IL days; this counts who is down now. Shown on the Roster Snapshot tile, red at ≥10%.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Year-grouped view of MLB-signed overseas free agents (NPB / KBO / CPBL / etc.), with per-class rollups for total bonus, mean WAG, and mean WAR/yr.
entries.methodology: On the Overseas page's Signed sub-tab. Each signed prospect is grouped by posting_year (posted_date.year, else signed_date.year). Each year shows class totals (count, bonuses paid) plus mean WAG and mean WAR per season over signees with ≥1 full-season MLB sample, joined through milb_key to the graduate career payload. This WAG is the signing table's own residual against the survivor WAR per season at the grade, not the engine WAG the boom/bust pill and farm grade read.
entries.formula:
class = posting_year = posted_date.year, falling back to signed_date.year
per-class rollups: signee count, SUM bonuses, mean WAG and mean WAR/yr over signees with >= 1 full-season MLB sample (joined via milb_key to the graduate career payload)
entries.example: A class of 11 signees and $185M paid averages WAG and WAR per season only over the signees with a full MLB season on file; the rest sit out of both means.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Extra draft slots awarded to small-revenue clubs under the 2022 CBA. Round 1A (6 picks) lands after round 1; Round 1B (6 picks) lands after round 2.
entries.methodology: Eligible clubs are the smallest-revenue and smallest-market teams. Round 1A picks follow the first round; Round 1B picks follow the second. They are the only draft picks a team may trade. Tankathon's projection assigns them by current eligibility; the lottery view lists them at the bottom with a 1A / 1B label.

entries.definition: Post-All-Star-break snapshots subtract 0.25 years from the ETA - scaled by the org's historical H1/H2 promotion tendency (H2-heavy orgs get a stronger pull-in).
entries.methodology:
The All-Star break (fixed at July 15) splits the season into H1 and H2. By H2 a AAA prospect has used about half his AAA year, so the level baseline should shrink.

Post-break snapshots subtract 0.25 years. Org tendency scales it: each org's last 3 years of promotions are bucketed H1/H2. Orgs with h2_rate ≥ 60% get a stronger ×1.4 pull-in; orgs with h1_rate ≥ 70% get ×0.6.

H2-heavy orgs pre-break add +0.10 (less likely to debut before the break). Offseason snapshots (Nov-Feb) and balanced orgs (40-60 split) get no adjustment.

Shown as a 'Snapshot: post-All-Star break' eyebrow and an 'Org promotes X% H1 / Y% H2' line on the ETA panel. Code: eta.py (season_phase, HALF_SEASON_ADJ, _org_promotion_phase_weight).
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Per-level, per-side age threshold that keeps old-for-level prospects out of the Risers / Rebounders / Fallers buckets. Anchored on target baselines (A 21, A+ 22, AA 23, AAA 24, MLB 26).
entries.methodology:
Hitters are cut at ≥ +2.0 years over the level baseline; pitchers at ≥ +3.0 (later debuts are common). Target baselines, not empirical level means: the empirical AAA pool is pulled up by the journeymen the cap exists to filter.

At AAA (baseline 24) a 26.0+ hitter and a 27.0+ pitcher are cut. The cap runs inside _classify_movement in spotlights.py before bucket assignment (bucket = none).

Rookie levels (DSL / CPX / ROK) and missing age or level pass through. Spotlights only: no effect on the active list, farm rosters or leaderboards.
entries.formula:
cut when age >= level baseline + 2.0 (hitters) or + 3.0 (pitchers); baselines A 21, A+ 22, AA 23, AAA 24, MLB 26
fires inside _classify_movement BEFORE bucket assignment (bucket = none); rookie levels and missing age / level pass through
entries.example: A 26.0yo AAA hitter is cut (24 + 2.0); a AAA pitcher survives to 27.0. The cap touches the Spotlights buckets only, never the board, leaderboards or farm rosters.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: How hard a hitter strikes the ball, in mph off the bat. Higher = louder contact and more damage on balls in play.
entries.methodology: Mean batted-ball speed at contact. The fastest-stabilizing batted-ball signal (~40 batted balls), so it reads raw contact quality before results settle. Pairs with launch angle to define barrels. MLB average ~89 mph; 92+ plus; 95+ elite.
entries.example: A prospect averaging 92.5 mph sits about one standard deviation above the MLB mean.
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant): the speed of the ball off the bat.

entries.definition: Share of batted balls in the exit-velocity and launch-angle window that historically produces ≥ .500 AVG and ≥ 1.500 SLG.
entries.methodology: Barrels ÷ batted balls. Isolates loud, well-angled contact that drives extra-base power, excluding weak contact and hard mishits. League average ~8%; 12%+ plus; 16%+ elite.
entries.formula:
Barrel% = barrels / batted_balls × 100
barrel = (EV, launch angle) in the ≥.500 AVG / ≥1.500 SLG zone
entries.example: A 14% Barrel% over a full MiLB season profiles as plus game power even with an ordinary home-run total.
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant): a barrel is a batted ball whose exit velocity and launch angle historically produce elite results.

entries.definition: Share of batted balls hit ≥ 95 mph. A volume measure of quality contact - broader than Barrel% (no angle requirement).
entries.methodology: Batted balls at 95+ mph ÷ all batted balls. How often a hitter makes loud contact at any angle; Barrel% adds the angle requirement. League average ~40%; 45%+ plus. High Hard-Hit% with low Barrel% points to a launch-angle fix.
entries.formula: Hard-Hit% = batted_balls ≥ 95 mph / batted_balls × 100
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant): share of batted balls hit 95+ mph.

entries.definition: Share of pitches outside the strike zone that a hitter swings at. Lower = better plate discipline.
entries.methodology: Swings at out-of-zone pitches ÷ out-of-zone pitches. The core discipline input: low chase predicts walks and protects the hit tool. Stabilizes quickly and travels across levels. League average ~28-31%; under 25% is plus. The site defines the zone geometrically (a fixed rulebook rectangle), not by the called zone, so the metric is consistent across levels even though enforcement differs: MLB runs the ABS challenge system in 2026, AAA has used ABS since 2023, the Florida State League since 2022.
entries.formula: Chase% = out-of-zone swings / out-of-zone pitches × 100
entries.example: A 20-year-old at AA with a 22% Chase% has discipline that usually survives MLB sequencing.
entries.origin: Industry metric (O-Swing%). Plate-discipline rate from pitch tracking; the Statcast/Savant zone definition is used here.

entries.definition: Share of swings that miss. For hitters lower is better; for pitchers (induced whiff) higher is better.
entries.methodology: Swinging strikes ÷ swings. For hitters, bat-to-ball skill and strikeout risk; for pitchers, stuff. Per swing (K% is per plate appearance), so it stabilizes faster. Hitter average ~24%; 30%+ induced whiff on a pitcher's primary pitch is plus.
entries.formula: Whiff% = swinging strikes / swings × 100
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant): swinging strikes per swing.

entries.definition: Share of swings at in-zone pitches that make contact: the most direct bat-to-ball signal.
entries.methodology: In-zone contact ÷ in-zone swings. Limited to hittable pitches, so it isolates bat control from approach: the tracked complement to the Hit tool. League average ~85%; 90%+ plus.
entries.formula: Z-Contact% = in-zone contact / in-zone swings × 100
entries.origin: Industry metric. Plate-discipline rate popularized by FanGraphs (contact on in-zone swings).

entries.definition: Pitcher metric: share of pitches that are called strikes or whiffs. How often a pitch beats the hitter.
entries.methodology: (Called strikes + swinging strikes) ÷ pitches. Combines stuff (whiffs) and command (called strikes); stabilizes faster than K% because every pitch counts. League average ~28%; 30%+ strong; 32%+ elite. Under the 2026 MLB ABS challenge system (AAA since 2023, FSL since 2022) borderline calls are correctable, so the called-strike half is not strictly comparable to a human-umpire baseline.
entries.formula: CSW% = (called strikes + whiffs) / pitches × 100
entries.origin: Industry metric. Called Strikes plus Whiffs, popularized by Alex Fast at Pitcher List.

entries.definition: Revolutions per minute on a pitch. Drives movement - high fastball spin → ride; high breaking-ball spin → sharper break.
entries.methodology: On four-seamers, high active spin produces ride that beats hitters up in the zone; on breaking balls, tighter and later break. Spin matters through the movement it creates (efficiency and axis), so it is a stuff-model input, not a grade. Typical four-seam spin ~2,250 rpm; 2,500+ is high.
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant), measured by Hawk-Eye tracking.

entries.definition: How far in front of the rubber a pitcher releases the ball (feet). More extension = less reaction time = effective velocity above the radar reading.
entries.methodology: Distance from the rubber to the release point. More extension shortens the ball's travel and adds effective velocity: a 95 mph fastball at 7.0 ft plays like ~96-97. League average ~6.3 ft; 7.0+ is a meaningful add.
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant): how far off the rubber the ball is released.

entries.definition: Top running speed in feet per second on a player's fastest competitive runs. The tracked-data version of the Run tool.
entries.methodology: Feet per second over a player's fastest one-second window on qualified runs. The tracked complement to the Run grade; feeds range and baserunning. League average ~27 ft/s; 28+ plus; 30+ elite (70-80 run).
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant): feet per second in a runner's fastest one-second window.

entries.definition: Strikeout rate minus walk rate: one peripheral-skill number per pitcher.
entries.methodology: K% − BB%, both per batter faced. Captures the two outcomes a pitcher controls most and tracks run prevention better than K/9 or BB/9 because it is per batter, not per inning. League-average starters ~13-14%; 18%+ plus; 22%+ elite.
entries.formula: K-BB% = K% − BB%
entries.example: A starter at 30% K% and 7% BB% posts 23% K-BB%.
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: Level-anchored offensive index for a MiLB season: 100 is the league average for that level and season. Computed as wRC+ vs level since 2026-07-31 (the key keeps the OPS+ name): a linear-weight wOBA against a plate-appearance-weighted pool of the whole league, not an OPS ratio against the prospects the site tracks.
entries.methodology: One set of FanGraphs-shape linear weights, rescaled inside each level-season so the pool's mean wOBA equals its OBP, then indexed against that pool and shrunk toward it by plate appearances (K = 200 PA, the retired chip's shrink strength). The baseline change mattered as much as the metric: the old tracked-prospect baseline ran 7-8 percent low at Double-A and High-A (.703 against a true .752, .708 against .767), which flattered every hitter at those levels. Across 1,972 served hitters the new chip sits about 2 points lower on the median, slightly tighter, and 8.5 percent of pairs swap order. Coverage 100 percent, from the MLB StatsAPI response the site already fetches. No park adjustment.
entries.formula:
wRC+ vs level = 100 × wOBA_adj / lg_wOBA, where wOBA_adj = (PA·wOBA + K·lg_wOBA)/(PA + K), K = 200 PA; weights rescaled per level-season so pool wOBA = pool OBP
retired chip (still computed, not displayed): OPS+ = 100 × OPS_adj / lgOPS, OPS_adj = (AB·OPS + 170·lgOPS)/(AB + 170)
entries.origin: Industry metric. OPS+ in the Bill James tradition (Baseball-Reference implements the league version). Here it is computed relative to the player's minor-league level and carries no park adjustment.

entries.definition: Career WAR an org's graduates produced per $1M of signing bonuses. The main capital-efficiency leaf of the Value branch.
entries.methodology: Total career WAR of an org's graduates ÷ total signing bonuses (draft + IFA), in $M. Did the money turn into MLB production? Lagging (WAR accrues after the debut), so it needs ≥3 graduates with both bonus and career WAR on file. Anchored across the 30 orgs into the Value branch.
entries.formula: WAR per $M = Σ career_WAR(grads) / (Σ signing_bonus_USD / 1,000,000)
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Per-year dollar surplus on an org's graduates: current AAV minus the signing bonus amortized over a fixed six years.
entries.methodology: For each graduate with Spotrac contract data and a signing bonus on file: surplus per year = current AAV − (signing bonus ÷ 6). The divisor is a fixed 6 in this leaf: it is a bonus amortization, not the valuation set's 7-season valuation window and not the club control window the MLB Projections board prices. Averaged across qualifying graduates and z-anchored into the Value branch.
entries.formula: per-year surplus = current_AAV − (signing_bonus / 6)
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The org-level roll-up of its active prospects' $DvM+ - development of surplus dollars, indexed to 100 = league mean.
entries.methodology: Mean of the $DvM+ of an org's active prospects (development-vs-mean on projected surplus dollars rather than FV), 100-anchored. Credits systems growing the dollar value of the talent they hold. Feeds the Value branch beside WAR per $M and contract surplus.
entries.formula:
Org $DvM+ = mean of the org's active prospects' per-prospect $DvM+ (surplus-dollar development vs the FV-tier mean), 100 = league mean
feeds the Value branch as the fin_dollar_dvm leaf
entries.example: An org whose actives average $DvM+ 108 reads Org $DvM+ 108: the dollar value of its talent is rising faster than tier-mean development.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Travel the consensus board to any past monthly snapshot, or diff two dates for a changelog of risers, fallers, new entries, graduates, and grade changes.
entries.methodology: Each monthly run snapshots the board (rank, consensus FV and the Arkmetric family per prospect) into metric_snapshots. The Time Machine rebuilds the board at any past snapshot and diffs two dates into a changelog of risers, fallers, debuts and grade changes. URL-shareable.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Export a shareable graphic - a prospect card, farm card, list, or card pack - as a PNG (or a short animated clip), with rarity treatment matching the list.
entries.methodology: Templates: single-prospect cards (compact / detailed / scouting / stats / card back), farm cards, ranked-list boards and multi-card packs. Cards carry the FV-tier rarity frame, the FV history chart, tool radar, Statcast sliders and surplus. PNG exports at 2x; an animated WebM shows the foil. The image is pre-rendered, so Copy / Download / Share are immediate.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A configurable plot/query builder: any X/Y metric, color + size encodings, log scales, filters, brush-to-zoom, a shareable URL config, and a GFX export.
entries.methodology: Any two-axis plot over a cohort (MiLB, debuted, draft, overseas, IFA or farm systems): X / Y from any metric, color and size encodings, log scales, org / level / position and per-axis threshold filters, brush to zoom, player search. The configuration lives in the URL.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A personal, locally-saved set of starred prospects, filterable and exportable as a GFX card pack.
entries.methodology: Starred prospects are stored in the browser (localStorage; nothing leaves the device). The list filters like any board and exports as a Generate GFX card pack.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Movement buckets (Risers, Fallers, Rebounders) plus breakout and upside flags, with the driver signals behind each placement.
entries.methodology: Classifies recent movement by consensus-FV velocity, confirmed or contradicted by performance signals (RPS+, SC+, tool velocity), and shows the driver chips behind each placement. The spotlight age cap removes old-for-level prospects first.
entries.formula:
bucket rule: risers = consensus-FV velocity up AND performance signals confirm; fallers = velocity down or performance contradicts; rebounders = pedigree or past-list players whose current performance recovers
the spotlight age cap runs first (capped prospects return bucket = none); each placement carries its driver chips
entries.example: A 20yo A+ bat whose consensus rose 2.5 points with RPS+ and SC+ confirming lands in Risers with those chips. The same line from a 26yo AAA hitter never reaches a bucket: the age cap fires first.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: FV-keyed collectible treatment on prospect photos: shine (45) → foil (50) → chrome (55-60) → holo (61-69) → legendary (70+). Same logic on the list and in Generate GFX.
entries.methodology: FV 45 = shine (static gold), 50 = foil (silver shimmer), 55-60 = chrome, 61-69 = holo (rainbow), 70+ = legendary (rainbow and glow); below 45, a team-color frame. The same FV → tier map drives list headshots and Generate GFX cards (GFX captures the animation as a static frame for PNG).
entries.visual: 70legendary → holo → chrome → foil → shine
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Press ⌘K (Mac) or Ctrl+K to look up any glossary term - or jump to any prospect - from anywhere on the site.
entries.methodology: Type any metric name or alias to see its definition and open the full entry, or a prospect name to jump to him. Opens with ⌘K / Ctrl+K (or /); Escape closes it.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Predicted total guarantee for a free agent from the market model, on the deferral-adjusted NPV basis (a 97%-deferred sticker is not the same liability as level cash; schedules in the curated deferral ledger discount at the platform's net 7% rate, deals with no schedule keep their sticker). What teams will pay in present value, not what the production is worth. Formerly mGuarantee.
entries.methodology: A two-stage regression (contract length first, then log guarantee given length) trained on the 2014-15-to-present FA signing corpus. Features: age, projected year-1 WAR (eWAR basis), position group, qualifying-offer status, class supply, the winter $/WAR level (carried forward ex-ante), nearest-comps anchors, and economic anchors (discounted projected WAR x $/WAR; prime years x quality). Predictions clamp to a 2.5x envelope around the comps median and blend toward comps in the megadeal regime. P10-P90 bands are empirical residual quantiles from the forward-chained backtest. It beat the nearest-comps baseline on guarantee, AAV and years across nine held-out winters (Gate 2, Model Accountability page). Phase 2 (2026-06) moved targets, comps anchors and the winter $/WAR series to the NPV basis; the Gate 2 re-run read guarantee MAE 10.06 against comps 11.19. A LightGBM challenger with monotone economic constraints lost to this model on all three ship criteria at n = 1,199, so the two-stage OLS stays. The flat 5% $/WAR escalation also held: fitted trend forecasts lost the forward-chained eval (MAPE 0.122 / 0.132 against 0.102).
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Predicted average annual value: projGuarantee / projLength, with its own P10-P90 band. Formerly displayed as mAAV.
entries.methodology: Both framings are projected: the per-year price (projAAV) and total value / length (projGuarantee / projLength). The projAAV band rides the guarantee band at the point-estimate term.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Predicted contract length in years (P10-P90 banded), from a log-years model with comps stacking and a prime-years-remaining term. Formerly displayed as mYears.
entries.methodology: Length is modeled before money (teams trade years against AAV). The stage predicts log(years) with curvature terms (WAR squared, age x WAR), prime years remaining (max(0, 30 - age)) and the nearest-comps median length as a feature. It beat the comps baseline 0.441 against 0.485 MAE across nine held-out winters (Gate 2, fa_mkt_v2).
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The FA surfaces print a verdict (value = projected underpaid, market = about right, overpay = projected overpaid) backed by Deal+, the 100-scale index of rational value against price.
entries.methodology: Deal+ = 100 x rational value / predicted (or actual) guarantee. The verdict edges are empirically centered corpus terciles, not symmetric around 100: Deal+ is right-skewed under convex pricing. Since 2026-07-30 (owner decision) the edges are per position group, cut on the 1,300-signing forward-chained corpus at the actual price, so 'value' means cheap for the position group: SP overpay < 86 / value ≥ 182, RP 65 / 146, C 101 / 243, other position players 103 / 237. The RP edges sit lowest because relievers are paid more per projected WAR; about half of the old all-pitchers-look-like-overpays effect was that market property. A class that skews one way against these fixed edges is information.
entries.formula:
Deal+ = 100 x rational value / guarantee (predicted before signing, actual after)
verdict: overpay < lo, value >= hi, market between, with per-position-group tercile edges (lo/hi): SP 86/182, RP 65/146, C 101/243, POS 103/237
entries.example: A starter predicted at $60M with $115M of rational value reads Deal+ 192 (100 x 115/60): past the SP value edge of 182, verdict value. The same 192 on a catcher sits under the C edge of 243: market.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Rational value minus predicted market price.
entries.methodology: Two independently derived numbers: rational value (what the projected production is worth in NPV) and predicted market price (what teams will pay, from the market model). Contract Surplus ($) = rational − market; positive means the market is expected to underprice the player. The retrospective ledger applies the same lens backward: realized WAR (eWAR basis) x each season's estimated $/WAR minus prorated money paid, for every MLB free-agent deal since 2014-15.
entries.formula:
Contract Surplus ($) = rational value - predicted market price (both NPV, independently derived)
retrospective ledger: realized WAR (eWAR basis) x each season's estimated $/WAR - prorated money paid, summed over the deal
entries.example: Rational value $88M against a predicted guarantee of $70M reads +$18M. Backward, a 4-year $70M deal that returned 9 WAR at $11M/WAR ledgers 9 x 11 - 70 = +$29M.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The mean of the worst 10% of simulated WAR paths over the predicted term: a conditional value at risk, not the P10. A surplus point estimate hides what a deal looks like when it goes wrong; this is that number.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The probability a player reaches free agency at all. It is 100% when a contract simply expires, and lower for the option family, where membership stays probabilistic until the option resolves.
entries.methodology: Band-priced options read the option price against the predicted AAV band (v2); mutual and conditional options keep explicit v1 priors. The source is carried per row in enterProbSrc.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A 0 to 1 score for how well a club and a free agent match, built from positional need, contention window, payroll room, park and the club's own signing behaviour. It is a demand estimate, not a prediction of where he signs.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The dollar cost of forfeited draft picks (and intl pool money) when signing a qualifying-offer free agent.
entries.methodology: Signing a QO-attached free agent forfeits picks per the CBA compensation matrix (rule-versioned; CBT payors forfeit their 2nd- and 5th-highest picks plus $1M of international pool). Each forfeited slot is priced from the site's own draft research: realized expected first-six-season WAR at the slot through the surplus machinery. Rational value and pick values share the same 7% NPV currency, so the tax subtracts directly.
entries.formula:
QO tax = SUM(forfeited picks priced in $) + forfeited intl pool $ at face value
pick $ = realized expected first-6-season WAR at the representative slot, spread flat over 6 control years, priced through the service-time surplus machinery with a draft-to-debut lag (fallback: median consensus FV at the slot through the prospect surplus curve)
forfeiture matrix is rule-versioned CBA text, e.g. CBT payors forfeit their 2nd- and 5th-highest picks + $1M of intl pool
entries.example: A CBT-payor club signing a QO free agent gives up its 2nd- and 5th-highest picks plus $1M of international pool. With the two slots pricing near $12M and $3M of prospect surplus, the tax takes about $16M off the signing's rational value.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The NPV of a free agent's projected WAR path: each season priced convexly through the tier curve at the winter's ex-ante FA $/WAR level, escalated per season and discounted at the platform's configured 7% rate. What the production is worth, never what the market will pay.
entries.methodology: Same NPV currency as PROSPX prospect surplus and, since v2, the same convex season pricing (the value framework's tier curve rescaled to the winter's $/WAR level): a 1-WAR season and the third win of a 3-WAR season are different products, and flat pricing graded the bottom of the class as bargains (class median Deal+ 220 under flat pricing). Computed with no reference to the market model; Contract Surplus is only meaningful because neither side reads the other. The winter $/WAR level is the NPV-basis signings-implied series (deferral-adjusted numerator) carried forward at the measured-best flat 5%.
entries.formula:
RV = SUM_t tiered_war_value(WAR_t) x level x (1 + infl)^t / (1 + r)^t
level = winter $/WAR (ex-ante, signings-implied) / the valuation set's flat $/WAR; r = the platform's configured discount rate
each season prices through the CONVEX tier curve, never WAR x a flat rate
entries.example: A projected 3.0-WAR season at a $12M/WAR winter prices above the flat 3.0 x 12 = $36M because the tier curve pays a premium for the third win; a 0.7-WAR season prices below its flat $8.4M. A discounted 3.0 / 2.6 / 2.2 path lands near $90M.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The 10th-90th percentile range around every FA market prediction: empirical residual quantiles from the forward-chained backtest. Parametric intervals failed the coverage gate (0.858 against the 0.75-0.85 target) and were rejected.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Probability that an option-holding player reaches the free-agent class. Single-party options are priced from the market model's own band distribution; mutual options carry a fixed empirical prior; rows with no market anchor show no number.
entries.methodology: Single-party options (club option, player option, opt-out) use the market model's band distribution (v2): a log-normal interpolated from the empirical residual bands (mu = log point estimate, sigma = P10-P90 span / (2 x 1.2816)), and P(enter) is the tail probability of the market against the strike. Strike and market number must be the same kind of quantity: club and player options strike one season's salary against projected AAV; an opt-out strikes the remaining guarantee against the projected multi-year guarantee. Mutual options keep a fixed empirical prior (both sides cannot want to exercise at once); conditional options carry a documented unknown prior. The v1 $-gap logistic (fa_class, config-documented) is the heuristic these paths replaced. Decision-level validation waits on historical option-decision data; the 2026-27 winter's logged events are the first live test.
entries.formula:
player-held (opt-out / player option): P(enter) = 1 - Phi((ln K - mu) / sigma); club option: P(enter) = Phi((ln K - mu) / sigma)
mu = ln(point estimate), sigma = (ln P90 - ln P10) / (2 x 1.2816); K = the strike (one season's salary for options, the remaining guarantee for opt-outs)
mutual option: fixed empirical prior; conditional: documented prior; no anchor -> no number
entries.example: A $20M club option on a player priced at $14M AAV (P10 $9M, P90 $22M): the club likely declines, P(enter) near 0.85. As a $20M player option he keeps the money: near 0.15.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The 2022 CBA expires 2026-12-01, so every 2027 threshold, tax band and QO figure is the last known rule carried forward, not a bargained number. Every surface using one carries the carry-forward flag.

The per-winter price of a win implied by that winter's FA signings: guaranteed dollars over projected WAR, carried forward ex-ante so a prediction never sees its own winter. Not the PROSPX $/WAR (tiered), a three-tier rolling market price for prospect valuation.
entries.methodology: Two ex-ante steps. First, each winter's implied price: total NPV guarantee (deferral-adjusted when a schedule is on file) divided by total discounted projected contract WAR across that winter's MLB free-agent deals. WAR is projected point-in-time, so the ratio reads what buyers thought they were buying; thin winters are dropped. Second, the carry-forward: a class year's level uses PRIOR winters only (config market_model.dpw_forecast.method): flat5 carries the latest prior winter forward at a flat escalation, the trend variants fit a log-linear trend, and under four prior winters it is always flat5. The method choice is adjudicated by the forward-chained ledger in data/dpw_forecast_eval.json. This series sets the level rational value prices at; the PROSPX tiered $/WAR is a different quantity.
entries.formula:
dpw(winter) = SUM NPV guarantees / SUM disc-WAR over that winter's deals; disc-WAR = SUM_t WAR_t / (1 + r)^t over each contract's term; thin winters dropped
winter_dpw(class year) = carry-forward from PRIOR winters only: flat5 = dpw(latest prior) x (1 + esc)^gap; trend = log-linear fit on prior winters; under 4 priors always flat5
entries.example: If the 2026 winter implied $11.5M per discounted projected WAR, the 2027 class prices off that number carried forward one year, about $12.1M under flat5. The 2027 winter's own signings never enter its level.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Badge on FA projections whose platform season is missing or injury-shortened: below 30% of a role-aware full season, scaled by how much of the season has elapsed. A projection resting on older seasons is the model's weakest case (the Burnes / Bieber rehab class).
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The five 0-1 scores behind every FA team fit: need (displacement WAR gap at the position, discounted when a near-ETA PROSPX prospect blocks it; MLB incumbents block through the gap and are named in the blocked-by list), window (marginal playoff leverage at the club's baseline wins), afford (CBT-basis tax space against the predicted AAV, with a floor for habitual taxpayers), park (batted-side park factor, the smallest weight) and behavior (biggest-ever guarantee against this price, recent 3-winter outlay, $100M-deal participation).
entries.methodology: v2 weights: need 0.31 / window 0.19 / afford 0.22 / park 0.04 / behavior 0.24. Park was cut from 0.12 after the most suppressive park topped every pitcher's fit list. Afford reads Spotrac's CBT-basis tax space and floors at 0.4 for over-the-line clubs that keep signing nine-figure deals; behavior blends deal-scale history (0.5), recency-weighted three-winter outlay (0.3) and $100M-deal count (0.2). Blocked-by names two kinds of blocker: PX = a near-ETA PROSPX prospect (FV ≥ 50), MLB = a contracted incumbent projecting ≥ 2.5 WAR at the slot.
entries.formula:
fit = 0.31 x need + 0.19 x window + 0.22 x afford + 0.04 x park + 0.24 x behavior, each component 0-1
behavior = 0.5 x deal-scale history + 0.3 x recency-weighted 3-winter outlay + 0.2 x $100M-deal count; afford floors at 0.4 for over-the-line clubs that keep signing nine-figure deals
entries.example: A club with a 2-WAR hole at short (need 0.9), on the playoff bubble (window 0.8), tax room (afford 0.7), a neutral park (0.5) and a real spending record (behavior 0.8) scores 0.31x0.9 + 0.19x0.8 + 0.22x0.7 + 0.04x0.5 + 0.24x0.8 = 0.80.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Winter events (signings, option decisions, qualifying offers) are dated the day the pipeline first saw them, because the source publishes terms without dates. Stamps are append-only and never revised.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The FA module's two shipping gates: Gate 1, the projection engine against ten held-out seasons (beat the naive baseline; P10-P90 coverage in 0.75-0.85); Gate 2, the market model against nine forward-chained winters (beat nearest comps on guarantee, AAV and years). Both verdicts render on the Free Agency Model Accountability page, misses included.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The most similar historical contracts to a free agent's profile, by standardized feature distance over the 2014-15-to-present signing corpus. Always real deals; they anchor the market model and appear on every board row.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A Marcel-style weighted-rates projection (5/3/2 recency weights) with hitter ISO blended toward Savant xISO (2015+), mapped to WAR (eWAR basis; corpus labels follow the served series) through a fitted rate-to-WAR model and decayed along survivorship-corrected aging curves fit on the 2000-2026 corpus. Multi-year decay walks regressed-rate curves: raw observed deltas mix aging with luck regression, and chaining them double-counted the regression (the horizon-5 star tail collapsed to a 0.06 predicted/actual ratio). Power and finesse pitchers age on separate curves; hitter power/contact cohorts were measured and parked.
entries.methodology: Beyond Gate 1 (next season), multi-year decay is measured by a forward-chained horizon backtest (proj_eval.py, bases 2017-2021): the regressed-rate curves doubled the horizon-5 ≥3-WAR tail ratio (0.06 to 0.12) and cut star bias from -1.34 to -0.64 WAR while Gate 1 improved. Since Phase 1 (2026-06) horizons 1-5 are served by proj_lgbm_v1, LightGBM quantile models (P10/P25/P50/P75/P90 per horizon) stacked on the Marcel champion (its prediction is a feature, so the trees learn its residuals), with no zero floor on the bands. It shipped after beating the champion on dev bases, the Gate-1 seasons and a touched-once 2022-2024 holdout. Marcel + aging stays the fallback, the stacking feature and the shape for horizons 6+. Long-horizon star medians run ~0.2 WAR below the champion (zero-inflated labels), with equal star MAE.
entries.formula:
year-1 rate = Marcel(5/3/2 recency weights, exposure-weighted) regressed to the league mean, hitter ISO blended toward Savant xISO; WAR1 = fitted rate-to-WAR map(rate)
year-t: WAR1 decayed along the survivorship-corrected REGRESSED-rate aging curve for the player's cohort (power and finesse pitchers on separate curves)
served horizons 1-5: proj_lgbm_v1 quantile heads (P10/P25/P50/P75/P90 per horizon) stacked ON the Marcel prediction; horizons 6+ and the fallback ride the Marcel+aging shape
entries.example: A 29yo hitter with trailing wOBA .350 / .340 / .320 (most recent first) blends to (5x.350 + 3x.340 + 2x.320)/10 = .341 before the league pull moves it a few points toward .310. The rate maps to a year-1 WAR, and the aging curve lowers each later season.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: ERA scaled so 100 = average; lower is better. 90 reads 10% better. Two quantities share the label: on MLB seasons it is MLB's published ERA- (park- and league-adjusted, read verbatim); on MiLB seasons it is level-relative, shrunk, and has no park adjustment.
entries.origin: Industry metric. The ERA- park- and league-adjusted index, implemented by FanGraphs (100 = average, lower is better). The MiLB version here is level-relative and not park-adjusted.
entries.methodology: MiLB: ERA- vs level = 100 × ERA_adj / level ERA, where ERA_adj = (IP × ERA + 50 × level ERA) / (IP + 50) pulls a short sample toward the level mean (K = 50 IP) and the level ERA comes from the level norms. No park term. MLB: read verbatim from MLB's published eraMinus.
entries.formula:
MiLB: ERA- = 100 × ((IP·ERA + 50·lgERA_level) / (IP + 50)) / lgERA_level
MLB: published eraMinus (park- and league-adjusted)

entries.definition: On-base average with each event weighted by its actual run value (a walk is worth less than a double, which OBP ignores). Scaled to look like OBP: ~.320 is league average, .400 elite.
entries.origin: Industry metric. Created by Tom Tango (The Book); implemented by FanGraphs. It weights each offensive event by its average run value.

entries.definition: Lifecycle markers on module names: α = newly launched, numbers may still move; β = established, in beta. The masthead chip and the nav superscript are the same marker.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The homepage event feed and ticker: debuts, promotions, trades, IL moves, real FV changes and free-agency winter events, dated and color-coded by type. FV items are real grade changes only; composite movement scores are not shown as news.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The currently tracked, non-graduated MiLB prospects that every ranking, farm grade and Arkmetric is computed over. MLB-side modules (Free Agency) read prospect data read-only and may not write into it.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Every projected WAR path ships three variants: mean, floor (P10) and ceiling (P90). Veterans take quantile paths; prospects take the 10th / 90th-percentile outcome bucket of the calibrated P(bucket|FV): a prospect's downside is the bust outcome, not a symmetric band.
entries.methodology: Since Phase 1 the veteran floor / mean / ceiling come from the quantile heads (trained on horizon residual distributions, negatives included). Before that, the Gate-1 empirical year-1 residual quantile for the reliability bucket (fa_gate1_eval.json band_quantiles, per side x exposure tier) was decayed along the aging curves, with measured 0.80 P10-P90 coverage. Surplus buckets price the floor and ceiling paths through the same convex curve as the mean; the surplus range on a card is the same machinery, not a separate model.
entries.formula:
veterans: floor / mean / ceiling = the quantile heads' P10 / mean / P90 paths (pre-Phase-1 shape: the year-1 empirical residual quantile for the reliability bucket, decayed along the SAME aging curves)
prospects: floor / ceiling = the 10th / 90th-percentile OUTCOME BUCKET of the calibrated P(bucket | FV) categorical
surplus range = the same three paths priced through the same convex curve as the mean
entries.example: A veteran projected at 3.1 WAR next season might carry a 1.2 floor and a 4.8 ceiling. A FV 50 prospect's floor is the bust bucket, about zero WAR.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The /projections/ surface: the FA module's Gate-1-validated projection engine applied to every MLB player with recent history (five-year WAR paths, eWAR basis, with floor / mean / ceiling buckets), plus PROSPX prospects joining at their projected ETA through the calibrated FV outcome model.
entries.methodology:
Veterans: the same Marcel engine, aging curves and fitted WAR map the FA class board uses. Prospects: P(bucket|FV) x per-bucket WAR trajectories scaled by FV and shaped by projected debut age (bust-inclusive means, outcome-bucket floor and ceiling). Seasons price through the convex tier curve at the ex-ante FA $/WAR level, escalating per season. Veteran surplus prices every season of the club control window: contracted dollars where a contract exists, the league minimum for pre arbitration seasons, and the projected award for arbitration seasons, discounted at the platform's 7% rate. Seasons past club control carry a projection and no price. Prospect surplus is the platform surplus value, over the 7-season valuation window from the projected ETA.

Team Outlook win totals are retro-backtested on 2022-25 with 2025 held out. Each roster sums the engine's mean year-1 projections (the median-like quantile point on player pages is never summed) plus a depth pool of sub-floor players, and every season is recentered uniformly so the league sums to 2,430 wins. Age-cohort corrections fit on 2022-24 residuals were tested as a challenger on the held-out 2025, lost, and are not applied. The Accountability view prints the served roll-up's team MAE and r per season beside a prior-season-wins carry-forward, read from team_outlook_eval.json.
