The board shows two different facts about the same player and keeps them apart by name: the Control column prints the last season the club HOLDS him (guaranteed contract seasons, then the remaining pre arbitration seasons, then the projected arbitration seasons) and its sub line prints the last season a signed contract GUARANTEES him. The seasons past the guarantee are projections and are drawn with a dashed border.
entries.formula:
veterans: the FA engine (Marcel + aging + fitted WAR map), five-year WAR paths (eWAR basis) with quantile floor / mean / ceiling; surplus over the club control window
prospects: P(bucket | FV) x per-bucket WAR trajectories scaled by FV and projected debut age, joining at projected ETA
team outlook: SUM roster mean year-1 WAR + depth pool, league-normalized to 2,430 wins (age-cohort corrections apply only while they win their holdout gate; today they do not)
entries.example: A 27yo 4-WAR starter shows a declining five-year path with a surplus claim over every season his club controls: his contracted years at their salary, then his projected arbitration years. A FV 55 prospect with ETA 2027 joins his club's 2027 line with a bust-inclusive mean.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The accountability tab on MLB Projections: each model's champion, the baseline it had to beat, the metric, the held-out result, and what is not yet scoreable. Verdicts read from the model registry, refreshed monthly.
entries.methodology: Forward-chained evaluation: fit through year Y-1, score the untouched year Y, repeat, and report pooled and per-year accuracy against a stated baseline. Validated requires that backtest to beat its baseline on the pre-registered metric; partial measurement (short window, descriptive, live-pending) ships provisional. The eval artifacts (data/*_eval.json) hold the tables; the registry (data/model_registry.json) holds the one-line verdict and disclosures, and test_methodology_freshness.py requires every registry model to map to a glossary entry.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The four-way label every registry model carries: validated (a forward-chained backtest beats the baseline), provisional (measured, partially: short window or descriptive), unvalidated (a predictive claim with no measurement yet, listed so it stays visible) or deprecated (failed validation, retired).
entries.methodology: Verdicts are committed with their eval artifact, not auto-derived: validated requires the artifact to exist and beat its baseline on the pre-registered metric; unvalidated must not carry an artifact. The monthly refresh re-stamps freshness (artifact age) and never upgrades a verdict.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Grading a model on history it never saw: train on seasons through Y-1, score the untouched year Y, walk forward a year at a time. No lookahead, so the error is what a reader would have gotten in real time.
entries.methodology: Curves, weights and maps are refit per target year on data through Y-1 (the Gate-1 pattern), predictions are compared with realized outcomes, and accuracy is pooled across folds and reported per year. A held-out season untouched during tuning is the cleanest read; the rest are dev folds. Team-level reads assign each player to his actual season team, isolating engine error from roster churn.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A season (or fold) kept out of every tuning decision and scored once, at the end. Its error is the least biased accuracy estimate; a model that wins on dev folds and loses the holdout does not ship.
entries.methodology: Dev folds are used repeatedly while iterating; the holdout is not. The projections engine reports a touched-once 2022-2024 holdout for veteran WAR paths and a held-out 2025 for team wins; out-years whose labels have not matured are flagged not yet scoreable.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The live scoreboard for a projection whose target has not happened: the number is logged now and graded against a stated baseline when the outcome lands.
entries.methodology: Team Outlook win totals are the standing case: only the first projected season is gated, scored as MAE against final standings (baseline = prior-season wins carried forward); out-years are a trajectory, not a scored forecast. The gate stays pending until the season ends, then the result is committed whatever it says.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The average size of a model's misses in the units it predicts: mean |actual - predicted|. Lower is better. A team-wins MAE of 7.7 means records miss by about eight wins on average.
entries.methodology: Reported with bias (mean signed error) and, for bands, coverage (share of actuals inside P10-P90, target ~80%). MAE weights misses linearly, so the heavy WAR tail does not dominate it the way it would a squared error.
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: The behavioral profile on each farm system's Tendencies tab: promotion aggressiveness, draft position and trait preferences, pitch identity of developed arms, per-tool development rates, international pool strategy (quality vs quantity), trade profile (volume, prospect-capital direction, quality vs depth, cash considerations), draft-pool allocation and IL burden. Every value is league-relative.
entries.methodology: Each axis comes from the platform's own records (grade history 2017-present, signed draft picks 2021-present, IFA classes, the trade ledger, MLB transaction text) as a z-score across the 30 orgs; verdict labels fire only at |z| ≥ 0.5. Tool development counts only same-source snapshot pairs ≥ 60 days apart inside one org, so cross-source disagreement never counts as development. Pitch identity profiles the MLB arsenals of players an org developed (per-pitch usage history is not archived yet). Cash-consideration direction is parsed from official transaction text.
entries.formula:
each axis: z = (org value - 30-org mean) / 30-org sd; a verdict label fires only at |z| >= 0.5
tool development counts only SAME-SOURCE snapshot pairs >= 60 days apart inside one org
entries.example: An org promoting hitters 0.8 sd faster than league with an intl class-size z of +0.6 and an average-bonus z of -0.4 reads 'aggressive promoter, quantity buyer': the +0.6 axis gets a label, the -0.4 axis stays unlabeled under the 0.5 gate.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: How far a drafted player has outrun his slot, on the Draft tab's Overperformers board. Two lenses: realized outcome (current prospect FV minus the median FV for his pick band, with career MLB WAR beside it) and draft-day value (how many picks past his pre-draft consensus rank he went).
entries.methodology: Realized outcome bins signed picks 2021-present into bands (1-5, 6-10, 11-20, 21-40, 41-75, 76-150, 151+) and takes the median current FV per band as the slot expectation; overperformance is current FV minus that median. Current value joins from the live board and debuts via the promoted / MiLB-key link, falling back to the draft-time grade. Draft-day value = actual overall pick − pre-draft consensus rank. Pooled across completed classes, deduped.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Contract dollars discounted for deferral schedules at the platform's net 7% rate, the basis for every Phase-2 market number. A curated ledger (data/deferrals.json) holds the schedules: Ohtani's $700M prices as ~$274.8M of present liability; deals with no schedule keep their sticker.
entries.methodology: NPV = sum of scheduled payments / (1+r)^years-out, with r the configured net rate 0.07 (value_framework discount_rate, from clemens_2026 params.discount.net_rate) and years-out counted from 0, so a first-season payment is undiscounted; schedules rescaled to the sticker total. The net 7% platform rate is harsher than the CBT's ~4.4% statutory rate, so these NPVs read lower than league-reported figures; one discount rate is used everywhere (prospect surplus, rational value, contracts). Every guarantee ≥ $200M must carry a schedule or an explicit none entry (the Gate-2 coverage audit lists misses); entries are curated and unverified until owner spot-check.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Swing-quality index from Statcast bat tracking (bat speed, swing length, attack angle and direction, swing-path tilt, intercept point), scaled so 100 = league average; higher is better. Built by Will Cahoon; eephus.io runs the model's scoring on each player's tracked MLB swings.
entries.methodology: Per-swing features are filtered to competitive swings, aggregated per hitter (means and variability), and scored through the model's run-value pipelines with a reliability shrink toward 100 below ~180 swings. Bat tracking exists only at MLB (2024+); no public MiLB tracking exists, so prospects light up after their debut.
entries.example: A debuted prospect at Swing+ 115 over 300+ swings has a plus MLB swing; 95 on 60 swings is mostly shrink.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: eephus.io's college baseball percentile module (created by Joseph Gillis): Savant-style hitter and pitcher dashboards over college TrackMan-era data, with per-metric leaderboards, player pages and search.
entries.methodology: Percentiles are computed within the college dataset's qualified pool per season. The module is in alpha.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: eephusFV (eFV) is our Future Value grade and the site's primary prospect ranking, grounded in what past prospects became. It predicts a prospect's realized first-six-MLB-season WAR (eWAR basis from the 2026-09 epoch, bWAR before it) and states it on the 20-80 FV scale; consensus FV shows alongside. eFV needs a pro track record, so very recent draftees and international signings show consensus FV until they have a season of production.
entries.methodology:
A prior-anchored, outcome-grounded model. The prior is consensus FV (raw, pre-rounding); a lean ridge model, with a guarded blend back toward consensus, moves the grade only on signals that add information beyond consensus out of sample. Hitters: level-translated on-base skill (OBP) and contact (K rate and its multi-season peak), an OPS-vs-level read for the fringe tiers, age relative to level and absolute age, track record (pro seasons, a missing-record indicator, IFA / college cohorts), highest level reached, and the hit and speed tools. Pitchers: multi-season peak and final-season strikeout rate, walk rate, K-backed run prevention (the x_era_k interaction behind KRP+), age relative to level and absolute age, and the fastball. Game power is excluded for hitters because scouts over-price it relative to realized WAR; that omission is eFV's power correction.

Training: prospects who debuted 2011-2024 (boards strictly before debut) against realized first-six-season WAR (eWAR v2 labels from the 2026-09 epoch, bWAR labels before it; hitter labels are identical under both, pitcher labels are FIP re-priced within role), busts at zero, forward-chained out of time. The 2024 debut class is right-censored (two of six seasons observed) and enters at reduced weight.

Grade scale (restamped 2026-07-30): the headline grade is value_framework.outcome_implied_fv(E[6yr WAR]), the inverse of the pooled empirical outcome curve fit on resolved cohorts, so the grade is the FV whose measured first-six-year WAR matches the prediction. A pure function of predicted WAR (no age or position). Below about FV 45 the measured curve is flat, so grades there preserve order but their spacing is not outcome-calibrated. Above about FV 57 the measured cells hold single digits per grade and are blended toward a published industry prior, so the top of the board is closer to the industry table than to our measurement. The retired per-side quantile map (a rank-map onto the consensus distribution) stopped being displayed on 2026-07-25.

Two other grades sit under the displayed one. Surplus dollars still price through the retired per-side quantile grade, because the surplus and WAR-path curves were fit on the consensus 20-80 scale that map lands on; re-anchoring the headline grade on 2026-07-30 moved zero dollars. The star/bust odds stay on the retired realized-implied map, where they were ground-truthed; re-keying them has not been measured.

Board overlays (live board only, owner-directed): injury, prospect age, stale list coverage and a reliever-ceiling dial tilt the model's WAR leg and show as labeled factor chips. The reliever ceiling is a policy dial, not an accuracy claim: relief-designated arms age 25+ whose model WAR runs hot take a bounded haircut on the model leg (0.80, or 0.70 from age 26), because list-time relievers of that profile almost never returned star value in the resolved rows and the censored data cannot price that risk.

Measured standing: a TIE. On eFV's own out-of-sample protocol the ordering gap against consensus FV is smaller than the margin the eval can resolve on both sides, so neither grade is shown as the winner. The live figures, noise floor and per-era split print on the Methodology page from the backtest artifact. By debut era the ordering is not uniform: consensus leads the oldest cohort, eFV the most recent, and the middle cohort splits by side.

LEVEL CALIBRATION, RETIRED 2026-08-14: the served WAR is the model's WAR. An affine dispersion correction shipped that morning and was reverted to identity the same day by owner decision (a_c 0.0 and b_c 1.0 on both sides); nothing rescales the model leg at the grade seam. The cost: the corrected arm was resolvably more accurate against realized WAR on the full pool (paired MAE -0.2787 hitters, CI95 -0.334 to -0.224; -0.1415 pitchers, CI95 -0.173 to -0.109), so the revert made eFV agree with scouts more and match outcomes less. It also widened the abstention floor: the FV20 floor population grows 784 to 1,149, because without the intercept those rows fall below zero predicted WAR, where the outcome map abstains. The revert kept the top of the board in order; the correction had inverted it. The retired coefficients stay in the code and are not live (hit 0.470359 / 0.663929, pit 0.493744 / 0.546915); reopening needs new resolved cohorts, not a new functional form.

Registry verdict: provisional.
entries.formula: eFV grade = outcome_implied_fv( E[6yr WAR] ) on eWAR v2 labels, the inverse of the pooled empirical outcome curve fit on resolved cohorts; surplus = value_framework( retired per-side quantile grade ); star/bust odds = outcome model( retired realized-implied FV )
entries.example: A contact-and-discipline hitter consensus has at 45 can read 48 eFV when his translated walk and strikeout rates beat the level; a power-over-hit profile can read lower, since power adds less realized WAR than scouts price.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Per-tool eFV: each 20-80 tool re-graded by how well it, plus the prospect's relevant production, predicts the MLB outcome the tool is meant to forecast.
entries.methodology: Each tool with a clean realized target is grounded in the MLB stat it predicts: power in ISO, hit in average and contact, speed in steals, the fastball in strikeout rate, command in walk rate. Tool eFV blends the consensus tool grade with pre-debut MiLB production only where production adds signal beyond the grade. Scout grades are already good (power grade to MLB ISO ranks at about 0.52); production adds most for fastball-to-strikeout. Tools with no clean realized metric (raw power, fielding, arm, individual breaking-ball shapes) pass the consensus grade through unchanged.
entries.formula: tool eFV = rank-map( z(grade) + w*z(MiLB production) ), w from the production's partial correlation after the grade
entries.example: A pitcher whose fastball grades 55 but who already misses bats at an elite MiLB rate can carry a higher fastball eFV, because realized strikeout rate adds to the grade for predicting MLB strikeouts.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A PROVISIONAL Future Value for prospects who have played pro ball but have no grade from any source: DSL / CPX breakouts the ranking cycle has not reached, plus deep-system depth. It ranks on the PROSPX board among the graded players by grade, and shows on farm rosters and its own detail page, always with a dashed badge and a small 'p'. Most land 20-30; real production breakouts reach the 40s, where a soft ceiling compresses the top so an unscouted player cannot run away from the scale.
entries.methodology: The flagship eFV is anchored on consensus FV and abstains without a source grade, so ungraded players get a production-only model: a ridge on the same translated MiLB production features (level-relative K / BB / OBP / ISO against contemporaneous norms, age for level, multi-season peaks, track record) without the consensus-FV feature (hitters keep level reached; pitchers drop it because it rewards quad-A org arms). Forward-chained, the served grade's rank correlation (Spearman) with realized WAR is 0.27 for hitters (n 1,032) and 0.11 for pitchers (n 895), from data/xfv_ungraded_eval.json. The WAR prediction maps through a linear grade curve with a soft knee: above the knee the grade is compressed toward a ceiling, so the order is kept but a thin sample cannot print a top-prospect grade. A typical org filler reads about 22-25. A leading indicator: it ranks on the board and in the farm-system top-end and depth pool, with no consensus anchor behind it.
entries.formula: provisional eFV = max( 20 , BASE + SLOPE * model E[6yr WAR] ), compressed above KNEE toward CEIL (no consensus-FV anchor). Hitters: 27 + 3.8 * WAR, knee 43, ceiling 49. Pitchers: 25 + 4.5 * WAR, knee 34, ceiling 38.
entries.example: Anthony Potestio (NYY, Single-A, age 21.9) has no source grade. A .513 OBP and .351 ISO over 80 plate appearances put his provisional eFV at 46.8 on the 2026-09-24 build, shown as 47: above the hitter knee of 43, so it sits in the compressed band.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Pitcher index for run prevention backed by missing bats: a below-level ERA supported by an above-level strikeout rate. 100 = active-pitcher-pool average, 10 points = 1 standard deviation; higher is better.
entries.methodology:
Puts the eFV pitcher model's run-prevention x strikeout interaction on the shared '+' scale. Raw term = (-era_rel) x k_rel, where era_rel = ERA minus the level-median ERA and k_rel = K% minus the level-median K%, both shrunk by batters faced with w = BF / (BF + 40) (80 before the 2026-07-24c loosen), so a cameo reads pool-neutral. The product is high only when both legs hold: K-backed run prevention, not a low ERA on weak contact.

The display pill and the model feature differ in one quadrant. With both legs bad (ERA worse than level and K% below level) the product of two negatives is positive. The eFV model feature (efv_model._x_era_k) zeroes that quadrant (2026-07-14 owner correction), which suits the fit but collapses roughly 834 doubly-below-average arms onto one league-average value. The display raw (efv_score._krp_display_raw, owner-authorized 2026-07-24) carries the negatively signed magnitude there instead, so those arms spread below the pool. Nothing else differs. For the display raw only, era_rel is winsorized to ±6 so a one-inning blowup cannot drive the pill.

The display raw is z-scored over the live pitcher pool and anchored 100 + 10z (population sigma, as SC+, DvM+ and pStuff+), unclamped (the 40-160 display clamp was removed 2026-07-24b; see the plus_metric_recal registry row). Pitchers with innings on file only. The same signal drives the 'K-backed run prevention' factor in the eFV explainer.
entries.formula:
KRP+ = 100 + 10 x (x_display - pool_mean) / pool_sd over the live pitcher pool, population sigma, no clamp.
x_display = (-era_rel) x k_rel everywhere EXCEPT the double-bad quadrant (era_rel > 0 AND k_rel < 0), where x_display = -abs((-era_rel) x k_rel).
MODEL feature (the eFV input, efv_model._x_era_k) = the same product except the double-bad quadrant returns 0.0. The pill and the model feature agree everywhere else.
era_rel and k_rel are level-relative rates shrunk by BF / (BF + 40); for the display raw only, era_rel is winsorized to plus or minus 6.
entries.example: A AA starter at a 2.90 ERA (level 4.20) with a 29% K% (level 22%) reads KRP+ ~120. The same ERA on a 19% K% reads near 100: run prevention the strikeouts do not support.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Values a trade both ways in one surplus currency: prospects on eFV surplus (calibrated NPV over the 7-season valuation window from their ETA), MLB players on projection surplus (NPV of projected production minus salary over the club control window). Build a package per side; the verdict reads net surplus, balanced within $5M.
entries.methodology:
A package evaluator plus the Bayesian trade-value board. Each player carries the surplus the rest of the site shows: a prospect's eFV-driven surplus over the 7-season valuation window (value_mm) or an MLB player's projection surplus (proj.surNpv, the MLB Projections NPV of convex production value minus salary over the club control window). An MLB Projections player page deep-links into the evaluator with that player loaded; evaluator rows link back. The Transactions Trade Audit prices every party at this same trade value, as of today rather than the trade date, and shares the $5M balanced band; it names no winner while any party is unpriced. Board ranks are contract-aware (surplus over the seasons still controlled), positional-scarcity and opt-out adjusted. Module by Anirudh Iyer.

A club controlled player with no contract for those years is priced on his salary path, not left at zero.
entries.formula:
side value = SUM player surplus: prospects at value_mm (calibrated eFV NPV over the 7-season valuation window), MLB players at proj.surNpv (NPV of projected production minus salary, the club control window only)
net = side A - side B; |net| <= $5M -> balanced, otherwise the verdict names the winning side
entries.example: A FV 55 prospect at $45M plus a FV 40 arm at $6M against a two-control-year MLB starter at $48M: net +$3M, inside the $5M band, verdict balanced.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A hitting prospect's projected first-MLB-season K% and BB%, translated from his final pre-debut level-relative MiLB rate. K% is the reliable read (2026-08 fit: r2 0.32); BB% is modest and flagged. Production (OPS / xwOBA) does not translate across the jump and is not projected.
entries.methodology: Matched-pair regression to the mean (the CollegeSavant college-to-Single-A method, applied MiLB-to-MLB): each debuted hitter's final pre-debut level-relative rate (k_rel / bb_rel vs the level mean) is paired with his first-MLB-season rate, and a shrunk slope is fit over the pairs. Leave-one-out validated, 2026-08 fit (n=287): K% LOO MAE 3.9, P10-P90 coverage 0.81, r2 0.32; BB% MAE 2.7, coverage 0.78, r2 0.14 (flagged with *). These are dated readings of the validation block in data/milb_translation.json and move with each refit. The band is the residual spread. OPS and xwOBA were tested and do not translate (r2 ~0.02): first-MLB production is dominated by selection, so only the sticky plate-skill rates are projected. A rate translation, not a value forecast; eFV is the value signal.
entries.formula:
projected first-MLB rate = y_mean + slope x (x - x_mean), where x = the final pre-debut level-relative rate (k_rel / bb_rel vs the level mean) and slope = OLS x n / (n + shrink K), fit on matched pre-debut vs first-MLB-season pairs
band = residual sd around the fit; K% and BB% only, production not translated
entries.example: A AAA bat striking out 4 points below his level's mean projects a first-MLB K% a couple of points better than the debutant average: the shrunk slope keeps only the share of the edge that historically survives the jump.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A reliever's run-prevention skill on a league-relative scale: 100 is an average reliever, 110 is 10 percent better. Built from stabilized strikeout, walk and contact-quality rates, regressed for small samples, anchored to the reliever-only pool. Higher is better. Coloured on the value ruler at 140 / 120 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology: A FIP-based skill rate in the ERA+ family, a ratio to the league rather than a z-score. The component rates (K%, BB%, HBP and a heavily regressed home-run rate) are shrunk toward the reliever pool mean by sample size and combined into a sample-shrunk FIP (Skill FIP). REM+ = 100 x pool-average FIP / the reliever's FIP, so a lower FIP scores above 100. The pool is relievers only, so 100 is the average reliever, not the average pitcher. Leverage stays out: gmLI, WPA and Shutdowns minus Meltdowns ride separate Impact columns, because the manager assigns leverage and it does not carry forward as skill.
entries.formula: REM+ = 100 x poolFIP / playerFIP (sample-shrunk FIP; 100 = average reliever)
entries.example: A reliever whose sample-shrunk FIP is 3.20 against a 4.00 reliever-pool mean reads REM+ 125, whatever his gmLI and WPA say.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Team bullpen rating: 100 is an average pen. Relief-innings-weighted REM+ of the pen's relievers. Coloured on the value ruler at 120 / 113 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology: Each reliever's REM+ is weighted by his relief innings, so a pen is credited for the quality of the innings it throws, not for how leverage is assigned. Lev Deploy+ weights by innings x gmLI to show how much leverage those innings carried. The board also shows depth (share of above-average arms) and a high-leverage core rating (the top arms by entry leverage).
entries.formula:
Bullpen+ = SUM(relief IP_r x REM+_r) / SUM relief IP_r over the pen's scored relievers
companions: Lev Deploy+ = the same mean weighted by IP x gmLI over gmLI-covered arms (blank when no coverage); depth = share of arms at REM+ >= 100; high-leverage core = mean REM+ of the top 3 arms by gmLI
entries.example: A pen whose top four arms (250 relief IP) average REM+ 112 while the last 150 IP average 92 reads Bullpen+ 105.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Team rotation rating: 100 is an average rotation. Starter-innings-weighted SEM+. On the Team Rotations board in MLB Stats; higher is better. Coloured on the value ruler at 120 / 113 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology: Each starter's SEM+ is weighted by his innings as a starter and divided by those innings, so a swingman with 30 innings cannot move the rotation the way a flat average would. Only starters with a scored SEM+ and positive innings enter; the display rounds to a whole point (unrounded as rotation_plus_raw). SEM+ is anchored on the starter pool, so 100 is the average rotation, and Rotation+ inherits SEM+'s shrinkage. Front 3 (mean SEM+ of the three best starters), the count of above-average starters and the durability columns (starter innings, games started) sit beside it as context. Built by starter_export.py from the StatsAPI season pitching leaderboard via sem_plus.score_pool and sem_plus.team_rotation.
entries.formula: Rotation+ = sum(SEM+ x starter IP) / sum(starter IP), over starters with a scored SEM+ (100 = average rotation)
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Team lineup rating: 100 is an average offense. Plate-appearance-weighted HEM+ of the club's hitters. On the Team Lineups board in MLB Stats; higher is better. Coloured on the value ruler at 130 / 120 / 112 / 100 / 88.
entries.methodology: Each hitter's HEM+ is weighted by his plate appearances and divided by those plate appearances, so playing time sets how much a bat counts without entering the rate: a bench bat with 40 trips cannot carry a lineup. Only hitters with a scored HEM+ and positive PA enter; the display rounds to a whole point (unrounded as offense_plus_raw). HEM+ is anchored on the hitter pool, so 100 is the average lineup. It rides HEM+'s wider display spread (HEM+ is stretched to the wRC+ deviation width by a fixed monotone gain), so read it at roughly 16 points per standard deviation, not the tighter REM+ / SEM+ bands. Heart 3 (top three regulars by HEM+), the count of above-average hitters and team PA are context; the batting orders against right- and left-handed pitching and the bench list are display only. Built by hitter_export.py via hem_plus.score_pool and hem_plus.team_offense.
entries.formula: Offense+ = sum(HEM+ x PA) / sum(PA), over hitters with a scored HEM+ (100 = average lineup)
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: HEM+ against one pitcher hand: a hitter's own line against left- or right-handed pitching, on the season HEM+ scale. The lead number on the Lineup Charts cards in MLB Stats under the vs LHP / vs RHP toggle, with the season HEM+ beside it, dim. Higher is better.
entries.methodology:
Each hand's counting line comes from the StatsAPI split feed (sitCodes vl and vr, every MLB hitter) and runs through the HEM+ shrunk-wOBA recipe. The anchor is the SEASON hitter pool, not a per-hand pool, so the league platoon effect survives: a left-handed hitter's vs-LHP number reads below his season number by what he loses against lefties. A split sample is smaller, so the same reliability constants pull it harder toward the pool.

On the card: a number on fewer than 100 plate appearances against the hand is dimmed with a dotted underline (mostly anchor). A hitter with no line against the hand shows his season HEM+ with a small s. The batting order is still built on season HEM+ and the handedness stagger; the per-hand number does not reorder it. Positions come from 2026 MLB fielding innings.

The Bench block lists active non-pitcher bats outside the nine, sorted by the per-hand number (lines at 100+ PA first). The Out block lists regulars (the club's top nine by season plate appearances) not on the active roster, labelled from MLB's cached 40-man status: IL-10, IL-60, Minors, Bereavement, Off 40-man, or Not active when the cache gives no reason. A day-to-day injury that is not a roster move does not appear.
entries.formula: vs-hand HEM+ = 100 + 2.28 x (100 x shrunk wOBA against the hand / season pool wOBA - 100)
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The PLT chip on a Lineup Charts card: a bench bat with the platoon edge against the toggled pitcher hand, at a position he has played, where the starter he sits behind lacks it, and whose vs-hand HEM+ beats the starter's by 15+ with 100+ plate appearances each against that hand. A read of this season's splits, not a lineup recommendation.
entries.methodology:
All six hold for opposing hand h, starter S and bench bat B: (1) S bats from the same side as h and does not switch-hit; (2) B bats from the other side or switch-hits; (3) B has 30+ 2026 MLB innings at S's primary position (the fielding position with the most innings, or DH when MLB lists the player as DH; DH is open to every non-pitcher); (4) both have a real vs-hand HEM+ against h, never a season fallback; (5) both have 100+ plate appearances against h; (6) B's vs-hand HEM+ minus S's is 15 or more.

The 100-PA floor is where the shrunk split stops being mostly anchor. The 15-point margin sits at the low end of the measured spread of a hitter's two hand numbers: roughly a one-sigma gate, not a significance test. Both numbers are shrunk toward the season anchor, so a marked gap understates the raw one. The thresholds ship in the payload (lineup_cards.constants). Display only: it never changes the batting order, Offense+ or any betting input.
entries.formula: PLT when S lacks the edge vs h, B holds it, B has 30+ innings at S's position (DH open), both have 100+ PA vs h, and vsHEM+(B, h) - vsHEM+(S, h) >= 15
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A fielder's sprint speed as a range read on the 100 + 10z scale (100 = league-average position player, ten points = one standard deviation). A chip on Position Fit rows in the Pitcher Alchemy Lab, shown ONLY for left-field and center-field destinations. Display only; never enters the position-fit model.
entries.methodology:
Sprint speed from the current-season Statcast leaderboard, falling back one season when a player has no current tracking (the chip names the season). Standardized against that season's MLB position-player pool: Rng+ = 100 + 10 x z(ft/s). The chip also shows the player's percentile among incumbents at the destination (400+ innings there over the trailing three seasons).

Why only LF and CF. Against OAA per 1,000 innings at the position played (400+ innings, 2016-2026), sprint speed tracks range in center field at r = +0.428 (95% CI +0.342 to +0.507) and in left field at r = +0.416 (+0.323 to +0.501). Right field clears the headline bar at r = +0.269 (+0.167 to +0.365) but is excluded, because the signal comes from displaced center fielders: right fielders with under 100 career center-field innings read r = +0.075 (-0.111 to +0.256), lower bound under the +0.15 bar. Left field survives the same pure-corner test (+0.359, +0.163 to +0.528, n = 89). Shortstop (-0.020, -0.122 to +0.083) and third base (-0.004, -0.108 to +0.100) show no signal, so no infield chip renders.

Nothing reaches the model: positional_fit's field() has no sprint term, because OAA already contains the legs (the same reason the arm feature was rejected). build_site.py decides which positions qualify and bakes every number; assets/pal.js computes none of it.
entries.formula: Rng+ = 100 + 10 x z(sprint speed, ft/s) against the current-season MLB position-player pool; shipped for LF and CF destinations only
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The average Leverage Index at the moment a reliever enters: how high-pressure his usage is, set mostly by the manager. About 1.0 is average; closers run high, mop-up arms low.
entries.methodology: Computed from the MLB win-probability feed: the Leverage Index of the play where the reliever enters, averaged across his appearances. Deployment, not skill, so REM+ keeps it in a separate column.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Relief-entry-weighted average gmLI over the trailing three seasons, with the pool percentile. Deployment context, not skill. About 1.0 is average; established high-leverage arms run 1.5 and up.
entries.methodology: Each season's gmLI (entry Leverage Index from the MLB win-probability feed) averaged over the trailing three seasons, weighted by relief entries. Year-over-year gmLI rank correlation on qualified relievers is 0.47 pooled over 2018-2025 (ex-2020), with within-season split-half stability of 0.53, so leverage assignment persists. Under 2 seasons or 60 relief entries in the window carries a provisional mark. Never feeds REM+.
entries.formula:
gmLI 3yr = SUM(entries_s x gmLI_s) / SUM entries_s over the trailing three seasons, shown with the pool percentile
provisional under 2 seasons or 60 relief entries in the window
entries.example: Seasons at gmLI 1.85 (62 entries), 1.60 (58) and 1.10 (20 so far) average (1.85x62 + 1.60x58 + 1.10x20) / 140 = 1.64.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The realized, leverage-weighted value a reliever produced this season, 100-anchored (100 = average, higher is more value). The deployment-value companion to REM+: REM+ is run-prevention skill with leverage held out; RIV+ credits the wins a reliever added in the leverage he was given. Coloured on the value ruler at 140 / 120 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology:
A WPA-primary composite standardized over the season's reliever pool and reported as 100 + 10z. The composite is 70 percent Win Probability Added (which weights every out by the leverage of the moment) and 30 percent shutdowns minus meltdowns (a lower-variance count of high-impact outings). Leverage enters only through value produced, never as credit for the role.

A realized-value measure, not a repeatable skill: its year-over-year rank correlation is 0.20 against 0.36 for REM+ (2018-2025, ex-2020; harness v2, data/riv_plus_eval.json generated 2026-08-30), which is why leverage stays out of REM+ and rides here. It is not shown to track free-agent pay any better than REM+: on 232 matched reliever signings the rank correlation with AAV is 0.573 for RIV+ against 0.567 for REM+ (data/riv_market_regate_eval.json, 2026-09-18 re-gate), a gap of 0.005 inside a noise floor of 0.086.
entries.formula:
z = 0.70 x z(WPA) + 0.30 x z(shutdowns - meltdowns), re-standardized on the blend's own pool spread
RIV+ = 100 + 10 x z, over relievers with a leverage feed only
entries.example: A closer at +3.5 WPA with 38 shutdowns and 6 meltdowns lands about two blended standard deviations up: RIV+ near 120. A same-REM+ arm used in mop-up sits in the 90s.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: REM+ over the trailing three seasons, innings-weighted, with the pool percentile. Same run-prevention skill scale (100 = average reliever). A steadier read, not a stronger forecast. Coloured on the value ruler at 140 / 120 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology: Innings-weighted mean of the trailing three seasons' REM+. Single reliever seasons are volatile (within-season split-half REM+ correlation about 0.34 at 100-150 batters faced). The forward test did not separate it from one season: three-year forward Spearman 0.237 against 0.232 for one year, with the 95% interval on the gap running negative. Ships as a steadiness companion.
entries.formula: REM+ 3yr = SUM(IP_s x REM+_s) / SUM IP_s over the trailing three seasons, shown with the pool percentile
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A starting pitcher's run-prevention skill on a 100-anchored scale (100 = the average qualified starter, 110 = 10 percent better). The starter version of REM+: a sample-shrunk, starter-pool-anchored FIP from strikeouts, walks, hit batters and a heavily regressed home-run rate. Durability (innings, games started, average start length) shows beside it, never inside it. Coloured on the value ruler at 140 / 120 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology:
Each rate is regressed toward the starter-pool average by sample size (REM+'s empirical-Bayes recipe), turned into a fielding-independent ERA, and expressed as 100 x pool-average Skill FIP / the pitcher's own. The pool is starters only.

Validated out of sample: forward-chained over 2018-2025 (ex-2020), SEM+ predicts a starter's next-year runs-allowed rate at a Spearman correlation of 0.42, beating ERA (0.28; gap confidence floor above zero) and edging its raw-FIP parent (0.38) (data/sem_plus_eval.json, generated 2026-08-30). A ground-ball-adjusted variant did not beat plain FIP out of sample. Quality starts and times-through-order are not in the source feed, so average start length carries the durability read.
entries.formula:
SEM+ = 100 x starter-pool FIP / player's sample-shrunk FIP
component K / BB / HBP rates shrunk to the starter-pool mean by sample size, the HR rate heavily regressed, recombined as a fielding-independent ERA; 100 = the average qualified starter
entries.example: A starter at a 3.40 sample-shrunk FIP against a 4.10 starter pool reads SEM+ 121. The same raw 3.40 over 50 innings is pulled toward the pool first and reads lower.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A hitter's offensive-rate skill on a 100-anchored scale (100 = the average qualified hitter), stretched to the wRC+ convention so the league shows real separation (about 15 points per standard deviation). The hitter version of REM+ / SEM+: a sample-shrunk, hitter-pool-anchored wOBA from unintentional walks, hit-by-pitches, singles, doubles, triples and home runs. Volume, baserunning and the slash line show beside it, never inside it. Coloured on the value ruler at 130 / 120 / 112 / 100 / 88.
entries.methodology:
Each wOBA component rate is regressed toward the hitter-pool average by sample size (REM+'s empirical-Bayes recipe, with a slower pull for extra-base hits, which stabilize late), recombined with one fixed set of FanGraphs-family linear weights (uBB 0.69, HBP 0.72, 1B 0.89, 2B 1.27, 3B 1.62, HR 2.10, the fa_config vintage, applied to every season; FanGraphs publishes season-specific weights), and re-anchored so the pool average scores 100. HEM+ = 100 x shrunk player wOBA / pool wOBA, then stretched: a ratio-to-league index in the wRC+ / OPS+ family, not a z-score.

Validated out of sample: forward-chained over 2012-2024 (ex-2020), HEM+ predicts next-year wOBA at a Spearman correlation of 0.41, beating batting average (0.23; gap confidence floor above zero) and even with its raw-wOBA parent (0.41). Volume, baserunning and defense stay out of the rate. Accountability artifact: data/hem_plus_eval.json. The stretch is a fixed monotone gain (HEM_SPREAD_GAIN 2.28) that preserves rank exactly, so the validation is unchanged.
entries.formula:
HEM+ = 100 + 2.28 x (100 x shrunk wOBA / pool wOBA - 100)
shrunk wOBA: each component rate (uBB, HBP, 1B, 2B, 3B, HR) regressed to the hitter-pool mean by sample size (slower for extra-base hits), recombined with fixed linear weights 0.69 / 0.72 / 0.89 / 1.27 / 1.62 / 2.10
the 2.28 gain (HEM_SPREAD_GAIN) is a fixed monotone stretch to the wRC+ deviation width; rank order is untouched
entries.example: A hitter whose shrunk wOBA is .365 against a .330 pool sits 10.6 percent above it: 100 + 2.28 x 10.6 = 124.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A hitter's HEM+ over the trailing three seasons, plate-appearance-weighted: a steadier talent read than one season, on the HEM+ scale. Coloured on the value ruler at 130 / 120 / 112 / 100 / 88.
entries.methodology: PA-weighted mean of the hitter's HEM+ across the last three seasons (2024-2026), so a partial current season counts by its plate appearances. Established = 2+ seasons and 600+ PA in the window; otherwise provisional. Forward-chained over 2012-2024 (ex-2020), the 3-year read predicts next-year wOBA at a Spearman correlation of 0.45 against 0.43 for one season on the same hitters, with the same-set gap confidence floor above zero. Accountability artifact: data/hem_plus_multiyear_eval.json.
entries.formula:
HEM+ (3yr) = SUM(PA_s x HEM+_s) / SUM PA_s over the trailing three seasons
established = 2+ seasons and 600+ PA in the window, else provisional
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: WAR/PA+ with the rate regressed toward the league rate by plate appearances taken, so a hot 100-PA line does not outrank a strong full season. Same 100-anchored, ten-points-per-standard-deviation scale, rebuilt on the regressed pool. Sort the board on this; read what a hitter banked on plain WAR/PA+. Coloured on the value ruler at 120 / 113 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology:

entries.definition: Total value a hitter banked per plate appearance, on a 100-anchored scale where ten points is one standard deviation of the hitter pool. entries.methodology:

Two volume floors: everyone at or above the pool floor sets the pool mean and spread; only players at 100 plate appearances or more get a published value. Forward-checked out of sample, and it lost. Over 2012-2025 (ex-2020) and 3845 year-to-year pairs, WAR/PA+ predicts next season's WAR rate at a Spearman correlation of 0.3711, while plain season WAR predicts the same thing at 0.4058 (measured on eWAR, which on the batting side reads the same as bWAR). entries.definition: A hitter's WAR/PA+ over the trailing three seasons, weighted by plate appearances. Steadier than one season, because a WAR rate carries fielding and baserunning on top of the bat. entries.methodology:

The payload carries the generation date.

entries.definition: A hitter's DESERVED offensive rate on the HEM+ scale: HEM+ computed from Savant expected wOBA (xwOBA) instead of results, so it reads contact quality rather than where the balls fell. Luck = Savant xwOBA minus wOBA, in wOBA points. Coloured on the value ruler at 130 / 120 / 112 / 100 / 88.
entries.methodology: xHEM+ = 100 x the hitter's Savant xwOBA / the PA-weighted pool average, on the HEM+ scale. xwOBA is built from each batted ball's launch conditions (exit velocity and angle), which strips BABIP and sequencing luck. Forward-chained over eight season-pairs 2016-2025 (ex-2020, 1871 pairs), xwOBA predicts next-year wOBA at a Spearman correlation of 0.45 against 0.41 for actual wOBA, gap confidence floor above zero. A companion for tracked hitters (Statcast is MLB-only; 100+ tracked PA), not the population-complete HEM+. Luck > 0: under-performing his contact; < 0: over-performing. Luck is read on the unshrunk pair, not as xHEM+ minus HEM+: HEM+ is shrunk toward the pool and xHEM+ is not, so that difference partly measured the shrink and disagreed in sign with xwOBA minus wOBA for 126 of 460 hitters on 2026-09-24. Accountability artifact: data/xhem_plus_eval.json.
entries.formula:
xHEM+ = 100 + 2.28 x (100 x player xwOBA / PA-weighted tracked-pool xwOBA - 100) (tracked hitters, 100+ Savant PA)
Luck = Savant xwOBA - Savant wOBA, in wOBA points
entries.example: A .352 xwOBA against a .320 tracked pool reads xHEM+ 123. With an actual wOBA of .322, Luck is +.030: his contact deserved more.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. Expected-stat inputs from Baseball Savant (Statcast).

entries.definition: The site's single-number read on a hitter's NEXT-year offense: a 70/30 blend of Savant xwOBA and the HEM+ skill core, on the HEM+ scale (100 = the average tracked hitter). xwOBA carries contact quality; the HEM+ leg adds the shrunk plate-discipline signal contact quality misses. Coloured on the value ruler at 130 / 120 / 112 / 100 / 88.
entries.methodology: Within the season, the hitter's xwOBA and his unrounded HEM+ core are standardized over the tracked pool (100+ Savant PA), combined 70/30, and mapped back onto the HEM+ display scale by the pool's HEM+ location and spread, a rank-preserving transform. Forward-chained over eight season-pairs 2016-2025 (ex-2020, 1871 pairs), the blend predicts next-year wOBA at a Spearman correlation of 0.466 against 0.454 for xwOBA alone, with the paired bootstrap gap floor above zero under the pre-registered convention (the newer clustered harness reads the same edge as positive but within noise, reported alongside). A multi-year decayed candidate failed its gate, so this single-season blend is the incumbent forward column. Tracked hitters only. Accountability artifact: data/xhem_plus_eval.json (X-H5 block).
entries.formula:
blend z = 0.70 x z(Savant xwOBA) + 0.30 x z(unrounded HEM+ core), each standardized over the tracked pool (100+ Savant PA), then re-standardized on the blend's own spread
xHEM+ Blend = the blend mapped back onto the HEM+ ratio display scale by the pool's HEM+ location and spread (rank-preserving)
entries.example: A hitter +1σ on xwOBA and average on the HEM+ core blends to about +0.8σ after re-standardization: mid-110s on the HEM+ scale.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. Expected-stat inputs from Baseball Savant (Statcast).

entries.definition: A hitter's projected NEXT-season wOBA from the site's FA-engine Marcel (the engine that prices the FA class board and drives MLB Projections). Read it like wOBA: ~.310 league average, .370 a star season, .400+ elite.
entries.methodology: The engine projects each wOBA component (walk rate, strikeout rate, isolated power, BABIP, home runs per PA) as a Marcel weighted average of the trailing three seasons (5/3/2 recency, exposure-weighted), regresses each to the league mean, blends ISO toward Savant xISO where tracked, and ages every rate along survivorship-corrected curves; the components reassemble into a wOBA with fixed run-value weights. Validated by the T1-10 projection gate (data/phem_marcel_lite_eval.json): over predictor seasons 2021-2024 (918 out-of-sample pairs) projected wOBA predicts next-year wOBA at a Spearman correlation of 0.5189 against 0.4939 for the best trailing-average incumbent, paired-bootstrap floor above zero, confirmed under the clustered harness. A purpose-built multi-year challenger lost the same gate. Shown for tracked hitters with 100+ PA over the trailing three seasons; current boards only (a past season has no next season to project).
entries.formula:
each component (BB%, K%, ISO, BABIP, HR/PA) = Marcel(5/3/2 recency, exposure-weighted), regressed to the league mean, ISO blended toward Savant xISO, aged along survivorship-corrected curves
pWOBA = the projected components reassembled with fixed run-value weights; shown at 100+ PA over the trailing three seasons
entries.example: Trailing component rates worth wOBA .355 / .345 / .330 blend to about .347; the league pull and a year of aging settle pWOBA near .340.
entries.origin: Projection column from the site's FA-engine Marcel. The Marcel weighted-rates framework is Tom Tango's; the engine that produces this number (survivorship-corrected aging curves, Savant xISO blend, league re-anchoring) is an Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: SEM+ over the trailing three seasons, innings-weighted, with the pool percentile. Same scale as SEM+ (100 = average qualified starter). A steadier read, not a stronger forecast. Coloured on the value ruler at 140 / 120 / 107 / 100 / 93.

The forward test did not separate it from one season: three-year forward Spearman 0.414 against 0.392 for one year on the same starters, with the 95% interval on the gap running negative. entries.formula: SEM+ 3yr = SUM(IP_s x SEM+_s) / SUM IP_s over the trailing three seasons, shown with the pool percentile

entries.definition: The total change in a player's team win probability across every play he was in, credited to the BATTER on offense and the PITCHER on defense (opposite signs on the same play). A counting stat of in-the-moment impact, scaled by the leverage of his spots.
entries.methodology: Summed from the MLB win-probability feed: each play's change in win expectancy, credited to the pitcher on the mound; the batter's credit is the negation on the same play. A run prevented in a tie game in the ninth moves win probability far more than the same out in a blowout, so WPA rewards high-leverage usage as much as performance.
entries.formula:
WPA = SUM of each play's change in team win expectancy over the player's plays; credited to the pitcher on defense, and the batter's credit is the negation of the pitcher's on the same play
per-play home-team win-probability delta, sign-flipped to the involved player's team
entries.example: A go-ahead two-run homer in the eighth might move win probability from 35 to 78 percent: +0.43 WPA to the batter, -0.43 to the pitcher. The same swing in a 10-1 blowout moves a point or two.
entries.origin: Industry metric. Win Probability Added, from the win-expectancy framework (Tom Tango and coauthors, The Book); implemented by FanGraphs.

entries.definition: Win Probability Added with the leverage of each play divided out, so it measures performance independent of how important the situations were. The leverage-stripped companion to WPA.
entries.origin: Industry metric. WPA divided by leverage index, a context-neutral wins measure from the win-expectancy framework (Tom Tango).

entries.definition: How important a game situation is, from inning, score, outs and baserunners; 1.0 is average. Below 0.85 is low leverage, 2.0+ high.
entries.origin: Industry metric. Leverage Index, created by Tom Tango (The Book): how much the current game state can swing win probability, 1.0 = average.

entries.definition: Per-appearance reliever outcomes. A Shutdown adds at least 0.06 to the team's win probability in an outing; a Meltdown subtracts at least that much. Shutdowns minus Meltdowns is a cleaner reliever record than saves and holds.
entries.origin: Industry metric. Reliever WPA thresholds proposed by Tom Tango and implemented by FanGraphs.

entries.definition: The bullpen leverage ladder, assigned from entry leverage (gmLI) and usage: Closer finishes games at the highest leverage; High-leverage and Setup pitch the tightest middle innings; Middle relief works average spots; Long and Mop-up cover multi-inning or low-stakes work.
A 0-100 candidate score for how well a current reliever would profile as a starter; higher is a better fit. A screen for candidates, not a probability of success.
entries.methodology: A weighted blend led by arsenal depth (a starter must survive a lineup three times, so a third and fourth pitch matter most), then command (walk rate), fastball reliance, platoon neutrality, contact quality and stuff. Fastball velocity is projected down about 1 mph for the longer role. Weights are literature priors, not fitted. The per-direction backtest does not validate the ranking in this direction: pre-conversion FIT ran against realized WAR change at rho about -0.21 on 25 gated events on the bWAR gate basis, and about +0.024 on the eWAR v2 series this page serves, a change of SIGN on a sample that resolves nothing either way. Read the list as arms with starter traits, not a forecast of who converts.
entries.formula: FIT = weighted blend, literature-prior weights: arsenal depth (largest weight), command (BB%), fastball reliance (penalized), platoon neutrality, contact quality, stuff; fastball velocity projected about -1 mph for the longer role
entries.example: A reliever with four usable pitches, a 6 percent walk rate and modest fastball reliance scores in the 80s.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A 0-100 candidate score for how well a current starter's stuff would play up in one-inning relief; higher is a better fit.
entries.methodology: The traits that hurt a starter help a reliever: a thin, fastball-heavy arsenal that leaks runs the third time through is fine for one inning. The score rewards a dominant putaway pitch, projected relief velocity (about +1 mph in short bursts), stuff quality and times-through-order leakage (the complement of arsenal depth). A display-only projected relief REM+ shows roughly what the arm might post in relief. This direction is validated: in the per-direction backtest, pre-conversion FIT out-ranked every same-event baseline against realized WAR change (rho about +0.29 on 61 gated events on the bWAR gate basis, about +0.271 on the eWAR v2 series this page serves, gap over the best baseline positive at the 95 percent floor).
entries.formula:
FIT = weighted blend: putaway pitch quality, projected relief velocity (about +1 mph in short bursts), stuff quality, times-through-order leakage (the complement of arsenal depth)
companion display: a projected relief REM+, display-only
entries.example: A two-pitch starter with a wipeout slider and a third-time-through collapse scores in the 80s, with a projected relief REM+ near 115 against a starting SEM+ in the 90s.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The model behind the Alchemy Lab: two candidate scores (RP->SP FIT and SP->RP FIT) plus a history of past role conversions that doubles as the backtest. SP->RP is validated; RP->SP is a structural screen.
entries.methodology:
Conversions are detected from season starting shares across 2018-2026 (a role flip between qualified seasons). The outcome is the change in realized WAR (eWAR basis from the 2026-09 epoch: Baseball-Reference run frame with pitching re-priced on FIP) from the pre-role to the post-role season, scored within each direction and never pooled; a held-the-role label (one full closed season in the new role) is a sensitivity check.

Two bases, and they disagree on reliever-to-starter. The registered gate ran on bWAR (data/pal_eval.json, 2026-07-15): SP to RP +0.2916 on 61 gated events (passes), RP to SP -0.2062 on 25 (fails). Every FIT score, history delta and live rho this module serves is on eWAR v2, where the same harness returns SP to RP +0.271 and RP to SP +0.024. The reliever-to-starter number changes sign between the gate basis and the served basis on a 25-event sample that resolves nothing; data/pal.json records backtest.gate.same_basis_as_live = false. The RP to SP list is a structural screen on either basis. The sample is small and selection-biased (only pitchers teams chose to convert), so neither score is a success probability, and the model ships provisional with a downgraded registry verdict.
entries.formula:
two candidate scores: RP->SP FIT and SP->RP FIT, 0-100 weighted blends with literature-prior weights (not fitted)
backtest, per direction and never pooled: rho(pre-conversion FIT, post-role minus pre-role WAR change) over detected role flips 2018-2026; SP->RP passes its gate, RP->SP fails it and ships as a structural screen
entries.example: A fastball-heavy starter with third-time-through leakage scores high on SP->RP FIT and low on arsenal depth; the history tab shows the real conversions the harness scored.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: How many distinct pitches a pitcher throws at least ten percent of the time. The main trait for surviving a lineup more than once, and the core of RP->SP FIT.
A pitcher's decline each time he faces the same lineup in a game. A deep, varied arsenal blunts it; a thin fastball-heavy mix collapses by the third time through. A reliever faces the order once.
entries.origin: Industry concept. The times-through-order penalty, quantified by Mitchel Lichtman and coauthors (The Book).

entries.definition: The change in fastball velocity when a pitcher changes roles: a starter stretching out loses about 1 mph; a pitcher moving to one-inning relief gains about that much. Studies put the central number near 1 mph, larger for pure power arms, so the Lab projects it modestly rather than the three or four of folklore.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A pitcher's best swing-and-miss pitch by whiff rate. A dominant one lets a starter's stuff play up in one-inning relief, so it drives SP->RP FIT.
The gap in OPS allowed to left- versus right-handed hitters. A flat split lets a pitcher face a full lineup, which supports starting; a large split is a conversion blocker.
The non-pitcher positions a player has real game experience at, from MLB and MiLB fielding logs rather than a projected multi-position tag.
entries.methodology: Built from StatsAPI game fielding, not a reported position string. A position counts at 10+ games or 5+ starts there. DH is excluded (not a fielding position). A listed shortstop with real innings at second and third shows all three.
entries.formula: Position qualifies at >= 10 G or >= 5 GS at that spot; DH excluded
entries.example: A shortstop with 40 G at SS, 12 G at 2B, and 6 GS at 3B shows Versa: SS / 2B / 3B.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A draft prospect's board rank as an index (100 = middle of the class, higher = more valued), nudged a few points by a college-performance signal.
entries.methodology: Maps consensus draft rank to roughly 70-130 (best of class near 130, back of the board near 70), on the raw fractional ranks so bunched prospects stay distinct. A z-scored college-performance term moves it up to about six points, then it is clamped. A heuristic stock indicator, not a validated projection. Draft Overperformance, by contrast, compares realized FV to slot after the fact.
entries.formula: DS+ = rank-to-index (about 70-130) + college-performance nudge (up to about +-6), clamped
entries.example: A prospect ranked 8th in a class of 250 with a strong statistical spring might carry a DS+ near 126.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: How much better a pitcher holds opposite-handed hitters than same-handed ones, the reverse of the normal platoon pattern. A reverse split supports a full-lineup starter role, because the batters who would platoon against him lose their edge.
entries.methodology: For a right-hander: OPS allowed to righties minus OPS allowed to lefties (mirrored for a lefty). Above zero is a reverse split. The radar flags > 0.03 and extreme at ≥ 0.15, counting only pitchers with 100+ batters faced on the lighter side.
entries.formula: reverse index = own-hand OPS-against minus opposite-hand OPS-against (RHP: vsR minus vsL); reverse if > 0.03; requires >= 100 TBF
entries.example: A righty allowing .720 to righties and .560 to lefties has a reverse index of +0.16.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A 0-100 read on whether a pitching prospect's tools fit a starting or relief role, from scout grades only (arsenal depth and command). A shape screen, not a stuff projection: it flags prospects whose listed role conflicts with their grades.
entries.methodology: Rewards arsenal depth (distinct pitches graded 55+, since a starter needs a third weapon) and command, about 60/40. A high score on a reliever-labeled prospect, or a low score on a starter-labeled one, is flagged as a role mismatch on the PAL Prospect Watch. No minor-league stats; descriptive, not a validated outcome model.
entries.formula: Starter Shape = 0.60 x arsenal-depth score (pitches graded >= 55) + 0.40 x command score, on scout grades only
entries.example: FB 60 / SL 55 / CB 45 / CH 40 with 40 command: thin depth, light command, low Starter Shape; a starter-labeled version is flagged as profiling in relief.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Expected wOBA: what a hitter's contact and plate results are worth from how the ball was struck, without defense and luck.
entries.methodology: Estimates wOBA from contact quality (exit velocity and launch angle) plus strikeouts and walks, at the run value of each outcome. xwOBAcon is the contact-only version. The value on player cards is our reconstruction from the tracking inputs available, not the official Savant figure.
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant). Displayed here as an estimate.

aliases: Batting Average on Balls In Play
entries.definition: Batting average on balls in play: how often balls put in play become hits. Read as a hot or unlucky line indicator.
entries.methodology: BABIP = (H - HR) / (AB - K - HR + SF). League average is near .300. Large gaps from a hitter's own norm usually regress; speed and hard contact sustain higher marks for some hitters.
entries.origin: Standard sabermetric rate; the DIPS insight that pitchers have limited control over BABIP is due to Voros McCracken.

entries.definition: Vertical approach angle: the steepness of a pitch's descent as it crosses the plate; VAAoe is that angle over expectation given the pitch's release and velocity.
entries.methodology: The angle of the ball's path at the plate. Flatter four-seam approach angles at the top of the zone tend to get more swing-and-miss, so VAA and VAAoe (over expectation, adjusting for release height and velocity) are fastball shape context, not a grade.
entries.origin: Derived here from Statcast pitch tracking (Baseball Savant); the approach-angle family was popularized across the public pitching-analysis community.

entries.definition: Whether a farm's prospects arrive while the big-league core is still under team control. Negative = the farm lands inside the window; positive = help arrives after the core has left for free agency.
entries.methodology: System Duration (etaMean) is the surplus-weighted average arrival season of a farm: each prospect's projected ETA weighted by his expected surplus dollars. The core center (coreCenter) is the WAR-weighted midpoint of the org's controlled-core production over 2027-2031. Window Alignment = etaMean − coreCenter. The arrival curve (etaByYear) shows the share of farm surplus landing each season.
entries.formula:
Window Alignment = etaMean - coreCenter
etaMean = SUM(surplus_i x ETA_i) / SUM surplus_i over the farm's prospects; coreCenter = WAR-weighted midpoint of the org's controlled-core production over 2027-2031
entries.example: A farm arriving (surplus-weighted) in 2028.4 under a core centered on 2029.1 reads -0.7: inside the window. +1.5 means the help arrives after the core has left.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Surplus weighed against its downside. Only the chance of falling short counts as risk; upside does not. Higher Sortino = more expected surplus per unit of downside.
entries.methodology: From the eFV surplus distribution the trade board carries (a p10-p90 fan plus the mean). Downside deviation is the semi-deviation below the mean. Sortino = (mean − p10) / that downside deviation, so a high-floor profile outscores a boom-or-bust one at the same mean. The tooltip adds a risk-adjusted surplus (mean minus half the downside deviation; a display haircut that does not re-rank the board) and the bust probability. Descriptive: it changes no shown surplus.
entries.formula:
DD = sqrt(SUM w_i x min(q_i - mean, 0)^2) over the p10/p25/p50/p75/p90 surplus fan, w = (0.15, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.10)
Sortino = (mean - p10) / max(DD, 0.1), clamped 0-99
tooltip risk-adjusted surplus = mean - 0.5 x DD (local display haircut, never re-ranks)
entries.example: Two prospects at $30M mean: a high-floor profile (p10 $20M, downside deviation $4M) reads Sortino 2.5; a boom-or-bust fan (p10 $5M, downside deviation $14M) reads about 1.8.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A market-structure overlay on a prospect's consensus FV history: candlesticks plus trader-style indicators (momentum, an RSI on grade changes, volatility). Descriptive, not predictive.
entries.methodology: One candle per consensus snapshot: open = prior grade, close = current consensus FV, wick = the range of source grades that period. Momentum = net grade change over the last three intervals. RSI = balance of upgrades to downgrades over recent grade changes only (flat re-confirmations dropped, so a static grade never pins it); above 70 overbought, below 30 oversold. Volatility = standard deviation across sources on the latest grade. Candles need 4+ snapshots and RSI 6+ grade changes, otherwise hidden.
entries.formula:
candle: open = prior consensus FV, close = current consensus FV, wick = that period's source-grade range
momentum = net grade change over the last 3 intervals; RSI = balance of upgrades vs downgrades over recent GRADE CHANGES only (70 overbought / 30 oversold); volatility = sd across sources on the latest grade
gates: 4+ snapshots for candles, 6+ grade changes for RSI
entries.example: Consensus 45 -> 50 -> 55 over three snapshots prints green candles, momentum +10 and an RSI near 70.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. Candlestick and RSI conventions are borrowed from financial technical analysis.

entries.definition: A live draft-night board: each pick as it happens, priced against our board and the historical value of the slot, so a reach or a steal shows in surplus dollars.
entries.methodology: During the draft a poller reads the MLB Stats API every minute and writes a read-only feed. Each pick joins our board by name and carries consensus FV, the reach-or-steal gap (spots earlier or later than our board rank; a faller past his rank is a steal for the drafting team), the slot's expected first-six-year WAR from the realized pick-value curve, the slot surplus in dollars, and the signing bonus against slot value. A live view over published models; empty before the draft.
entries.formula:
per pick: reach / steal gap = our board rank - pick number (positive = steal for the drafting team); expected first-6yr WAR = the realized pick-value curve at the slot; slot surplus $ = that WAR through the surplus machinery; signing bonus shown against slot value
feed: MLB Stats API polled every minute on draft night, rendered read-only
entries.example: Our No. 14 prospect going 29th overall reads a 15-spot steal, with the slot's expected first-six-year WAR and surplus beside his consensus FV.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. Pick data from the MLB Stats API.

entries.definition: Option sensitivities on a prospect's value: Delta = dollars from a one-grade upgrade; Vega = the dollar swing implied by scouting disagreement; Theta = surplus lost per year of arrival delay.
entries.methodology: All three read off the surplus board's value framework. Delta: change in expected surplus when the grade moves up one full grade (5 FV points), on the FV-to-surplus curve at the prospect's grade, so a jump on the steep part is worth more. Vega: the local slope of that curve times the spread of source grades. Theta: the framework's annual discount applied to expected surplus. Implied volatility is the grade spread itself. Descriptive: no dollar figure changes.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. The Greeks framing is borrowed from options pricing.

entries.definition: The probability a prospect becomes a star: two or more seasons of 4+ WAR during his team-control years. Hitters run higher than pitchers, because a bullpen outcome rarely clears 4 WAR.
entries.methodology: The displayed figure is the FanGraphs 2026 published tier value for the player's FV and role, from the published valuation set. It matches the published table at the published knots (FV 37.5 through 70); between knots it is interpolated, below the lowest knot every grade takes the '35+' value, and above FV 70 the FV 70 value. The in-house mixture also computes a per-player version from the outcome-bucket distribution (per-season WAR profile per bucket, chance of 2+ control seasons at 4+ WAR, weighted by bucket odds, starter and reliever paths blended for pitchers). That version runs below the published tiers under the current bust-heavy anchors, so it is a diagnostic being calibrated toward them, not a replacement.
entries.formula:
star = 2+ seasons of 4+ WAR during the team-control years
displayed value = the FanGraphs 2026 published tier value at the player's FV and role, linearly interpolated between knots and clamped at FV 37.5 and 70
diagnostic model version = SUM_bucket P(bucket | FV) x P(2+ control seasons >= 4 WAR | bucket WAR profile), starter and reliever paths blended for pitchers
entries.example: A FV 60 hitter shows the published FV 60 hitter tier; a FV 60 pitcher shows a lower one. A FV 52 hitter shows the value interpolated between the 50 and 55 knots.
entries.origin: Published star-odds tiers from FanGraphs 2026; the per-player mixture model is Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The share of a prospect's grade value that comes from the chance of UPGRADING before he graduates, rather than from the likeliest outcome at today's grade. A low FV is worth more than its modal result because it can still improve.
entries.methodology: A role-split absorbing Markov chain over FV tiers 35-70 plus graduated and out, with an annual step estimated from dated grade history (FanGraphs and MLB Pipeline pooled to one grade per player per year, Laplace-smoothed). Graduation is a real MLB debut; out is a washed-out player; a still-active player's last observed year is censored. total = expected payoff under the full chain; intrinsic = payoff with the grade frozen; option = total − intrinsic; PLUS% = option / total. Payoff is the clemens_2026 table value of the grade a player graduates from. Low tiers are option-rich (a 45 FV hitter runs about 60 percent); high grades run low or negative, because mobility at the top is mostly downgrade risk and the top-tier samples are thin. Provisional and descriptive: negatives are shown, and no surplus changes.
entries.formula:
total(g0) = SUM_g N[g0, g] x P(graduate from g) x payoff(g), over the absorbing Markov chain on FV tiers 35-70 (annual step fit on dated grade history)
intrinsic(g0) = P(graduate | grade frozen at g0) x payoff(g0); payoff = clemens_2026 table value at the graduating grade
PLUS% = (total - intrinsic) / total
entries.example: A FV 45 hitter draws most of his expected dollars from paths that upgrade to 50 or 55 before debuting: PLUS% near 60 percent. A FV 65 reads near zero or negative.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Expected slugging: the slugging a hitter's contact deserved from how the ball was struck, without defense and park luck.
entries.methodology: Baseball Savant estimates SLG from exit velocity and launch angle at each outcome's run value. Shown on MLB player cards as a percentile against the season's qualified-hitter pool.
entries.origin: Baseball Savant (MLB Statcast), Tom Tango and the Statcast team; our card value is a percentile reconstruction from the tracking inputs available.

entries.definition: Expected isolated power: deserved extra-base power, computed as xSLG minus xBA, so it isolates the power a hitter's contact earned from the singles.
entries.methodology: xISO = xSLG - xBA, both from Savant's contact-quality model (exit velocity + launch angle): the deserved-power analog of ISO (SLG - AVG). Shown on MLB player cards as a percentile against the qualified-hitter pool, beside the Luck tile (actual wOBA minus xwOBA).
entries.origin: Baseball Savant (MLB Statcast), Tom Tango and the Statcast team; our card value is a percentile reconstruction from the tracking inputs available.

entries.definition: A reliever's DESERVED run prevention on the REM+ scale: REM+'s 100-anchored convention applied to Savant expected wOBA allowed instead of FIP, so it reads the contact a reliever gives up rather than where the balls fell. Luck = actual minus expected wOBA allowed. A companion to REM+. Coloured on the value ruler at 140 / 120 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology: xREM+ = 100 x reliever-pool expected wOBA allowed / the reliever's own (inverted: lower allowed scores higher), anchored on the reliever board so 100 is the average reliever. Expected wOBA from each batted ball's launch conditions strips balls-in-play and sequencing luck. Statcast expected wOBA allowed was tested against FIP for the pitcher run-prevention models and did not forward-predict better, so REM+ stays FIP-based; xREM+ is a deserved read plus a luck residual, not a sharper predictor. Tracked relievers with 80+ batters faced only. Luck > 0: allowed more than his contact deserved; < 0: over-performed.
entries.formula:
xREM+ = 100 x reliever-pool xwOBA allowed / player's xwOBA allowed (INVERTED: lower allowed scores higher), tracked relievers with 80+ BF
Luck = actual wOBA allowed - expected wOBA allowed
entries.example: A .270 xwOBA allowed against a .310 pool reads xREM+ 115. An actual .300 beside it is +.030 of bad luck.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. Expected-stat inputs from Baseball Savant (Statcast).

entries.definition: A starter's DESERVED run prevention on the SEM+ scale: SEM+'s 100-anchored convention applied to Savant expected wOBA allowed instead of FIP. Luck = actual minus expected wOBA allowed. A companion to SEM+. Coloured on the value ruler at 140 / 120 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology: xSEM+ = 100 x starter-pool expected wOBA allowed / the starter's own (inverted), anchored on the starter board so 100 is the average starter. Statcast expected wOBA allowed was tested against FIP for the pitcher run-prevention models and did not forward-predict better, so SEM+ stays FIP-based; xSEM+ is a deserved read plus a luck residual. Tracked starters with 150+ batters faced only. Luck > 0: allowed more than his contact deserved; < 0: over-performed.
entries.formula:
xSEM+ = 100 x starter-pool xwOBA allowed / player's xwOBA allowed (INVERTED: lower allowed scores higher), tracked starters with 150+ BF
Luck = actual wOBA allowed - expected wOBA allowed
entries.example: A .295 xwOBA allowed against a .320 starter pool reads xSEM+ 108. An actual .270 beside it is -.025: over-performing his contact.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. Expected-stat inputs from Baseball Savant (Statcast).

entries.definition: An org's international-amateur spending efficiency: bonus dollars per projected FV point over the graded (tracked) signees in a class. Lower is more efficient. A projected-FV proxy, not realized value; recent classes have no outcomes yet.
entries.methodology: Per org, over graded signees only: covered bonus dollars / their current projected FV points (raw FV, as in fv_per_m_pool and surplus_per_fv_pt). The Coverage column shows the graded subset's share of total class spending. Orgs with fewer than 3 graded signees in view are listed, not ranked. Provisional; no surplus changes.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. IFA signing bonuses from Spotrac.

entries.definition: Roster-decision exposure for the trade board: Rule 5 must-protect, on the 40-man, out of options. Flags players an org may have to move or protect. Deterministic, not a predictive model.
entries.methodology: From roster status: on_40_man, option years used and left (3 to start), Rule 5 exposure (off the 40-man and past the exposure-year threshold since signing: protect by November or risk losing him for about $100K), and service phase. The 0-100 score is additive: +55 Rule 5 must-protect or in the November window, +30 on the 40-man and out of options, +12 one option left, +10 occupying a scarce 40-man slot. The per-org summary counts only that org's rostered and MLB board players, not a full 40-man census. No outcome to backtest, so no predictive gate.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. Roster status from the MLB Stats API.

entries.definition: Average Leverage Index of the situations a player was in: how high-stakes his plate appearances (batters) or entries (relievers) were. 1.0 is neutral.
